items.desc: StellDirVor is an independent consulting, trade and technology company specializing in immersive technologies for healthcare. We support organizations in implementing digital innovations — Virtual, Augmented and Mixed Reality as well as AI — particularly for learning, training and real-time assistance in clinical and care environments. By combining technology and healthcare, we help optimize processes, improve knowledge transfer and enhance quality of care. Supported by a Germany (ZIM) and Taiwanese (GIPIP) partnership grant, we are currently developing ARAIAS — an AR- and AI-based hands-free training and assistance system for chronic wound care. Using AR smart glasses, the system enables 3D capture, AI-supported analysis, and standardized remote expertise and documentation directly at the point of care. As our ML Engineer (Computer Vision & ML Ops), you will build the AI capabilities at the core of ARAIAS: evaluating and fine-tuning computer vision models on smart glasses data, running the ML operations behind them, and applying generative AI to create synthetic medical images for education. We're at an early stage — moving from concept to working prototype — so the near-term focus is on validating models and building toward a proof of concept we can test in real education and clinical settings. As part of a small team, you will own the full data lifecycle end to end — from sourcing, consent and annotation to preparation — alongside model development and deployment. We welcome candidates at different experience levels. What matters most is a solid ML foundation and genuine awareness of the medical imaging domain. items.desc: About Us INNOPLUS TECHNOLOGIES LTD is a UK-based pet technology company. We build smart products that help pet owners better understand and care for their pets’ health, well-being and daily routines. Our two flagship products — the Pet Smart Collar and the Pet Health Monitor — are now in the final pre-mass-production phase. UK and China are our primary strategic market, supported by Europe and the US. We are a small, focused team. Everyone here owns real work, moves quickly, and helps shape the company as it grows. This role offers the opportunity to build our algorithm foundation from the ground up. The Role We are looking for an Algorithm Software Engineer to take ownership of algorithm development, tuning, deployment and compliance for our smart pet collar and health detector. You will work closely with the CEO and cross-functional teams to deliver production-grade algorithms in computer vision, audio, IMU and multi-modal fusion, ensuring they are accurate, efficient, compliant and ready for mass production. algorithm version control (e.g., Git, model versioning) and maintain clear version history for models, training configurations and evaluation results. l Organize and maintain algorithm documentation, including design documents, training and evaluation reports, deployment guides and model cards. Essential Requirements l Strong proficiency in Python and C/C++ for algorithm development and embedded deployment. l Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, MMDetection, MMPose, MMPretrain or equivalent. l Proven experience in at least two of the following: computer vision, audio algorithms, IMU algorithms. l Experience in multi-modal fusion — combining vision, audio, IMU or other sensor data to improve recognition or decision accuracy. l Experience deploying AI models to edge devices (ONNX, RKNN, TensorFlow Lite, CMSIS-NN, or similar). l Solid understanding of open-source licences and commercial compliance. l Experience with data privacy, GDPR and compliance-aware algorithm development. l Experience with version control (Git) and maintaining well-documented development records. l Ability to work cross-functionally with hardware, firmware, cloud and App teams. l Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Desirable Skills l Experience with NPU-enabled SoCs and heterogeneous Linux + RTOS architectures. l Hands-on experience with sensor fusion frameworks (e.g., Kalman filters, particle filters, Bayesian fusion, attention-based fusion, or transformer-based multi-modal architectures). l Experience fusing vision with radar, UWB or other vital-sign sensing for health or behaviour monitoring. l Cloud integration (MQTT, REST APIs) and end-to-end data flow debugging. l Experience with pet tech, wearables, or consumer IoT products. l Experience supporting patent applications and IP protection. l Mandarin Chinese language skills (to communicate with Asian partners). items.desc: Research Scientist – Robotics & Physical AI 📍 Zurich, Switzerland 🏢 Hybrid | Full-time ✈️ Relocation support available I’m looking for a Research Scientist to join a robotics company developing foundation models using data from robots already operating in commercial environments. This is an opportunity to take research through to deployment, using real robot behaviour and failures to improve how models learn, adapt and perform. There’s scope to focus on either pretraining or post-training , depending on your strengths. What you’ll work on: Develop transformer and diffusion architectures that learn from visual observations, robot actions and state data. Shape datasets, training objectives and experiments to understand what improves generalisation. Work alongside ML infrastructure engineers to scale training efficiently. Adapt policies through imitation learning, reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and distillation. Test models on physical robots, investigate failures and improve reliability in unfamiliar situations. Who I’m looking for: A strong research background combining machine learning with practical robotics. Experience building or adapting large deep learning models, particularly VLMs, VLAs or learned robot policies. Strong PyTorch or JAX skills and the engineering ability to troubleshoot complex systems. An understanding of perception, control and state estimation, alongside confidence working with hardware. An experimental mindset: someone who enjoys testing ideas, learning from results and getting models to work outside the lab. Experience deploying learned policies on real robots would be particularly valuable. You’ll join a focused team where your research can directly influence the performance of a deployed robot fleet, with flexible working hours and an English-speaking environment. Interested? Send me a message to find out more. #Robotics #PhysicalAI #MachineLearning #ResearchScientist #Zurich

 About the job 
 As a member of our AI research team, you will drive innovation in model compression and efficient deployment for advanced multimodal AI systems, including large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). Your work will focus on reducing model footprint and computational cost while preserving accuracy, enabling high-performance AI to run efficiently across resource-constrained edge devices. You will apply and advance compression techniques such as quantization, knowledge distillation, and pruning to streamline complex multimodal architectures that integrate text, images, and audio. 
 We expect you to have deep expertise in model compression methods and a strong background in multimodal model architectures. You will adopt a hands-on, research-driven approach to develop, test, and implement novel compression strategies that balance model size, latency, throughput, and accuracy. Your responsibilities include building robust compression pipelines, establishing performance and fidelity metrics, and addressing bottlenecks in production inference. The ultimate goal is to deliver scalable, low-memory, low-latency AI systems on edge devices (i.e., smartphones) that maintain high fidelity and tangible real-world value. 
 Responsibilities 
 Break down the key responsibilities in bullet points. It’s helpful to make them actionable and measurable. This could also be grouped into categories for more complex roles. 
 Apply low-bit quantization to reduce model size and inference latency for generative AI models (LLMs, VLMs, multimodal) while maintaining accuracy and output quality. 
 Leverage knowledge distillation to transfer capabilities from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling efficient multimodal reasoning across text, image, and audio inputs. 
 Implement pruning techniques to remove redundant parameters and attention heads, reducing computational overhead without sacrificing task performance. 
 Analyze trade-offs between model efficiency (size, latency, memory) and accuracy across quantization, distillation, and pruning methods; propose improvements based on empirical findings. 
 Research and apply mixed-precision quantization and other advanced compression strategies (e.g., adaptive pruning schedules, distillation with intermediate feature matching) to optimize the accuracy–performance balance. 
 Stay current with the latest research in model compression, including emerging techniques for multimodal and generative architectures.

items.desc: Your Mission & Challenges Own the outcome on the robot: Drive the development of cognitive robotics applications through Physical AI and the NeuraGym platform — you own the outcome on the customer's robot, not just the model in the repo. Execute the full pipeline: Take foundation models to production-ready robotic intelligence by executing the complete NeuraGym pipeline — teleoperation, data annotation, training, simulation, deployment, and validation — tailored to real-world robotics applications. Define the data strategy that makes a fine-tune work and own the full post-training loop including hyperparameter iteration, data mixture, LoRA, and honest evaluation. Deploy to real-time control: Take policies from checkpoint to real-time closed-loop control — distillation, quantization, action chunking, latency budgets, and on-device/edge inference under the customer's cycle time and reliability requirements. Master the full robotics stack: Work across NEURA OS and the control layer — real-time control, kinematics, motion planning, force/impedance control, and the safety architecture — and integrate learned policies cleanly with the low-level controller instead of treating it as a black box. Hands-on system integration: Work directly on MAiRA, MiPA, LARA, and humanoid platforms alongside multidisciplinary engineering teams — end-effectors and tool changers, sensor selection and mounting, calibration, electrical and fieldbus interfaces, and the mechanical reality of the cell. Enable and support customers: Guide and onboard users to NeuraGym by reviewing training pipelines and scripts, identifying data quality issues, troubleshooting model behavior, and providing hands-on support to resolve persistent blockers. Cross-functional collaboration: Serve as a key interface between Cloud and AI teams, ensuring smooth collaboration, technical alignment, and efficient problem-solving across domains. Build evaluation rigor: Create the eval harnesses, success-rate benchmarks, and regression tests that decide whether a policy is ready for handover — and make failure modes visible before the customer finds them. Research to production: Prototype techniques from recent papers together with the research team and bring the ones that survive contact with reality into production deployments. Close the feedback loop: Translate field experience and customer insights into actionable feedback for both the NeuraGym product roadmap and the NEURA core AI roadmap. What We Can Look Forward To Your education: Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. ML in robotics depth: 5+ years of hands-on machine-learning experience in robotics — strong in at least one of vision-based manipulation, reinforcement/imitation learning, or multimodal models, and keen to learn the rest. Fine-tuning expertise: Demonstrable experience fine-tuning large pretrained models for robotics or another domain: PEFT/LoRA and full fine-tunes, dataset curation, distillation, and evaluation. Familiarity with the open VLA and policy-learning ecosystem (e.g., π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, LeRobot, diffusion policies) is a strong plus. Programming skills: Solid Python skills (C++ is a plus); practical experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow. Cloud and simulation: AWS, Azure, or GCP experience and familiarity with robotic simulation tools (IsaacSim, MuJoCo, etc.) are pluses. Robotics software stack: Working command of a robotics software stack beyond the model layer — robot operating systems and middleware (NEURA OS, ROS/ROS2 or comparable), real-time control, kinematics and motion planning, force/impedance control, and how a learned policy wires into a low-level controller and its safety layer. Hardware literacy: Solid understanding of robot hardware — drives and joint modules, torque sensing and encoders, end-effectors, sensor integration, calibration, electrical and fieldbus interfaces (e.g., EtherCAT), and functional safety concepts — enough to distinguish a model problem from a machine problem on site. Execution mindset: Proven problem-solving abilities, ability to handle multiple projects in parallel, and a strong bias toward execution and personal commitment. You take deployments personally, work through setbacks, and measure yourself by what runs at the customer. Communication: Clear communicator who translates between researchers, engineers, and end-users. You have solid command of English and German (B2–C1 level). Travel readiness: Willingness to travel frequently to customer sites and NeuraGyms (approximately 40–60%).

About The Role As a Member of Technical Staff, you’ll own infrastructure across the intersection of ML systems, data, compute and research engineering. The challenge isn’t to build an enormous internal platform for its own sake. It’s to understand what researchers need, identify the bottlenecks slowing them down, and build the smallest, strongest abstractions that make experimentation faster and more reliable. You could be working on GPU orchestration one week, research data infrastructure the next, and improving model serving, experiment reproducibility or distributed training workflows after that. You’ll have significant freedom to make build-vs-buy decisions, introduce new infrastructure where it creates genuine leverage, and deliberately avoid unnecessary complexity where it doesn’t. Examples Of The Problems You Might Tackle Building the ML platform researchers use to train, evaluate, deploy and iterate on scientific models. Designing infrastructure for GPU-intensive training and inference workloads, including scheduling, resource utilisation and workload isolation. Improving distributed model serving using technologies such as vLLM, TensorRT, Triton, Ray or equivalent systems. Building reliable data pipelines and storage systems connecting simulation, modelling, experimental data and downstream research workflows. Creating reproducible experimentation environments so researchers can move quickly without repeatedly solving infrastructure problems. Designing systems for experiment tracking, model versioning, evaluation, observability and lineage. Improving inference latency, throughput, GPU utilisation and cost efficiency. Building internal APIs, tooling and abstractions that make complex infrastructure accessible to researchers without constraining how they work. Supporting workloads that may move between local compute, cloud infrastructure and dedicated GPU environments. Designing systems capable of evolving as the organisation moves from individual research experiments towards increasingly automated scientific workflows. What You’ll Do Build the research platform: Design the infrastructure connecting models, compute, data and scientific workflows, allowing researchers to move from an idea to a reproducible experiment quickly. Own AI infrastructure: Build and operate GPU infrastructure for model training and inference, thinking carefully about scheduling, utilisation, latency, throughput, reliability and cost. Build the data layer: Develop scalable pipelines and systems for ingesting, processing, storing and serving scientific, simulation and experimental data. Productionise research: Help researchers move promising ideas beyond notebooks into robust systems without introducing unnecessary process or infrastructure overhead. Improve model serving: Profile and optimise inference workloads, choosing the right serving architecture and hardware configuration for different models and research requirements. Design for researchers: Work directly with Research Scientists and Engineers to understand how they work and build tools that increase their velocity rather than forcing them into rigid platform abstractions. Make pragmatic architecture decisions: Start from requirements, scale and constraints before choosing technologies. Decide what should be built internally, what should be borrowed and what simply doesn’t need to exist yet. Shape the technical foundation: As an early infrastructure hire, you’ll have significant influence over architecture, engineering standards and how the research platform develops as the company scales. items.desc: What we do No matter if you’re the biggest sports fanatic, have a ‘minor’ shoe addiction or you own just one pair of sneakers, you know that finding the “perfect” shoe can be challenging. We’re here to help people find that perfect fitting shoe every single time. We have created a way to make a 3D scan of your feet and match that profile with our own (and the world’s largest) database of 3D-scanned shoes. We are also developing technology for 3D printing custom shoes and insoles based on a person’s foot profile. Our goal is to inspire people to do what they love in maximum comfort, whether it’s running a marathon, dancing all night or simply going for a stroll in the park. To accomplish this, we work with the largest shoe retailers and brands (Nike, HOKA, Intersport, Adidas, PUMA, Amazon and many more) across 70+ countries. As an employer, we strive to translate this philosophy into a happy and balanced lifestyle for all our team members, giving them the opportunity to grow and thrive while doing what they love. The fit we hope to find We're looking for an experienced Software Engineer with broad technical interests who wants to work across the full path from raw inputs and Computer Vision, through data processing and model training, to production inference and analytics. This is a software engineering role first: you should be comfortable designing, writing, testing and maintaining production-quality code, primarily in Python. Rather than owning one narrow component, you will help connect the pieces of the system - processing images, 3D scans and other data; maintaining data and training pipelines; improving ML/DNN models; deploying inference; and building analytics and diagnostics around the outputs. The scope is intentionally broad, and that is a core part of the opportunity. We are not looking for someone who is already an expert in every layer. If you are stronger in some areas and less experienced in others, don't let that put you off. What matters most is curiosity, learning speed, technical judgment and the willingness to dig into unfamiliar code, data and systems. You will have significant room to learn across ML, data engineering, Computer Vision and production software while developing deeper expertise over time What you'll do At SafeSize you will work across the end-to-end software chain behind our 3D scanning and recommendation technology - from camera inputs and Computer Vision processing, through data preparation and model training, to production inference, analytics and monitoring. You will not be expected to own every area alone, but you should be comfortable following a problem across boundaries and contributing wherever needed. As part of your role, you will: Develop and maintain production-quality Python software across our ML, data processing, Computer Vision and 3D scanning systems; Build and maintain data pipelines to ingest, clean, transform, validate and version the training, validation and test data used by our ML models; Maintain and improve ML/DNN training pipelines, including reproducible experiments, training, validation, evaluation and the tooling that makes model development reliable; Train, retrain or fine-tune models when needed; evaluate performance; perform error analysis; and help determine whether improvements should come from the model, the data or the surrounding software; Package, version and deploy ML/CV models into production, and maintain reliable inference on-device or in the cloud; Build data-processing and analytics workflows around scan data, model outputs and logs to understand model/product performance, diagnose problems and support better decisions; Design and improve Computer Vision and image/3D processing pipelines for tasks such as feature extraction, camera-based measurements, calibration and geometric analysis; Investigate real-world issues end to end using images, 3D scans, datasets, model outputs, logs and sensor data, and build diagnostics and tests that improve accuracy and robustness; Build APIs, services and internal tools that connect data processing, ML, Computer Vision, inference and analytics with the rest of the SafeSize platform, working closely with Software, Data/ML, DevOps and Hardware teams; Navigate unfamiliar systems and codebases when needed. You may occasionally need to read code in languages other than Python and, where useful, contribute to JavaScript/TypeScript-based tools or interfaces. United by curiosity and a culture of caring, we develop smart solutions that anticipate our customer’s and partner’s needs and solve their challenges. Being part of Zebra Nation means you are seen, heard, valued, and respected. Drawing from our unique perspectives, we collaborate to deliver on our purpose. You’ll have opportunities to learn and lead in a forward-thinking environment, defining your path to a fulfilling career while channeling your skills toward causes you care about—locally and globally. Come make an impact every day at Zebra. What We're Looking For We are looking for an AI Research Scientist specialising in SLAM, Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), and 3D Spatial Perception to join our central CTO Group. In this horizontal, high-impact organisation, you will collaborate with cross-functional business units across the globe and work closely with our London-based research hub of ~15 AI specialists. In this role, you will be bridging the gap between innovation and on-device execution -prototyping new algorithms, training spatial models, and optimising them to run directly on resource-constrained mobile edge devices to power next-generation Augmented Reality (AR), enterprise vision, and edge intelligence. You will be based at our central London office (Endeavour House, Shaftesbury Avenue, WC2H 8JR) on a flexible hybrid model - collaborating in person 3 days a week, with 2 days working from home. Responsibilities Research, design, and implement robust Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), 6-DoF camera pose estimation, and monocular SLAM pipelines tailored for resource-constrained edge hardware. Develop advanced algorithms for spatial localisation, multi-view ray triangulation, sensor fusion (IMU + Camera), and plane-fitting (e.g., RANSAC, PnP) to achieve sub-centimetre overlay accuracy and eliminate tracking drift. Translate research papers into real-time algorithms, optimising neural networks and spatial pipelines for low-latency execution on mobile NPUs, DSPs, and GPUs. Build spatial foundations that deliver seamless on-device AR experiences, barcode/shelf product recognition, OCR, and multi-modal edge AI capabilities without relying on cloud connectivity. Partner with global hardware, software, and product engineering teams to integrate your models into commercial product roadmaps. Qualifications Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related quantitative field with a specialised focus on Computer Vision, Spatial AI, or Robotics. At least 2 years of hands-on experience in research and development of SLAM / Spatial tracking systems. Deep theoretical understanding and hands-on implementation of SLAM (Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping) and VIO (Visual-Inertial Odometry). Strong foundation in 6-DoF pose tracking, sensor fusion (IMU + Vision), and camera calibration (intrinsic/extrinsic parameters). 3D geometric computer vision: ray-plane intersections, epipolar geometry, bundle adjustment, and monocular depth estimation. High proficiency in C++ and/or Python, along with standard ML and Computer Vision frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, OpenCV, ROS/GTSAM/Ceres Solver). items.desc: The Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS) conducts research to advance intelligent systems that perceive, learn, and interact. Through fundamental research across computational, physical, and social dimensions, we shape artificial intelligence and robotics to advance knowledge and benefit society. The Haptic Intelligence Department at the institute’s Stuttgart site is looking for a Research Engineer (m/f/d) - Actuated Bio-Inspired Whisker-Sensor Systems Roles & Responsibilities The Haptic Intelligence Department at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS) seeks a research engineer to work on our Electrovibrissa project, where we are investigating actuated bio-inspired whisker-sensor systems. The successful candidate will carry out research on biomimetic tactile sensing by designing and maintaining the hardware and software components of our whisker-sensor setup. They will also be responsible for conducting data collection, analysis, and visualization, working closely with existing team members on this collaborative research project that also involves the Robotic Materials Department of MPI-IS. The position is preferably full-time for a period of 6 to 12 months. We also encourage applications from individuals who are interested in a part-time position (40% – 90%) for any duration in the specified range. Candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree. Specifically, the successful candidate will: Design and develop hardware for robotic applications of instrumented bio-inspired whiskers that combine commercial sensors (e.g., microphones), custom electrohydraulic actuators, high-voltage amplifiers, and microcontrollers (e.g., Raspberry Pi, Arduino) (25%) Design and develop software for whisker-sensor data acquisition, including data synchronization and integration of low-level control architectures (20%) Develop algorithms for whisker-based object detection and identification of distinct object properties such as surface texture and material classification (20%) Implement machine learning algorithms to evaluate and compare different bio-inspired whiskers with various sensors and different whisker actuation frequencies (15%) Implement compelling real-time data visualizations of whisker-sensor outputs relevant to the robotic demonstrations (10%) Present data and findings in an informative and engaging manner to facilitate understanding of actuated bio-inspired sensors (10%) Education & Experience Applicants should have: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer What You’ll Do Own and evolve the ML and cloud infrastructure used to train and evaluate large models Provision, scale, and maintain multi-node, multi-GPU environments on cloud and/or on-prem, including scheduling, quotas, and capacity planning Support distributed training (PyTorch DDP/FSDP, NCCL) and keep large runs stable, performant, and reproducible Build and optimize storage and networking for petabyte-scale datasets Deploy workloads with Docker and Kubernetes, and manage infrastructure-as-code with Terraform Set up monitoring, logging, and alerting for cluster health, job performance, and cost, and define SLOs and incident response practices Manage secrets, IAM, and network security across research and production Work with researchers to unblock training and support the move from research to served models What We’re Looking For 3+ years in infrastructure, platform, or cloud engineering Hands-on GPU performance debugging (CUDA/NCCL concepts, utilization, network bottlenecks, profiling) Strong experience running AWS, GCP, or Azure, including networking, IAM, and cost management Proficiency with Docker, Kubernetes, and Terraform Strong scripting and automation skills in Python plus Bash or PowerShell Familiarity with distributed training in PyTorch (DDP/FSDP or similar) Experience with observability tooling such as Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or ELK Experience building CI/CD for infrastructure and ML workflows Nice to Have Prior ML infrastructure experience supporting large-scale training Experience running on-prem GPU clusters alongside cloud capacity Experience with model evaluation and serving infrastructure Experience running on-call and incident response Why Join Ownership. You will be responsible for the infrastructure behind a research program, not one corner of a larger platform. Scale. Multi-node GPU training and petabyte-scale datasets are part of the daily work. Proximity to research. You will work alongside the people who depend on your systems. Influence. In a small team, your views on tooling and architecture carry weight. What to Expect This is an on-site role in London. Expect to work across the stack, from cluster operations to developer tooling, and to share responsibility for reliability. If this sounds relevant, get in touch for a confidential conversation.

items.desc:
AI Software Engineer - C++/Python
 Job ID 2026-19000 
 Date posted Sep. 01, 2026 
 Location Lund, Sweden; Manchester, United Kingdom 
 Category Software Engineering 
 Apply 
 About the Role
 We’re looking for experienced software engineers to help develop ExecuTorch, PyTorch’s framework for running AI models efficiently on edge devices.
 You’ll join a team building software across AI model optimisation, compilers, runtimes and hardware acceleration. Our technology spans Python developer tools and ahead-of-time compilation through to portable C++ runtimes and hardware-accelerated backends, giving you the opportunity to contribute at different layers of the software stack.
 A key part of this role is understanding how AI models execute on hardware, identifying bottlenecks and improving cycle count, latency, memory use and power efficiency.
 You’ll move between high-level model transformations and low-level runtime and hardware behaviour to solve complex performance problems.
 ExecuTorch targets Arm technology including Mali GPUs with Neural Graphics, Cortex-A and Cortex-M CPUs, and Ethos-U NPUs. We contribute to ExecuTorch in the open and work with the wider PyTorch community to help developers deploy AI models efficiently across mobile, embedded and other resource-constrained platforms.
 What You’ll Do
 Develop and optimise components of the ExecuTorch compiler, runtime and developer tooling, ranging from Python APIs and model transformations to low-level C and C++ components.
 Analyse and profile AI workloads to identify bottlenecks, improving latency, memory use, cycle count and power efficiency across model transformations, generated code, runtimes and hardware backends.
 Develop optimised backends for Mali GPUs, Cortex-A and Cortex-M CPUs, Ethos-U NPUs and other edge platforms, while investigating software and performance challenges across the stack.
 Identify technical opportunities and take solutions from initial idea through delivery, working with engineers across Arm and contributors in the PyTorch open-source community.
 Share technical knowledge and, depending on your experience, contribute to technical projects and mentor other engineers.
 What We’re Looking For
 We’re looking for professional software engineering experience using C++ and Python, including developing, debugging and maintaining production-quality software.
 You’ll have knowledge of programming, compilers, runtimes or performance optimisation, along with an interest in understanding how software executes on hardware and how its efficiency can be improved. An interest in AI and deploying models on resource-constrained devices will also be valuable.
 You should be able to identify technical problems, determine a practical approach and take work through to completion. The role also requires good communication, technical judgement and the ability to work effectively with engineers across different teams.
 You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification. AI and edge computing are evolving quickly, and relevant experience can come from different technical areas. If you’re keen to develop your knowledge and tackle new technical challenges, we’d like to hear from you!
 Useful Additional Experience
 Experience with PyTorch, ExecuTorch or another machine-learning framework would be useful, as would knowledge of ahead-of-time compilers, graph transformation or model optimisation. We’re also interested in experience with embedded systems, mobile or edge computing, hardware-accelerator programming, performance analysis, Vulkan, open-source development, technical leadership or mentoring.
 Why Join the Team?
 Help develop open-source AI technology used by developers around the world! You’ll have opportunities to build expertise across AI software, compilers, runtimes and edge computing while solving problems that connect software directly with the underlying hardware.
 The breadth of the role allows you to explore both high-level AI frameworks and low-level hardware optimisation, improving performance and power efficiency across a wide range of edge devices. You’ll also work with specialists across Arm and the wider PyTorch ecosystem, with opportunities to develop and share your technical expertise.
 We support different needs and ways of working. If you need reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know and we’ll work with you to provide the support you need.
 Please note that no relocation package is available for this role.
 #LI-CM1
 Our 10x Mindset 
 At Arm, we believe progress happens when people are empowered to think bigger and push beyond what seems possible. Our 10x mindset is about curiosity, ambition and creating impact that will be used by millions. We learn fast, prioritise collaboration and turn bold ideas into real technology. We look for people who are inspired by this way of working and want to grow in an environment where bold ideas are welcomed. Discover how the 10x mindset shapes life at …

items.card: Responsibilities The Haptic Intelligence Department at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS) seeks a research engineer to work on our Electrovibrissa project, where we are investigating actuated bio-inspired whisker-sensor systems. The successful candidate will carry out research on biomimetic tactile sensing by designing and maintaining the hardware and software components of our whisker-sensor
items.desc: The Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS) conducts research to advance intelligent systems that perceive, learn, and interact. Through fundamental research across computational, physical, and social dimensions, we shape artificial intelligence and robotics to advance knowledge and benefit society. The at the institute’s Stuttgart site is looking for a Research Engineer (m/f/d) - Actuated Bio-Inspired Whisker-Sensor Systems Roles & Responsibilities The Haptic Intelligence Department at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems (MPI-IS) seeks a research engineer to work on our Electrovibrissa project, where we are investigating actuated bio-inspired whisker-sensor systems. The successful candidate will carry out research on biomimetic tactile sensing by designing and maintaining the hardware and software components of our whisker-sensor setup. They will also be responsible for conducting data collection, analysis, and visualization, working closely with existing team members on this collaborative research project that also involves the Robotic Materials Department of MPI-IS. The position is preferably full-time for a period of 6 to 12 months. We also encourage applications from individuals who are interested in a part-time position (40% – 90%) for any duration in the specified range. Candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree. Specifically, the successful candidate will: Design and develop hardware for robotic applications of instrumented bio-inspired whiskers that combine commercial sensors (e.g., microphones), custom electrohydraulic actuators, high-voltage amplifiers, and microcontrollers (e.g., Raspberry Pi, Arduino) (25%) Design and develop software for whisker-sensor data acquisition, including data synchronization and integration of low-level control architectures (20%) Develop algorithms for whisker-based object detection and identification of distinct object properties such as surface texture and material classification (20%) Implement machine learning algorithms to evaluate and compare different bio-inspired whiskers with various sensors and different whisker actuation frequencies (15%) Implement compelling real-time data visualizations of whisker-sensor outputs relevant to the robotic demonstrations (10%) Present data and findings in an informative and engaging manner to facilitate understanding of actuated bio-inspired sensors (10%) Education & Experience Applicants should have: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Neuroscience, or related fields – required Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Neuroscience, or related fields – preferred but not required Patience and persistence when troubleshooting complex hardware and software systems, combined with a rigorous and systematic approach to experimental work and data analysis Experience with machine learning techniques Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or similar programming languages Experience with microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, ESP boards) Knowledge of software engineering practices, including object-oriented programming (OOP) and version control using Git Ability to work independently and as part of a team Eagerness to learn and explore new topics Strong written and oral communication skills in English Our offer The position will be located in Stuttgart at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems. You can expect an international environment with regular opportunities for further personal and professional growth. You will work closely with scientists, other engineers, administrative staff, and IT. You will enjoy an open, multicultural, and informal working environment. Salary and contract will be based on qualifications and previous professional experience according to the Public Service Wage Agreement (TVöD Bund) guidelines. All social benefits of public service apply. With us you receive a financial contribution to the job ticket (ÖPNV) and the possibility of mobile working. Application To apply, please submit a cover letter, your CV, and the contact details of two professional references. Please prepare these documents in English and upload them as one PDF file to our . The position will be open until filled. Preference will be given to the applications received by November 1, 2026. Questions related to this position should be addressed to Dr. Andrew K. Schulz at . The Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society seeks to increase the number of women in its workforce in those areas where they are underrepresented and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply. Closing date for applications 01.11.2026

items.desc: Robot Learning Research Engineer | Paris Our client is a seed stage physical AI company based in Paris, spun out of one of Europe's leading robotics research institutes. Their software lets a humanoid robot learn a new industrial task from a handful of demonstrations and be working on the production line in under an hour, with no code. The software is hardware agnostic and runs across multiple humanoid platforms. It is already deployed with major European manufacturers in automotive, industrial equipment and consumer goods. The team is small and research led. The CTO is a world renowned researcher in robotics and machine learning, and the company combines the rigour of a research lab with the pace of an early stage startup. The role You will design the few shot imitation learning algorithms at the core of the product. The central challenge is data efficiency: learning robust, generalising behaviour from a few demonstrations rather than thousands. Every improvement you make ships directly into real factories. As one of the first 15 hires, you will help shape the company's long term research agenda, culture and hiring. Responsibilities - Design, prototype and evaluate few shot imitation learning algorithms - Advance the state of the art in imitation learning, policy learning and representation learning for control - Run rigorous experiments on real robots, including humanoids, mobile manipulators and industrial arms - Turn research prototypes into algorithms robust enough for production - Work closely with the Vision & Perception and Integration teams to take research from prototype to deployment - Help shape the research roadmap and future hiring Requirements - PhD in robotics, machine learning or a related field from a leading research lab - Research experience at a top academic group or industry lab - Publications at top venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS or ICML - Deep expertise in imitation learning, learning from demonstration or policy learning for robots - Hands on experience training and debugging learning systems on real robots, not only in simulation - Strong Python and PyTorch - Professional English Nice to have - Few shot learning or meta learning for control - Representation learning for embodied agents - Experience with humanoids or other high DoF platforms - Postdoctoral or industry research lab experience - A track record of taking research into deployed systems - ROS 2 familiarity What's on offer - Open salary for the right candidate - Early and generous founding equity - Full relocation support to Paris - EU and non EU candidates welcome - English speaking team, no French required - Access to a fleet of advanced robots, including humanoids - Research that ships into real factories - Real ownership of the research agenda

items.title: Robotics Foundation Models Engineer (Mensch)
items.card: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotics-Anwendungen durch Physical AI und die NeuraGym-Plattform voran — du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Kundenroboter, nicht nur das Modell im Repo. Führe die gesamte Pipeline aus: Du führst Foundation Models in produktionsreife Robotics-Intelligence über — die komplette NeuraGym-Pipeline mit
items.desc: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotics-Anwendungen durch Physical AI und die NeuraGym-Plattform voran — du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Kundenroboter, nicht nur das Modell im Repo. Führe die gesamte Pipeline aus: Du führst Foundation Models in produktionsreife Robotics-Intelligence über — die komplette NeuraGym-Pipeline mit Teleoperation, Data Annotation, Training, Simulation, Deployment und Validation — tailored auf echte Robotics-Anwendungen. Du definierst die Data Strategy und besitzt den gesamten Post-Training-Loop mit Hyperparameter-Iteration, Data Mixture, LoRA und ehrlicher Evaluation. Deploye zu Real-Time Control: Du bringst Policies vom Checkpoint zu Real-Time Closed-Loop Control — Distillation, Quantization, Action Chunking, Latency Budgets und On-Device/Edge Inference unter den Cycle-Time und Reliability Requirements des Kunden. Beherrsche den vollen Robotics Stack: Du arbeitest über NEURA OS und die Control Layer hinweg — Real-Time Control, Kinematics, Motion Planning, Force/Impedance Control und Safety Architecture — und integrierst gelernte Policies sauber mit dem Low-Level Controller statt ihn als Black Box zu behandeln. Hands-on System Integration: Du arbeitest direkt an MAiRA, MiPA, LARA und humanoiden Plattformen zusammen mit multidisziplinären Engineering-Teams — End-Effektoren und Tool Changer, Sensor-Auswahl und Mounting, Calibration, elektrische und Fieldbus-Schnittstellen und die mechanische Realität der Zelle. Aktiviere und unterstütze Kunden: Du leitest Nutzer in NeuraGym ein, reviewst Training Pipelines und Scripts, identifizierst Data-Quality-Issues, troubleshootst Model-Verhalten und bietest Hands-On-Support, um hartnäckige Blockers zu lösen. Cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit: Du bist eine Schlüsselschnittstelle zwischen Cloud und AI Teams — du gewährleistest sanfte Zusammenarbeit, technische Alignment und effiziente Problem-Lösungen über Domänen hinweg. Baue Evaluation-Rigor auf: Du erstellst die Eval Harnesses, Success-Rate Benchmarks und Regression Tests, die entscheiden, ob eine Policy ready für Handover ist — und machst Failure Modes sichtbar, bevor der Kunde sie findet. Research in Production: Du prototypisierst Techniken aus aktuellen Papers zusammen mit unserem Research-Team und bringst die ins Produktionsdeployment, die Kontakt mit der Realität überstehen. Schließe den Feedback-Loop: Du übersetzt Field-Erfahrung und Customer Insights in Actionable Feedback für sowohl die NeuraGym Product-Roadmap als auch die NEURA Core AI Roadmap. Was du mitbringst Dein Hintergrund: Master-Abschluss oder PhD in Informatik, Robotik, Elektrotechnik oder verwandtem Bereich. ML in Robotics Tiefe: 5+ Jahre praktische Machine-Learning-Erfahrung in Robotics — stark in mindestens einer von Vision-Based Manipulation, Reinforcement/Imitation Learning oder Multimodalen Modellen, und motiviert, den Rest zu lernen. Fine-Tuning-Expertise: Nachgewiesene Erfahrung beim Fine-Tuning großer vortrainierter Modelle für Robotics oder eine andere Domäne: PEFT/LoRA und vollständige Fine-Tunes, Dataset Curation, Distillation und Evaluation. Vertrautheit mit dem Open-VLA- und Policy-Learning-Ecosystem (z. B. π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, LeRobot, Diffusion Policies) ist ein großer Plus. Programming-Skills: Solide Python-Kenntnisse (C++ ist ein Plus); praktische Erfahrung mit PyTorch oder TensorFlow. Cloud und Simulation: AWS-, Azure- oder GCP-Erfahrung und Vertrautheit mit Robotics-Simulation-Tools (IsaacSim, MuJoCo, etc.) sind Pluses. Robotics Software Stack: Working Command des Robotics Software Stack jenseits der Model Layer — Robot Operating Systems und Middleware (NEURA OS, ROS/ROS2 oder vergleichbar), Real-Time Control, Kinematics und Motion Planning, Force/Impedance Control und wie eine gelernte Policy in den Low-Level Controller und seine Safety Layer integriert wird. Hardware-Literacy: Solides Verständnis von Roboter-Hardware — Drives und Joint Modules, Torque Sensing und Encoder, End-Effektoren, Sensor-Integration, Calibration, elektrische und Fieldbus-Schnittstellen (z. B. EtherCAT) und Functional Safety Concepts — genug, um ein Model-Problem von einem Machine-Problem vor Ort zu unterscheiden. Execution-Mindset: Nachgewiesene Problem-Solving-Fähigkeiten, Fähigkeit, mehrere Projekte parallel zu handhaben, und ein starker Bias zu Execution und persönlichem Commitment. Du nimmst Deployments persönlich, arbeitest dich durch Rückschläge und misst dich daran, was beim Kunden läuft. Kommunikation: Klarer Communicator, der zwischen Forschern, Ingenieuren und End-Usern übersetzt. Du sprichst Englisch und Deutsch auf solidem Niveau (B2–C1). Reisebereitschaft: Bereitschaft, häufig zu Kundenseiten und NeuraGyms zu reisen (ca. 40–60%).

We're looking for researchers and domain experts with deep machine learning knowledge to design the evaluation challenges that define — and push — the limits of today's most capable AI systems. This isn't routine review work. You'll apply your hard-earned research expertise to craft problems that state-of-the-art models genuinely struggle to solve. Your contributions directly shape how the next generation of AI is measured, benchmarked, and improved. Organization: Alignerr Type: Hourly Contract Location: Fully Remote Commitment: 10–40 hours/week What You'll Do Design complex, original machine learning problems rooted in your specific domain of expertise Craft evaluation tasks that require advanced domain knowledge well beyond standard ML pipelines Draw from your own research experience to create problems that genuinely challenge state-of-the-art AI Define rigorous problem statements, evaluation criteria, and gold-standard solutions Assess AI-generated ML solutions for correctness, creativity, and methodological soundness Document problem difficulty levels, required domain knowledge, and expected AI failure modes Collaborate asynchronously with a global team of researchers and engineers Who You Are Graduate-level expertise (MS or PhD preferred) in a scientific or technical domain that intersects with machine learning Strong working knowledge of ML methods — model selection, feature engineering, evaluation metrics, and pipeline design Deep familiarity with active research problems in your field Able to identify precisely where general ML knowledge falls short and specialized domain insight becomes critical Experience publishing or conducting original research is highly valued Excellent written communication — you can articulate complex problems clearly and precisely Self-motivated and comfortable working independently on intellectually demanding tasks Example Domains (Not Exhaustive) Computational biology, genomics, or bioinformatics Climate science and environmental modeling Medical imaging and healthcare ML Materials science and computational chemistry Astrophysics and signal processing Natural language processing for low-resource or specialized corpora Robotics, control theory, or reinforcement learning in complex environments Financial modeling and quantitative analysis Why Join Us Work at the true frontier of AI evaluation and safety research Collaborate with top research labs pushing the boundaries of what AI can do Finally put your specialized domain expertise to use in a high-impact, meaningful way Full autonomy over your schedule — work when and how you do your best thinking Flexible, fully remote contract with potential for ongoing work and deeper research involvement Build your profile as a recognized contributor to cutting-edge AI development Join a items.desc: The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university. We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special. Overview Strep A is a common bacterial infection that causes spectacular, unexpected outbreaks of disease every few years. The cause of these outbreaks is unknown, but several factors are likely to contribute, for example, the burden of circulating viral infections. This project strives to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven early warning system to predict the risk of Strep A outbreaks and upsurges before they occur. The RA will work to integrate multiple datasets and apply a combination of mathematical modelling methods, including time-series modelling and probabilistic machine learning. Anticipated work includes developing and training models, with validation and refinement steps using retrospective data and simulation work undertaken where appropriate. This will be followed by a further evaluation phase to assess model performance, usability, and potential for real-world application using prospective data. Main Duties And Responsibilities Collate, clean and prepare epidemiological datasets from a range of sources, ensuring data quality. Apply and help develop machine learning models, including feature preparation, model selection, fitting, and hyperparameter tuning. Conduct exploratory data analysis and produce descriptive statistics and clear visualisations. Contribute to model evaluation and validation, including selecting appropriate performance metrics demonstrating model generalisability to the real world. Ensure all activities comply with data protection legislation, research ethics requirements, and information governance procedures for handling sensitive health data. Work proactively and on own initiative, responding constructively to feedback from the line managers / principal investigators. Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post. Person Specification Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. items.desc: Job Type: Flexible Contract (Remote) Job Summary: We are hiring senior security researchers, including faculty, research scientists, and experienced postdoctoral researchers, for a contract project that tests whether frontier AI models can carry out real research work in a command line environment. You will design research-grade tasks that a leading AI model cannot solve, then review how and why the model fails. What you will do Design self-contained command line tasks drawn from the practice of machine learning research, such as implementing a method from a paper's description alone, locating the error in a flawed experimental setup, reproducing a reported result and explaining a discrepancy, implementing a custom loss function or optimizer correctly, and running a sound statistical comparison between two models. Build the task environment, including code, data, and dependencies, write a reference solution, and write automated tests that verify whether a solution is correct. Because results can vary between runs, tests need to be deterministic or use well-justified tolerances. Run your task against a frontier AI model, review its attempt with the same rigor you would apply to a paper under peer review, and refine the task until the failure reflects a real gap in the model's capability rather than ambiguity or trick wording. Work with reviewers to bring each task to acceptance. Who we are looking for A PhD in security engineering, machine learning, computer science, statistics, or a closely related field. Industry or academic experience in machine learning research, in academia or industry. Years spent on doctoral research count toward this total. At least one publication, ideally peer-reviewed work at a recognized machine learning venue or journal. Deep working knowledge of Python and at least one major framework, such as PyTorch or JAX. Fluency in the Linux command line, shell scripting, Docker, and Git. Experience as a peer reviewer, or in designing course assignments and automated grading, is a strong advantage, because the work draws on the same skills. Why Cobalt AI Advance frontier AI where it counts. Apply your research expertise to the data that frontier labs cannot obtain any other way, where your reasoning directly shapes how the next generation of models works through technical problems. Grow professionally. Expand your influence through evaluation projects, advisory roles, and research collaborations, while deepening your understanding of how frontier models are trained and assessed. Work with a top-tier network. Collaborate with researchers from leading institutions and labs on high-impact, flexible work. Set your own schedule. Flexible 10 to 40 hour weeks that fit around your research position and your life. Competitive pay. Rates vary by project and are determined by a number of factors, including scope, skillset, and experience.

items.desc: Our Mission Reflection is a research lab making intelligence open and accessible for everyone to use, customize, and build on. About The Role You will build the evaluation infrastructure that researchers use to understand model capabilities, guide training decisions, and assess readiness for release. The role spans evaluation authoring, distributed execution, and results analysis, with a particular focus on pre-training. You will work directly with researchers to make evaluations faster, more reliable, and easier to use, ensuring that the results accurately reflect the models being evaluated. Design and evolve evaluation abstractions. Build clear APIs and data models for evaluation tasks, datasets, configurations, model outputs, and scores, making it straightforward to add new evaluations and extend existing workflows. Build scalable, reliable execution infrastructure. Develop distributed systems for evaluating model checkpoints throughout training and ahead of release, with robust orchestration, observability, and recovery from failures. Optimize evaluation and inference performance. Profile inference servers and distributed execution to improve throughput, GPU utilization, and time to results. Establish evaluation correctness and reproducibility. Build validation and regression tests, version datasets and configurations, and preserve the provenance needed to reproduce results and investigate discrepancies. Build researcher-facing tools. Create intuitive interfaces and dashboards for inspecting model outputs, comparing checkpoints and experiments, and debugging unexpected behavior. Operate and monitor evaluations as training progresses. Track evaluation workloads and results, triage failures, and develop alerts and diagnostics that help distinguish changes in model quality from inference or evaluation issues. Turn research needs into reusable systems. Partner directly with researchers to identify bottlenecks, prioritize high-impact improvements, and turn bespoke workflows into self-service tools that work across teams. About You Strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Rust, with the ability to reason deeply about concurrency, memory behavior, and performance. Experience designing, building, and operating reliable, maintainable distributed systems, with sound judgment about interfaces, failure modes, and architectural tradeoffs. items.desc: Flexible batteries with seamless integration in textiles will revolutionize the healthcare system. Such batteries could power sensors to continuously monitor vital signals (e.g. glucose) and antennas to immediately transmit the information to a medical doctor when urgent action is required. However, such batteries need to be completely safe and non-toxic, as well as energy dense and lightweight; requirements that are often conflicting. The SUSTAIN programme grant (www.sustain-pg.org) will address this challenge using water, lithium and special polymer fabrics to build the batteries. Compared to traditional batteries that use toxic organic solvents and salts, the SUSTAIN batteries will operate using non-toxic lithium-conductive hydrated polymers that enable high deformability and stretchability. Via collaborative work with leading textile designers, experts in printed electronics and wireless communications and sustainability analysts, the SUSTAIN program will build working demonstrations of textile electronics that can act as wearable doctors. This post is suitable for chemists or materials scientists with a PhD (awarded or imminent) in chemistry, materials science or a closely related discipline or equivalent qualification and experience. Although the current funding for this vacancy is for 2 years, we expect to be able to extend the contract further, and there is flexibility about the start date. For informal enquiries about the project, please contact Prof. Nuria Garcia-Araez (N.Garcia-Araez@soton.ac.uk). The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Center for Quantum Computing in Pasadena, CA, is looking to hire a Quantum Research Scientist in the Fabrication group. You will join a multi-disciplinary team of theoretical and experimental physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. You should have a deep and broad knowledge of device fabrication techniques. 
Candidates with a track record of original scientific contributions will be preferred. We are looking for candidates with strong engineering principles, resourcefulness and a bias for action, superior problem solving, and excellent communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. As a research scientist you will be expected to work on new ideas and stay abreast of the field of experimental quantum computation.

Job Description Summary 
You will work within an interdisciplinary team to innovate and push the technical envelope in all aspects of magnetic resonance imaging. You will have opportunities to work both on MRI systems hardware as well as algorithms and pulse sequence development. The research and development work will be across 1.5T-3.0T whole body and 3.0T-7.0T high-performance, head-only MRI platforms. 
 Job Description 
 Job Description 
 As a Magnetic Resonance Research Scientist, you will:
 Apply deep knowledge in MR physics, mathematics, engineering and chemistry to conceptualize and prototype novel MR systems and applications that address key clinical needs.
 Develop impactful applications that leverage next-generation MRI sub-systems that have enhanced imaging capabilities. Examples are in high-performance gradient coils, RF coils, receiver sub-systems, gradient drivers, etc.
 Develop and deploy investigational MR applications and systems in clinical and preclinical environments for tests and validation.
 Determine the impact of systems hardware performance on image quality and safety.
 Develop algorithmic and/ or systems hardware solutions for MR-guided therapy and interventional applications.
 Grow external collaborations with academic and industry partners through joint publications, grant submissions and advanced technology development.
 Work with clinicians to refine emerging technologies for clinical applications.
 Create intellectual property by generating invention disclosures and filing patents.
 Maintain external visibility through conference presentations and peer-reviewed journal publications.
 Required Qualifications 
 Ph.D. degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Computer Engineering, or other related fields, with at least 3 years of research experience.
 A demonstrated record of research and development outcomes as evidenced by peer-reviewed conference proceedings and journal publications.
 Strong fundamentals in MR imaging physics and sub-systems, signal processing and electromagnetic theory.
 Demonstrated strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to understand and address root causes of MR image quality issues in investigational prototypes.
 Proficiency in programming in C, Python and/ or simulation tools.
 Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. You will need to have valid, on-going authorization to work in the U.S.
 Must be willing to work out of an office located in Niskayuna, NY.
 You must submit your application for employment on the careers page at https://careers.gehealthcare.com to be considered.
 Desired Characteristics 
 Demonstrated ability to originate and follow through on ideas.
 High levels of curiosity, independence and adaptability.
 Strong interpersonal skills.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Experience in writing and executing grant proposals.
 Experience in developing or modifying components of MR sub-systems leading to measurable changes in image quality and new applications.
 Experience in EM and multi-physics modeling, especially for analysis of RF transmit and gradient field bioeffects.

items.desc: Spanish (Spain) Audio Transcriptionist (AI Training) About The Role What if your native fluency in Peninsular Spanish could directly shape how AI understands real human conversation? We're looking for detail-oriented transcriptionists based in London with native-level command of Spain Spanish to produce precise, high-quality transcriptions of spoken Spanish audio — helping build the datasets that teach AI systems to truly listen. London's large and diverse Spanish-speaking population makes it one of Europe's best talent hubs for this work. You'll tackle real-world audio featuring crosstalk, multiple speakers, background noise, and natural speech patterns — turning authentic conversation into clean, structured text. No prior AI experience needed. Organization: Alignerr Type: Hourly Contract Location: Remote Commitment: 10–40 hours/week What You'll Do Listen to audio recordings in Peninsular Spanish and produce accurate, verbatim transcriptions following detailed style and formatting guidelines Handle challenging audio scenarios — including crosstalk, overlapping speakers, filled pauses (e.g., "eh", "mm"), background noise, and varying audio quality Accurately identify and differentiate between multiple speakers within a single recording Apply consistent formatting conventions for timestamps, speaker labels, non-verbal sounds, and unclear segments Flag audio segments that are unintelligible or ambiguous, following established protocols Maintain a high standard of accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail across all assignments Work independently and asynchronously — fully on your own schedule Who You Are Native or near-native speaker of Spain Spanish (Peninsular Spanish) — with an intuitive command of Castilian vocabulary, expressions, accents, and speech patterns Exceptional listening skills with an ear for subtlety — you catch what others miss Comfortable working with imperfect audio: background noise, fast speech, interruptions, and overlapping dialogue don't throw you off Naturally detail-oriented with a methodical, patient approach to repetitive work Able to follow detailed style guides and formatting rules with precision and consistency Strong written skills in Spanish — your transcriptions read cleanly and accurately Self-motivated and reliable when working independently No prior AI or tech experience required Nice to Have Professional experience as a transcriptionist, court reporter, or stenographer Background in subtitle creation, closed-captioning editing, or media post-production Training or experience in linguistics, phonetics, or language documentation Prior work with annotation platforms, data labeling tools, or AI training workflows Familiarity with different regional accents and dialects within Spain Experience handling specialised or technical audio content Why Join Us Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs Fully remote and flexible — work when and skills on diverse, real-world audio Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

items.card: Your Mission & Challenges As an AI Data Annotation Specialist, you will operate at the intersection of data ingestion, annotation workflow design, and machine learning — with a strong focus on building training datasets for multimodal foundation models that connect perception, language, and robot action. Your primary responsibility is to design and maintain scalable workflows for automated and human-in-the-loop
items.desc: Your Mission & Challenges As an AI Data Annotation Specialist, you will operate at the intersection of data ingestion, annotation workflow design, and machine learning — with a strong focus on building training datasets for multimodal foundation models that connect perception, language, and robot action. Your primary responsibility is to design and maintain scalable workflows for automated and human-in-the-loop annotation, ensuring that datasets are properly labeled, curated, validated, and formatted for efficient model training and evaluation. You play a critical role in enabling high-quality embodied AI systems by transforming raw multimodal robot data into structured, reliable, and semantically rich training datasets. Design, build, and maintain pipelines for automated, semi-automated, and human-in-the-loop data annotation, with a focus on subtask labeling for long-horizon robot demonstrations Develop annotation workflows for language-grounded robot learning and Visual Question Answering (VQA) datasets, including instruction generation, subtask decomposition, and grounding of natural language in visual and Your work will span the full research-to-product cycle: formulating problems from real industrial use cases, developing and evaluating new methods, validating them on operational plant
items.desc: KIIO is building AI for AI for process reliability in chemical manufacturing and beyond. Chemical and process manufacturing plants generate enormous amounts of sensor data, yet troubleshooting remains largely reactive. Emerging problems can propagate across interconnected equipment and control loops long before conventional alarms reveal what is happening, while identifying the true root cause can still require hours or days of manual investigation. KIIO develops interpretable diagnostic technology that learns how industrial processes behave from operational data and detects when these relationships begin to change. By modelling the plant as an interconnected dynamical system, our technology identifies emerging faults, traces how disturbances propagate, and helps engineers understand where a problem originates, what may be causing it, and how to respond, without requiring historical examples of every fault. Our goal is to give process engineers and operators the intelligence they need to intervene before deviations become downtime, equipment damage, or quality losses. Role Description We are looking for a Founding Research Engineer to help turn KIIO's research into a robust industrial product. You will work at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, fault diagnosis, and industrial process data , developing algorithms that learn from multivariate sensor data and reason about complex interconnected systems. Your work will span the full research-to-product cycle: formulating problems from real industrial use cases, developing and evaluating new methods, validating them on operational plant data, and translating successful approaches into software that can eventually run continuously in industrial environments. You will work closely with the founder, research collaborators, and industrial partners, and have significant influence over KIIO's technical direction and product architecture. Typical problems include : modelling complex and partially observed industrial dynamical systems; detecting subtle process deviations under changing operating conditions; localising faults and estimating their severity; distinguishing sensor, actuator, and process-related faults; reasoning about fault propagation through interconnected processes and control loops; building reliable evaluation and deployment pipelines for real-world industrial data. Qualifications We are looking for someone with strong technical depth and, equally importantly, the desire to turn research into something that works in the real world. Master's or PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Control, Signal Processing, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Mechanical/Chemical Engineering , or a related quantitative field. Strong background in one or more of: fault detection and diagnosis, dynamical systems, time-series modelling, system identification, graph machine learning, signal processing, or control . Strong mathematical and algorithmic reasoning, with the ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems rigorously. Experience developing and evaluating machine-learning or data-driven methods on real datasets. Strong programming skills, particularly in Python and modern scientific/ML tooling. Ability to write clean, maintainable software and translate research prototypes into robust implementations. Comfortable working with noisy, incomplete, high-dimensional sensor data rather than curated benchmark datasets. Interested in understanding why a system behaves the way it does , rather than treating models purely as black boxes. Comfortable working closely with process engineers and industrial partners to translate domain knowledge into technical solutions. Able to work independently and take ownership in a small, fast-moving team. Strong written and spoken English. Particularly relevant backgrounds include PhD researchers or engineers working on fault diagnosis, system identification, process monitoring, industrial AI, time-series ML, graph learning, or data-driven control who want to move from research toward building a real product.

items.desc: L'école MIRA est une 'école d'ingénieur·e·s, accréditée par la Commission des Titres d'Ingénieur et reconnue par l'État. Implantée à Ajaccio et à Bastia, elle forme en robotique, intelligence artificielle, cybersécurité, marketing et innovation. Depuis 2010, sa raison d'être est de contribuer au développement économique et social de la Corse en développant les compétences sur l'île et en y ancrant les talents. Son équipe de recherche MIRA-Recherche, travaille sur la robotique interactive : elle étudie les usages pour intégrer l'IA, l'IoT, la robotique dans des interactions humain-machine utiles aux organisations (cobotique, jumeaux numériques, objets connectés). Le contexte Le poste associe des activités d’enseignement, de recherche, de formation professionnelle, d'animation d'ateliers et de représentation de l'école. Les activités pédagogiques. Les activités pédagogiques portent sur les programmes dispensés au sein de l’école. Les activités de recherche s’inscrivent dans le cadre d’un projet financé consacré à la transition des entreprises corses vers l'industrie 5.0 : une industrie qui associe robotique, objets connectés et intelligence artificielle tout en plaçant l'humain au centre des systèmes. Ce que nous proposons Un poste varié qui associe recherche appliquée avec des entreprises partenaires, enseignement en formation initiale et professionnelle, ateliers et représentation de l'école. L'accès au LabTech de MIRA : impression 3D, découpe laser, CNC 4 axes, atelier PCB, matériel IoT et Arduino, réalité virtuelle, drones et rovers. Un travail en réseau avec les partenaires de MIRA-Recherche. Une équipe à taille humaine et un cadre de vie à Ajaccio, entre mer et montagne. Avantages : Mutuelle Formation Activités de recherche Concevoir l'architecture des réseaux de capteurs et l'électronique basse consommation ; garantir la qualité des mesures en conditions réelles. Concevoir la chaîne d'imagerie multispectrale de la vigne (fixe ou sur drone) et la vision pour le contrôle qualité sur les lignes. Optimiser et embarquer les modèles d'IA sur des cibles contraintes ; prendre en compte la sécurité des objets connectés et la protection des données. Rédiger les livrables et publier ; proposer des sujets de stage et de thèse ; co-encadrer des doctorants, ou les diriger si vous êtes titulaire de l'HDR. Activités d'enseignement Assurer des cours, TD, TP et projets dans le programme Ingénieur et dans le parcours CLIC. Encadrer des stages et des missions de fin d'études ; participer aux jurys ; faire évoluer les contenus d'embarqué et d'IoT. Intervenir en formation professionnelle auprès des entreprises et des salariés. Vous enseignerez dans le programme Ingénieur en Robotique & Informatique (titre d'ingénieur accrédité CTI, Bac+5), dans le parcours CLIC — Conception Logicielle, IA & Cybersécurité (Bachelor DIAC, Bac+3, et Master of Science BIHAR, Bac+5,), ainsi qu'en formation professionnelle. Les enseignements confiés seront définis avec la Direction des études. Domaines d'enseignement : électronique et systèmes embarqués, réseaux de capteurs et objets connectés, vision par ordinateur et intelligence artificielle embarquée, dans le programme Ingénieur comme dans le parcours CLIC. Animation d'ateliers Animer des ateliers au LabTech de MIRA et avec les entreprises partenaires, pour des publics étudiants, professionnels et scolaires. Manifestations et représentation Présenter des démonstrations lors des journées portes ouvertes, des salons d'orientation et des événements de l'école. Représenter MIRA dans les salons numériques et industriels, les conférences, et auprès des entreprises et des collectivités. Diplômes et expérience Doctorat en systèmes embarqués, IA, électronique, informatique ou vision par ordinateur ; une expérience post-doctorale ou industrielle est appréciée. La qualification en tant que maître de conférence est recommandée. Une HDR est un plus. Publications dans le domaine des systèmes embarqués, IA, de l'IoT ou de la vision. Première expérience d'enseignement dans le supérieur. Compétences scientifiques et techniques Systèmes embarqués : microcontrôleurs et nano-ordinateurs, C/C++, conception de cartes, gestion de l'énergie. Réseaux de capteurs et IoT : LoRaWAN, MQTT, protocoles basse consommation, sécurité des objets connectés. Vision et IA embarquée : imagerie multispectrale, optimisation et déploiement de modèles sur cibles contraintes (Jetson, Raspberry Pi ou équivalent), Python, PyTorch, OpenCV. Une expérience de déploiement en extérieur ou en agriculture de précision est un atout. Qualités attendues Goût du terrain et des installations réelles, capacité à dialoguer avec des non-spécialistes. Sens pédagogique auprès de publics variés, du Bachelor au Bac+5, en formation initiale et en alternance. Travail en équipe pluridisciplinaire, autonomie, rigueur. Français et anglais courants (enseignement possible en anglais).
