items.desc: Job Details Section Electrochemistry Location: Highfield Campus Salary £37,369 to £45,641 Per annum Full Time Fixed Term for 2 years Closing Date: Monday 16 November 2026 Interview Date To be confirmed Reference 3526226EB Flexible batteries with seamless integration in textiles will revolutionize the healthcare system. Such batteries could power sensors to continuously monitor vital signals (e.g. glucose) and antennas to immediately transmit the information to a medical doctor when urgent action is required. However, such batteries need to be completely safe and non-toxic, as well as energy dense and lightweight; requirements that are often conflicting. The SUSTAIN programme grant (www.sustain-pg.org) will address this challenge using water, lithium and special polymer fabrics to build the batteries. Compared to traditional batteries that use toxic organic solvents and salts, the SUSTAIN batteries will operate using non-toxic lithium-conductive hydrated polymers that enable high deformability and stretchability. Via collaborative work with leading textile designers, experts in printed electronics and wireless communications and sustainability analysts, the SUSTAIN program will build working demonstrations of textile electronics that can act as wearable doctors. This post is suitable for chemists or materials scientists with a PhD (awarded or imminent) in chemistry, materials science or a closely related discipline or equivalent qualification and experience. Although the current funding for this vacancy is for 2 years, we expect to be able to extend the contract further, and there is flexibility about the start date. For informal enquiries about the project, please contact Prof. Nuria Garcia-Araez (N.Garcia-Araez@soton.ac.uk). items.desc:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs. You'll work at the frontier of audio AI, shaping the models behind products used by millions of people. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy:

 - Training state-of-the-art models - across any modality.

 - Pushing existing models further through post-training, data curation, architectural improvements, and novel training paradigms.

 - Designing rigorous benchmarks and evaluations that tell us whether a new model iteration is genuinely better - and why.
   
   


REQUIREMENTS 

We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions.

Ideally you bring:

 - 3+ years of experience in the field of AI, with an emphasis on implementing, training, and improving machine learning models.

 - Demonstrated capacity to autonomously evaluate novel concepts or enhance existing machine learning projects, potentially contributing to published work.

 - Experience conducting exploratory research to improve the quality of gathered data.
   


LOCATION

The
items.desc: Job number NAT02307 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 3 Nov 2026 About the role Do you have expertise in genetic engineering and want to contribute to developing next-generation strategies to control mosquito populations that transmit malaria? We have an exciting opportunity for a Research Associate to join a new research programme funded by the Gates Foundation and focused on developing self-limiting genetic strategies for the population suppression of Anopheles mosquitoes. The successful candidate will play a key role in conducting independent research as part of a small team. The experimental work will focus on improving proof-of-principle technologies that we have already developed, with the aim of advancing them towards potential future deployment, as well as investigating new target genes and developing novel molecular tools to support the next generation of these technologies. What you would be doing As a Research Associate, you will play an active role in planning and delivering research within our programme. You will take initiative in designing and conducting experiments, developing appropriate molecular and experimental approaches, and analysing robust and reproducible data. You will maintain accurate records of your work and contribute to publications, presentations to funders and research meetings. You will work collaboratively with scientists, technicians and students at Imperial and with external collaborators in the UK and internationally. You will also contribute to the supervision and development of undergraduate and postgraduate students and research assistants and, where appropriate, help coordinate the work of small research teams. Alongside your research, you will contribute to the smooth running of the laboratory and to maintaining a safe, collaborative and productive research environment. What we are looking for We are looking for a motivated and proactive researcher with experience in molecular biology and genetic engineering, including DNA cloning, genetic construct design and CRISPR-Cas9 or related genome-editing approaches. You will also have experience with mosquitoes or other model organisms and transcriptomic data analysis. Previous experience with molecular and genetic assays is required as well as basic experience in bioinformatics and data analysis. Experience in embryo microinjection work would be highly advantageous. What we can offer you You will join a collaborative research environment at Imperial College London, with the opportunity to contribute to research addressing major global health challenges. The Group has a long-standing relationship with the Target Malaria research consortium, providing opportunities to engage with researchers and initiatives across the consortium and gain insight into the development, evaluation and potential deployment of genetic strategies for malaria control. You will have access to Imperial’s dedicated career development support for researchers, including 10 development days each year, alongside opportunities for progression, a competitive benefits package and a supportive, inclusive working environment. Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant. This is a full-time post. This role is for a fixed-term contract 31 August 2028, extendable for an additional 12 months subject to funding availability. If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Federica Bernardini (f.bernardini11@imperial.ac.uk) or Ms Clelia Supparo (c.supparo@imperial.ac.uk). items.desc: Job number NAT02295 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences (Silwood Park) Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Silwood Park Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 30 Nov 2026 About the role This research associated with this post will be part of a wider team within the new Horizon Europe OceanSOS project https://oceansos.net/. This exciting interdisciplinary project aims to determine the impact of seamounts and the currents they create on stimulating the overlying biological carbon pump (BCP), to then inform marine spatial planning. The knowledge generated will provide a stronger foundation for assessing future ocean risks and developing sustainable management approaches. By improving understanding of the links between biodiversity, food webs, and carbon cycling, this work will support decision-making aimed at protecting ocean ecosystems and the processes that sustain them. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of an international team of biogeochemists, physical ocean modellers, ecologists and policy makers. What you would be doing You will focus on identifying how seafloor topology influences the mesopelagic biological carbon pump, specifically looking at particle type, size and microbial remineralisation across a seamount and abyssal plain. You will be part of a wider team https://oceansos.net/wp3 capturing the contributions of larger organisms, deep-sea communities, and connections between the seafloor and the open ocean in the BCP. Your specific responsibilities will include going to sea in the North Atlantic (Summer 2027) and will use multiple techniques to determine the regional BCP, to then feed into the physical, food-web and statistical models, used by the OceanSOS team. The post-holder will also facilitate fieldwork south of South Africa (early Summer 2027) and the samples collected from this region. The tools you will use at sea include sediment traps, marine snow catchers and optodes to measure microbial remineralisation. You will be responsible for organising your component of the fieldwork so it is essential you have fieldwork experience at sea. You will also process the samples you collect to then lead and co-author peer-reviewed publications, and will work closely with the wider project team. You will have the opportunity to present findings to the research team as well as at national and/or international conferences. As this project is part of a large consortium, the you will have the opportunity, and be expected to, collaborate widely within our smaller sub-team, but also with the rest of the consortia including at annual science meetings. There will also be the opportunity to work with international partners. items.desc: Full-Time, Fixed-term appointment to 31st December 2027 We are seeking an experienced and motivated Post Doctoral Research Associate to join a multidisciplinary programme investigating the molecular basis of insecticide resistance in malaria vectors. Based within the Chemical Biology Group, Department of Vector Biology, at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine , you will lead computational analysis and integration of transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic and phenotypic data, using robust statistical and, where appropriate, interpretable machine-learning approaches. Working closely with experimental scientists, you will integrate molecular data with insecticide uptake, metabolism and functional validation studies using laboratory and field-derived Anopheles populations. Your work will support resistance monitoring, genomic surveillance and the development of next-generation vector control products. We are looking for a candidate with a background in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, biostatistics or data science, with experience analysing biological datasets and strong skills in R and/or Python. Experience in multi-omics, machine learning, malaria or vector biology would be advantageous. Key Responsibilities Will Include Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis Lead transcriptomic analysis from quality control and quantification through differential expression and functional enrichment, using appropriate comparators and accounting for population, selection history and batch effects, including assessment of data quality, enrichment, controls, missing data and false discovery. Lead analysis of quantitative and chemical/affinity-enrichment proteomics datasets Integrate transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic, insecticide uptake, metabolism and phenotypic evidence to identify and rank candidate resistance mechanisms and testable biological hypotheses. Candidate prioritisation and functional validation Develop an integrated molecular evidence framework to identify shared and compound-specific resistance mechanisms, assess potential cross-resistance and prioritise a tractable set of candidates for experimental validation. Work with experimental and analytical colleagues to design and interpret functional, biochemical and molecular validation studies, including RNAi-based approaches where appropriate. Assess evidence supporting candidate resistance markers and translate validated findings into priorities for genomic surveillance and resistance monitoring. Develop and evaluate statistical and, where appropriate, interpretable machine-learning approaches for multi-omics integration, feature selection and prediction of resistance phenotypes; use sequence analysis or structural bioinformatics where informative. Reproducibility, data management and research outputs Develop version-controlled Python/R workflows with documented quality control, statistical methods, software versions and data provenance. Contribute substantially to curated datasets, figures, peer-reviewed manuscripts, reports and presentations, with opportunities to lead outputs where appropriate; contribute analytical or methodological content to research proposals, grants and fellowship applications. Share documented code and datasets through appropriate repositories in line with open-access, data-management and confidentiality requirements. Work with collaborators and core facilities to resolve data-quality issues, support colleagues and students, and transfer reproducible workflows across the team. Ideally You Will Demonstrate PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, proteomics, systems biology, biological sciences, computer science, or a closely related discipline, with substantial computational or bioinformatics experience. Strong experience analysing high-dimensional molecular data, with substantive expertise in at least one of quantitative proteomics or transcriptomics and the ability to work across complementary molecular data types Strong programming skills in Python and/or R, with practical Linux/command-line experience and the ability to develop maintainable, version-controlled and reproducible computational workflows. Strong quantitative judgement in experimental design and analysis, including quality control, normalisation, missing data, batch effects, confounding, statistical power, differential analysis, multiple-testing correction, exploratory analysis and appropriate visualisation. Ability to critically evaluate analytical outputs, uncertainty and biological plausibility, and to communicate findings clearly to experimental scientists to inform validation studies. Clear scientific writing and presentation skills, with the ability to contribute substantially to peer-reviewed publications and research proposals, with opportunities to lead outputs where appropriate. items.desc: Job ref: NAT02237 Salary: Competitive Closing date: 31 Oct 2026 About the role You will play a key role in a multidisciplinary programme on computational proteomics in a new physical dimension, supported by UKRI and the NSF, involving Imperial College London (Physics), the University of California San Diego (Computing), as well as industrial and academic partners in Europe and the US. The programme aims to develop conceptually new de novo sequencing tools based on two-dimensional partial covariance mass spectrometry, invented and developed in the Department of Physics at Imperial College London. This role offers a unique opportunity for a physicist interested in developing transformative analytical technologies. What you would be doing This role combines computational and experimental aspects. You will design and implement advanced computational algorithms for reconstructing peptide sequences directly from experimental mass spectral data, without recourse to protein sequence databases. You will also be engaged in mass spectral data acquisition in an analytical mass spectrometry laboratory. You will work collaboratively with the Imperial College team and US project partners on the development and optimisation of de novo sequencing algorithms. You will liaise with project partners and participate in data acquisition campaigns in partner laboratories. What we are looking for You will hold a PhD in Physics (or a closely related quantitative discipline) and have an outstanding record of research achievement. We are particularly interested in candidates with exceptional computational and analytical skills, demonstrated through the development of novel algorithms, advanced data-analysis methodologies, scientific software, machine learning approaches or other computational research tools. The ideal candidate will be intellectually ambitious, highly self-motivated and excited by the prospect of working at the boundary between physics, computation and biomolecular science. Experience in proteomics or mass spectrometry is not required; candidates with strong backgrounds in computational physics, statistical physics, machine learning, signal processing, inverse problems, optimisation, applied mathematics or related fields are particularly encouraged to apply. What we can offer you The opportunity to contribute to a pioneering international research programme aimed at establishing an entirely new physical paradigm for biomolecular sequencing. You will help develop both the underlying physical methodology and the computational frameworks required to unlock information inaccessible to conventional analytical approaches, creating new capabilities with broad scientific and technological impact. Collaboration within a multidisciplinary team involving physicists, computer scientists and analytical mass spectrometrists. Involvement in publications, conference presentations and future grant applications. The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and contribute to our mission of “Science for Humanity”. Access to Imperial’s sector-leading career support for researchers, as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. A sector-leading salary and remuneration package, including 41 days’ leave per year and generous pension schemes. A diverse, inclusive and collaborative working culture, with staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information The position is available immediately. We would ideally like the successful candidate to start as soon as possible, but the start date is flexible and can be agreed to accommodate notice periods and other commitments. This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term role based at our South Kensington Campus. If you require further details about the role, please contact: Professor Vitali Averbukh – v.averbukh@imperial.ac.uk

items.title: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry
items.card: Responsibilities Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA
items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) At HAWK University of Applied Sciences and Arts Hildesheim/Holzminden/Göttingen, Faculty of Engineering and Health, Göttingen campus, the position is to be filled at the earliest possible date, for a fixed term of three years. Within the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS, novel photonic and molecular analytical methods are being developed for the high-resolution investigation of dynamic protein-DNA interactions. Femtosecond laser-based crosslinking (fliX) is combined with complementary methods in quantitative and structural proteomics (LC-MS/MS), genomics and sequencing (ChIP-Seq, nanopore sequencing), and bioinformatics for multiomics data integration and analysis to characterise protein–DNA interactions at the structural and functional levels. The aim is to make previously inaccessible dynamic molecular processes experimentally measurable and thereby establish new foundations for investigating regulatory mechanisms in biological and disease-relevant systems. A central focus is the development and physicochemical characterisation of novel irradiation and measurement approaches based on ultrashort laser pulses. Tasks & Responsibilities Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA damage Systematically investigating and optimising relevant laser and process parameters, such as wavelength, pulse duration, pulse energy, repetition rate, temporal pulse separation, and irradiation dose Characterising, validating, and standardising the optical setups and measurement methods developed, including benchmarking, reproducibility assessments, troubleshooting, and the preparation of SOPs Working closely with experts in physics, molecular biology, proteomics, sequencing, and bioinformatics; jointly interpreting results and integrating them into experimental planning Contributing to scientific publications, project communication, and, where results are eligible for intellectual property protection, invention disclosures and patent applications Qualifications A completed university degree at Master’s or Diploma level in physics, photonics, physical chemistry, or a related natural science; a completed doctorate is desirable Excellent theoretical and practical knowledge of non-linear optics and ultrashort laser pulses and extensive experience with sophisticated experimental laser setups Demonstrated experience in the independent design, alignment, characterisation, and operation of complex optical and/or spectroscopic experimental setups Experience in photochemistry, femtochemistry, time-resolved spectroscopy, or related fields is advantageous Strong analytical and independent scientific thinking, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and develop solutions to scientific and methodological challenges A strong interest in biological and biomedical research questions, together with a willingness to acquire expertise in protein‑DNA interactions and molecular analytical methods Enthusiasm for method and technology development, systematic optimisation, and experimental troubleshooting, as well as an independent, structured, and responsible working style Excellent teamwork and communication skills, together with an enthusiasm for close collaboration in an interdisciplinary team A demonstrated record of scientific publications; experience with invention disclosures, intellectual property rights, or patent applications is desirable Very good English skills for scientific communication and laboratory work and very good German skills for handling administrative matters HAWK sees itself as a place that creates opportunities. We therefore expect the successful candidate to foster an equal-opportunity and diversity-oriented working environment in interactions with colleagues and students. As a diversity-friendly university, we welcome employees with different backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from people from underrepresented groups. Our university supports the compatibility of family and career, among other things through highly flexible working-time models. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the relevant statutory provisions if they have equal aptitude, qualifications and professional performance.

items.desc:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
 The Position
 About the project: 
 The implementation of robotics and automation in industrial environments currently requires high investment, significant engineering effort, and extensive setup times. Consequently, automation is often only economically viable for processes characterized by high repetition, low uniformity, low variance, or strict requirements for product and personal protection.
 This PhD project aims to drastically reduce the implementation effort and associated costs of robotic systems. By lowering these barriers, automation can become viable for flexible, low-volume, and high-variance production environments. The core focus of this research is the utilization of Physical AI for fast, intuitive, and efficient training and adaptation of robots. The project will evaluate key factors required to achieve effortless implementation while simultaneously ensuring high process robustness and safety.
 Degree: Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Robotics, Computer Science, Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Physics, or a closely related field.
 Your tasks and responsibilities: 
 Physical AI & Machine Learning: 
 Solid understanding of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) architectures
 Familiarity with concepts like Reinforcement Learning (RL) , Imitation Learning (Learning from Demonstration), or Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) 
 Experience applying AI to physical systems or hardware
 Robotics & Automation: 
 Strong foundation in robot kinematics, dynamics, and control
 Experience with robotic frameworks, primarily ROS / ROS2 (Robot Operating System)
 Software Engineering: 
 Advanced programming skills in Python and/or C++ .Experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.Familiarity with simulation environments (e.g., Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Gazebo)
 Domain Knowledge & Soft Skills
 Industrial Application: Basic understanding of production environments, ideally regarding process safety, robustness, or flexible manufacturing (low-volume, high-variance)
 Regulated Environments: Interest in or prior exposure to strict production standards (like cleanrooms or pharmaceutical/diagnostic constraints) is a strong plus
 Analytical Mindset: Ability to bridge abstract AI theory with practical, real-world robotic deployment
 Communication & Collaboration: Strong team player capable of working in interdisciplinary teams and presenting research at international conferences
 Your Advantages: 
 3,750 € salary per month for a full-time 
 The possibility of accommodation in the Roche Boarding House or convenient transport connections to Munich with the Roche Shuttle
 Your Application: 
 Please upload your Curriculum vitae specific to this position. 
 Start: As of January 2027 or according to the agreement for a period of 3 years. 
 We are excited to see your application! 
 Your contact to us! With people. For people.
 Do you need further support?
 Please have a look at our FAQs, you will find them via https://careers.roche.com/global/en/faq .
 Who we are
 A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.
 Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

 As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will implement the infrastructure that unlocks our scientific data and accelerates the discovery of life-changing treatments. You will work at the intersection of computational engineering and biology, partnering with scientists, ML experts, and DevOps engineers to put powerful AI tools directly into the hands of those driving drug discovery.

 You build tools to evaluate AI/ML model performance and establish new ways to understand and measure AI quality. 
 You partner with product managers and scientists to understand user needs, shape requirements, and translate them into actionable technical specifications. 
 You develop and maintain data systems for collecting, structuring, and storing diverse scientific data that power advanced analytics, machine learning, and other data-driven initiatives. 
 You implement, adopt, and evaluate new AI/ML algorithms and analytical techniques. 
 You own features end to end from initial model evaluation through to production deployment, within a team that prizes technical rigor and mentorship. 
 You shape how we build contributing to architectural decisions, code reviews, and the evolution of our development processes. 
 You span the stack and contribute where needed, staying curious about emerging technologies and industry best practices. 
 Who you are: 
 You bring technical rigor with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Computer Science or a related technical field, and proven experience in machine learning engineering. You treat testing, clean code, and documentation as the foundation for scalable, high-impact systems. 
 You span the stack working across the ML lifecycle — from GPU optimization and model performance to backend systems and cloud-native architecture (e.g. Kubernetes, AWS) — with a solid grounding in statistics, ML theory, and modern AI/ML frameworks and tools. 
 You value collaborative engineering , seeing code reviews and architectural decisions as spaces for shared growth, and translating complex technical challenges into shared goals with partners from research scientists to DevOps engineers. 
 You are a continuous learner approaching new frameworks and languages with curiosity, as comfortable mentoring others as learning from them. 
 You are an excellent communicator translating technical complexity into clear, actionable insights with empathy and precision, so every stakeholder feels aligned and heard. 
 Preferred: 
 Experience with biological data (ideally multimodal) and scientific processes. 
 Experience working with scientists or in a research environment. 
 Experience with workflow automation, GenAI, and/or agents.

items.desc:
Lieu : Limours, France 
 Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance 
 Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. ​
 Nos engagements, vos avantages 
 Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée
 Un package de rémunération attractif
 Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes
 Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs
 Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu
 Votre quotidien 
Situé à 20mn du Pôle technologique de Paris-Saclay, le site est l’un des plus grands centres d’excellence radars de surface. Nous contribuons à développer, concevoir, intégrer et tester des radars de surveillance aériennes dédiés à la détection et l’identification de cibles. 
 En tant qu' Ingénieur Systèmes - Algorithmie et IA Radar chez Thales, vous serez impliqué(e) dans un environnement très dynamique dans le cadre du développement des radars Ground Maste r, des projets complexes à haute valeur technique au sein d'une équipe motivée et accueillante.
 Techniquement, vous devrez contribuer à l'analyse fonctionnelle détaillée du système Radar notamment en tenant compte des besoins client et des autres parties prenantes. De plus, vous devrez démontrer votre capacité à communiquer dans ce type de contexte (diplomatie, capacité à convaincre, management sans lien hiérarchique, etc.).
 Mais dans un premier temps, vous participerez à la cellule innovation de nos radars, au sein d'une équipe dédiée et dynamique, vous partagerez les idées d'innovations avec l'appui de nos experts. Au titre de l'innovation vous serez co-localisé(e) pour permettre le développement de solution permettant d'améliorer les performances de nos radars. 
 Puis au titre de votre rôle d'ingénieur système dans le cadre d'un développement plus classique vous serez en charge, en phase de spécification, des aspects suivants :
 Définir les caractéristiques fonctionnelles du radar (bilan énergétique, séquencements, définition algorithmique de traitement en particulier à base d'IA) répondant aux exigences de performances opérationnelles souhaitées,
 Réaliser des analyses et des évaluations en support de la justification de la conception, au moyen de calculs analytiques ou de simulations au moyen de modèles du comportement fonctionnel,
 Proposer des évolutions du système en prototypant les traitements algorithmiques notamment à base d'intelligence artificielle qui font leur apparition dans les chaînes de traitement radar,
 Produire la malle documentaire idoine de spécifications système et sous-systèmes permettant l'implémentation par les métiers.
 En phase de validation du système vous devrez :
 Apporter votre expertise aux équipes d'intégration en identifiant et résolvant les problèmes remontés par celles-ci,
 Réaliser des analyses fonctionnelles sur des données radar simulées ou enregistrées suite à des essais terrain (éventuellement par la ré-exécution informatique des algorithmes de traitement), en développant au besoin vos propres outils d'analyse
 Valider les algorithmes et évaluer les performances face à divers scénarios de test,
 Être un support aux projets, lors de présentations clients, revues, démonstrations.
 Plus globalement, en nous rejoignant, vous participerez à favoriser l'émergence de modèles, algorithmes et éléments de simulation standardisés et réutilisables au sein de la discipline.
 Votre Profil : 
 De formation supérieure BAC +5, type école d'ingénierie ou équivalent universitaire, vous justifiez d'une expérience confirmée d’une dizaine d’années dans le domaine de l'ingénierie des systèmes complexes , de préférence dans le monde du radar. Vous avez acquis de solides compétences en traitement du signal, probabilité, modèles mathématiques et en algorithmie ainsi que des connaissances en électronique et logiciel. Vous justifiez de plus d’une expérience réussie en algorithmie à base d'intelligence artificielle .
 Pour assurez votre réussite en mission, vous disposez de ces compétences spécifiques :
 Traitement du signal et traitement de données , couplés en particulier avec de l’expérience en Machine et Deep Learning .
 Bonnes pratiques de développement, en particulier dans l'utilisation de Git et de Gitlab ou Github est attendu.
 Développement en Python avec un niveau avancé attendu , dont connaissance des librairies/frameworks utilisés en IA (PyTorch, Numpy, Pandas, …

Job Description: 
 Zur Verstärkung der Abteilung "Operationelle Analyse und Studien" suchen wir bei Airbus Defence and Space in Friedrichshafen in den nächsten Monaten eine/n
 Software Entwickler:in Simulation: Gen AI (d/f/m) 
 Diese Stelle ist auch mit reduzierter Wochenarbeitszeit und angepasstem Aufgabenbereich möglich. 
 Wir entwickeln militärische Simulationsumgebungen für Studien und Forschungsprojekte, welche für Analysen und zum KI-Training verwendet werden. Mittels Machine Learning/Deep Learning Ansätzen entwickeln wir KI-Verfahren zur autonomen Planung und Entscheidungsfindung unter unsicheren Bedingungen und in komplexen operationellen, militärischen Situationen.
 Wir implementieren und erproben modernste Deep Reinforcement-Learning Ansätze für die Nutzung im militärischen Umfeld, mit denen sich unsere KI-Anwendungen sicher, datensparsam und zuverlässig optimieren lassen. Die wegweisenden Ergebnisse publizieren wir auf internationalen Konferenzen (z.B. Using DeepMind's AlphaStar techniques to support military decision-makers ).
 Wir suchen einen Software Entwickler (d/f/m), der uns bei der Übertragung der Ergebnisse der akademischen Forschung auf reale Systeme unterstützt. Du arbeitest in unserer agilen Studienabteilung an interessanten Studien- und Forschungsprojekten der Bundeswehr, NATO, sowie Europäischen Union im Bereich Sicherheit und Verteidigung.
 Respekt, Teamwork und Kreativität sind die Schlüsselwerte unserer Abteilung. Als Studienabteilung sind wir auch in Innovationsaktivitäten im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz involviert. Zusammen mit der Airbus Innovation Factory in Friedrichshafen findest du bei uns das richtige Umfeld, um deine innovativen Ideen voranzutreiben und in die Realität umzusetzen. 
 Dein Standort 
 Am Airbus-Standort in Immenstaad am Bodensee arbeitest du dort, wo die Zukunft von Connected Intelligence, Space und Air Power entsteht. In einer Umgebung, die Weitblick bietet, gestaltest du technologische Innovationen über Domänen hinweg. 
 Unser Standort lebt vom Dialog: Auf dem Campus triffst du auf ein einzigartiges Netzwerk aus Experten für Satellitentechnik, militärische Luftfahrt, Cyber-Security, Künstliche Intelligenz sowie Combat Cloud und Ground Support von morgen. Auch unsere Zusammenarbeit ist geprägt von Dynamik – in agilen Teams widmen wir uns den komplexesten Fragestellungen, von KI-gestützter Erdbeobachtung bis zur sicheren Cloud-Architektur. Wer technologische Exzellenz und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit sucht, findet hier das ideale Umfeld.

items.desc:
ABOUT BLACK FOREST LABS

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX — foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and videos. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.




WHY THIS ROLE

Frontier image and video models are now good enough that the hard question is no longer whether they work, but whether a new one is actually better, and how you'd know. Aesthetics, prompt following, editing fidelity, text rendering, character consistency: none of these collapse into a single number, and public benchmarks have fallen well behind the models they're meant to measure.

You'll work on the system BFL uses to answer that question. Every FLUX checkpoint, every finetuning and RL run, and every competitor release goes through our evaluation stack, and you'll help build and sharpen it. Product Research relies on what it shows to decide what to fix next, and to confirm the fix worked.

It gets harder from here. FLUX 3 is our first multimodal model, spanning image, video, audio and action, and each new modality needs its own way of being measured.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

What you focus on will depend on where you're strongest and what the team needs most when you join.

In scope:

 - Building and maintaining the evaluation stack that every model checkpoint has to pass through and prove itself on, from automated benchmarking and LLM-as-judge pipelines, to human evaluation through panels (Prolific and otherwise).

 - Designing the breadth of evaluation across the taxonomy, from prompt adherence, editing fidelity, aesthetics, text rendering, subject and character consistency, to safety.

 - Evaluating the evaluation stack itself: checking that human and automated evals agree, that results stay stable over time, and improving them when they don't.

 - Benchmarking FLUX against the frontier models continuously, while obtaining a meaningful perspective on where we are better or worse than competitors and what such differences really mean.

 - Finding the ways in which the quality of the model's output falls short that are not captured by aggregate numbers.

 - Closing the loop, ideally, with the RL and finetuning researchers, by defining target metrics for them to aim for, and verifying that a new checkpoint improved the weakness without introducing new ones.

 - Designing how best to exploit the signals we already capture through the API and MCP, and what new signals we should capture, with help from research, data engineering and legal.

 - Maintaining the usefulness of existing metrics as their natural lifecycle brings up concerns of gaming and overfitting, and anticipating this for new metrics.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have made meaningful contributions to the evaluation of generative models already. You understand that a benchmark figure without careful consideration of sample size and judge agreement with humans is at best uninformed optimism and at worst dangerously misleading, and you have been the person that found that inconvenient regression that nobody wanted to talk about.

You likely have:

 - Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a relevant field or demonstrated equivalent practical experience

 - Practical experience with evaluating generative models, in a hands-on way. You may have worked with diffusion or flow-matching based image or video models already, but the capability to evaluate them in earnest transfers to other modalities too

 - Very strong Python and software engineering skills, with pipelines that run reliably and that other people can read if needed

 - Working knowledge of PyTorch and modern ML infrastructure and practices; you are not a pure Python developer, you know what the modern ML code looks like

items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle L’Inria est l’Institut national de recherche en sciences du numérique, dont le centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur fait partie. Avec une forte expertise en informatique et mathématiques appliquées, les projets de recherche du centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur touchent toutes les dimensions des sciences et technologies du numérique, et génèrent de l’innovation. Implanté principalement à Sophia Antipolis, mais également à Nice ou Montpellier, il regroupe 47 équipes de recherche et neuf services d’appui. Il est présent dans les domaines de l’intelligence artificielle, la science des données, la sécurité des systèmes informatiques, la robotique, l’ingénierie de réseaux, la prévention des risques naturels, la transition écologique, la biologie numérique, les neurosciences computationnelles, les données de santé… Le Centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur est un acteur majeur en termes d'excellence scientifique par les résultats obtenus et les collaborations tant au niveau européen qu'international. Contexte et atouts du poste Cette thèse s'inscrit dans le cadre du PEPR DynaBiod, qui vise à faire progresser la compréhension et la modélisation des dynamiques de la biodiversité, notamment en mobilisant les avancées récentes de l'intelligence artificielle et de la modélisation mathématique. Le projet sera mené à Montpellier, dans un environnement de recherche interdisciplinaire associant Inria et des équipes spécialisées en intelligence artificielle, écologie quantitative et modélisation des systèmes dynamiques. Il bénéficiera de la complémentarité des compétences des encadrants, ainsi que de l'écosystème scientifique développé autour de Pl@ntNet et de l'IA pour la biodiversité. Le doctorant ou la doctorante contribuera à un programme de recherche ambitieux, à l'interface entre apprentissage profond, modélisation mécaniste et écologie. Le poste offre l'opportunité de développer des méthodes originales, notamment autour des Process-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), et de les confronter à des données écologiques réelles, dans un contexte de collaborations interdisciplinaires. Mission confiée L'objectif de cette thèse est de développer de nouvelles approches d'intelligence artificielle permettant de mieux comprendre et prédire la dynamique spatio-temporelle des communautés végétales. Les travaux exploreront notamment le potentiel des Process-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) pour combiner apprentissage à partir de données et connaissances issues de l'écologie théorique. L'ambition est de dépasser les limites des approches purement corrélatives en intégrant des contraintes et des processus écologiques dans les modèles d'apprentissage. Un enjeu central sera d'identifier les formulations mathématiques et les architectures d'apprentissage les plus adaptées à la dynamique des communautés végétales, puis d'étudier leur capacité à inférer des processus et paramètres écologiques à partir d'observations spatiales et temporelles incomplètes, hétérogènes et bruitées. Principales activités Étudier l'état de l'art en modélisation dynamique des systèmes écologiques, en Scientific Machine Learning et en PINNs. Explorer différentes formulations mathématiques des dynamiques écologiques et leur intégration dans des architectures d'apprentissage profond. Concevoir et développer des approches fondées sur les PINNs et, si pertinent, d'autres méthodes hybrides combinant modèles mécanistes et apprentissage automatique. Étudier l'inférence de paramètres écologiques et la reconstruction de dynamiques spatio-temporelles à partir d'observations partielles. Développer des outils de simulation et d'évaluation sur des données synthétiques et réelles (inventaires de végétation, données environnementales, télédétection). Évaluer la robustesse, la généralisation et la pertinence écologique des modèles proposés. Publier les résultats dans des conférences et revues scientifiques internationales et contribuer à leur diffusion en logiciel libre. Compétences Formation : Master 2 ou diplôme d'ingénieur en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées ou discipline équivalente. Compétences attendues : Bonnes connaissances en apprentissage automatique, optimisation numérique et/ou modélisation mathématique. Solides compétences en programmation scientifique (Python). Capacité à concevoir et évaluer des méthodes numériques. Autonomie, rigueur scientifique et goût pour la recherche. Bonne maîtrise de l'anglais scientifique. Compétences appréciées : Connaissances en écologie quantitative, données spatiales ou télédétection. Expérience en apprentissage profond (PyTorch, JAX ou équivalent). Connaissances en équations différentielles, systèmes dynamiques ou PINNs. Expérience en simulation numérique et en inférence de paramètres. items.desc: 13.10.2026 Data Scientist (m/f/d, E13 TV-L, 100%) Cluster of Excellence HUMAN ORIGINS Bewerbungsfrist : 15.11.2026 The Cluster of Excellence HUMAN ORIGINS invites applications for a Data Scientist (m/f/d, E13 TV-L, 100%) to join the Cluster’s Research Data Management Unit. The position is expected to start on January 1st, 2027, and is limited until the end of the current Cluster funding period (December 31st, 2032). In the HUMAN ORIGINS Cluster of Excellence more than two dozen PIs and their teams engage in interdisciplinary research into the last five million years of human history, combining scientific, archaeological and humanities approaches. The Cluster’s Research Data Management Unit is responsible for research data and research software management, as well as research infrastructure and instrumentation. The unit is jointly led by the Quantitative Biology Center (QBiC) and the Digital Humanties Center (DHC), two of the University’s Core Facilities for research data management. The position is expected to complement the unit’s data stewards with a strong data science expertise and experience and will be jointly supervised by QBiC and DHC. Duties and responsibilities will include: Building, testing, and deploying custom research software, web applications, and interactive dashboards/portals to facilitate cluster-wide data exploration, integration, and visualization. Developing and applying state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, machine learning, or NLP solutions to extract patterns, classify artifacts/data, and support hypotheses in and across human origins research projects. Designing, implementing, and maintaining scalable analytical pipelines and workflows for heterogeneous, multimodal datasets (e.g., 3D scans, ancient genomics, archaeological spatial data, and text corpora). Developing interfaces between the research infrastructure of QBiC and DHC to ensure interoperability of computational environments and tools. Partnering closely with the Cluster’s PIs and research teams to translate complex research questions into robust computational methods and contribute to scientific publications. Establishing and applying best practices for Research Software Engineering, including version control, containerization, automated testing, and open-science compliance in close coordination with the unit’s data stewards. Expected applicant profile: Completed university degree (Master’s or equivalent), preferably with a doctorate, in computer science, data science, or a related field. A background or experience in the humanities is a plus. Experience in applying data science methods and tools in research projects, preferably in one or more of the disciplines relevant to the Cluster. Strong software development and web engineering skills. Experience in developing and applying artificial intelligence solutions in data science and software engineering. Openness to interdisciplinary data science and management covering a broad range of research domains, data modalities, methodologies, software and tools. Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work autonomously in an international and interdisciplinary environment. Very good English language skills, written and spoken. The Cluster and the University of Tübingen offer excellent opportunities for cutting-edge collaborative, interdisciplinary research, state-of-the-art laboratories, and access to a wide range of facilities. The position can be split. The University aims to increase the proportion of women in research and teaching and therefore particularly encourages qualified women scientists to apply. The University of Tübingen is committed to equal opportunities and diversity and actively promotes gender equality. Female candidates are expressly invited to submit their application. Disabled candidates will be given preference over other equally qualified applicants. Applications should be submitted electronically no later than November 15, 2026. They should include: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) certificates / diplomas / references. Please submit your application as a single PDF file (max. 10 MB) to admin.human-originsspam prevention@ifu.uni-tuebingen.de For any further questions regarding this job posting please contact human-originsspam prevention@dh-center.uni-tuebingen.de The appointment will be made by the Central Administration (Zentrale Verwaltung).

items.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About the role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key responsibilities: Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. Skills & Qualifications: Basic eligibility for doctoral studies: a degree at advanced level, or completed course requirements of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad, Specific eligibility: at least 90 credits in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or closely related subjects, Good command of English, spoken and written. Swedish is an advantage, Experience in machine learning, data analysis or industrial applications of AI is an advantage, but not a requirement, Comfortable working in an international company and in a cross-functional context. Who Are You: You are curious, driven and goal-oriented, with a strong interest in turning research into practical value. You like to ask the deeper question rather than settle for the first answer, and you are comfortable moving between the data, the shop floor and the clinic. You create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas, challenge assumptions and learn together. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively with others and take ownership of your work. You share our belief in respect for people and continuous improvement. What we offer: A rare opportunity for both technical and personal development: doctoral education at Mid Sweden University combined with work on real industrial and product data at one of Permobil’s most modern sites. You get close support from supervisors at both the university and Permobil, and the chance to see your research put to use in a company with a clear purpose and a strong belief in the future. Application Process We will conduct selection continuously so send us your application today or before 20th of November at the latest! The position is based in Sundsvall, with a project period of four years. Permobil is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals. For more information about the position, please contact Mikael Boija, Senior Director Operational Excellence, mikael.boija@permobil.com For information about the recruitment process, please contact Zivile Mitkute, Talent Acquisition Partner, zivile.mitkute@permobil.com Please respect that …

items.desc: Teaching and Research Fellow in Aircraft Structural Design Organisation Cranfield University Faculty or Department Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences Based at Cranfield Campus, Cranfield, Bedfordshire Hours of work 37 hours per week, normally worked Monday to Friday. Flexible working will be considered. Contract type Permanent Salary Full time starting salary is normally in the range of £38,655 to £46,492 per annum with potential progression to £53,108 per annum Posted Date 11/10/2026 Apply by 08/11/2026 Role Description We have an exciting opportunity for a talented and ambitious individual with industry or academic experience to join our Aircraft Structures team, conducting teaching and research into novel aircraft configurations ranging from zero emissions hydrogen propulsion through to supersonic transport and eVTOL. About the Role We are seeking a talented and ambitious individual to join our team. Working with senior members of the team, the position will be mainly responsible for the development and delivery of high-quality teaching at postgraduate level in various topics related to aircraft structures analysis and design, for academic course management, for postgraduate student research and design project supervision, as well as for engaging with the delivery of industrially sponsored projects. Some of your time will also be spent preparing research proposals and delivering research contracts and consultancy, as well as developing activities that complement and enhance existing research and teaching within the Aerospace and Aviation Theme. You will be supported to establish and grow your research portfolio and publications. About You You will be passionate about aerospace and the contribution and value of your specialised topic within this field. The impacts of the aerospace industry and air travel will be important to you, and playing your role in driving progress towards zero emissions aviation will be a personal priority. Your ideal working environment will be collaborative and open to new learning and experience, with personal satisfaction taken in supporting others to grow their knowledge and skills through our teaching activities. Professionally, you will be curious and creative, looking for new solutions and applying thinking from outside the traditional aerospace sector. You may be an academic, looking for a more postgraduate teaching-focused opportunity; you may be an industry professional looking for new challenges and a refreshing new professional environment. All are welcomed within a friendly, supportive, ambitious and energetic team environment. This specific opportunity is ideally suited, but not limited to, experienced industrial airframe design and analysis engineers, who wish to pursue a career in the academic sector. To be considered for this opportunity, you should have significant aeronautical structural analysis and design skills, ideally accumulated in an industrial setting. Your knowledge should span across any combination of the following subjects: airworthiness requirements knowledge and application; metallic and/or composite airframe structures analysis and design; fatigue and damage tolerance; computer aided design (3DEXPERIENCE, CATIA); finite element analysis (ABAQUS, NASTRAN / PATRAN / other); structural stability; aeroelasticity; or structural dynamics. Individuals with an industrial/academic background, having spent significant time in a relevant industrial airframe design and analysis post, will be considered. Further information about this position can be found in the job description. About Us As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield’s world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here. The Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences (FEAS) is a leading provider of postgraduate level engineering education, research and technology support to individuals and organisations. As part of the faculty, the aerospace theme translates specialist research in aircraft design, propulsion, aerodynamics and autonomous systems into practical aerospace solutions through strong industry partnerships. items.card: About the role Are you an ambitious bioinformatician looking to apply cutting-edge computational biology to one of the most exciting challenges in global health? As a Bioinformatics Research Associate in this specially created position by Imperial College to support the success of the £7.5 million ARIA-funded M2M (Mechanism to Medicine) programme, you will play a central role in helping to uncover the innate immune
items.desc: Job number MED06012 Faculties Faculty of Medicine Departments National Heart & Lung Institute Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Hammersmith Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 10 Nov 2026 About the role Are you an ambitious bioinformatician looking to apply cutting-edge computational biology to one of the most exciting challenges in global health? As a Bioinformatics Research Associate in this specially created position by Imperial College to support the success of the £7.5 million ARIA-funded M2M (Mechanism to Medicine) programme, you will play a central role in helping to uncover the innate immune mechanisms that protect individuals from respiratory viral infections and accelerate the development of a new generation of preventative medicines. Working alongside Professor Ajit Lalvani and a multidisciplinary consortium of leading academic and industry partners (including Prof Marko Nikolic at UCL, Dr Adrian Grzybowski at AnuBio inc., and Dr Sarah Teichman at University of Cambridge among others), you will integrate and analyse complex multi-omics datasets, generate novel biological insights, and directly support AI-driven approaches to therapeutic discovery. What you would be doing Lead the harmonisation, integration and analysis of large-scale multi-omics datasets, including single-cell transcriptomics, epigenomics and proteomics data. Develop, maintain and document robust computational pipelines for processing and quality control of next-generation sequencing and proteomics datasets. Identify innate immune correlates of protection through advanced bioinformatics analyses across clinical and laboratory-derived datasets. Work closely with AI and mathematical modelling teams to ensure bioinformatics outputs support downstream predictive modelling and therapeutic development. Collaborate with researchers across Imperial, UCL, industry partners and international collaborators to deliver key project milestones. Present findings to collaborators, funding bodies and at scientific conferences, while contributing to high-impact publications and future grant applications. Support implementation of FAIR data principles and open science practices across the programme What we are looking for We are looking for a highly motivated and collaborative scientist with: A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, genetics, statistics or a closely related discipline (or equivalent experience). Candidates who have not yet been officially awarded their PhD will be appointed as a Research Assistant within the salary range £45,399 - £48,876 per annum. Strong programming skills in Python, R, Bash and/or Perl and experience working in Unix/Linux environments. Hands-on experience analysing genomics and multi-omics datasets, including scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, bulk RNA-seq and proteomics data. Experience developing reproducible computational workflows using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake or equivalent workflow management systems. Experience working with HPC or cloud computing infrastructure and modern reproducible research practices. Excellent analytical, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. A passion for translating complex biological data into impactful scientific discoveries. What we can offer you The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. As a member of research staff, you have 10 development days to use to develop your skills and explore your career prospects Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. The opportunity to work on a pioneering £7.5 million ARIA-funded programme with the potential to transform protection against respiratory viral diseases. A unique position at the interface of bioinformatics, immunology, artificial intelligence and translational medicine. Collaboration with leading researchers and partners from Imperial College London, UCL, industry and international institutions. Genuine opportunities to contribute to high-impact publications, establish scientific independence and support future funding applications. Further information This is a full-time post (35 hours per week), fixed-term (48 months). If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Sofia Koletsi s.koletsi@imperial.ac.uk Available documents Attached documents are available under links. items.desc: Reference: OCT20262921 Expiry date: 17:59, Tue, 10th Nov 2026 Location: Liverpool Salary: £40,704.00 - £46,970.00 Per Annum Benefits: 30 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, plus Christmas closure days Duration: Fixed-term appointment to 13th April 2028 Fixed-term appointment to 13th April 2028 The Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine is seeking an experienced Post Doctoral Research Associate to support a multidisciplinary research programme investigating insecticide-treated materials and chemically functionalised surfaces. The postholder will lead surface and fibre characterisation using Cryo-SEM/EDS and Raman microscopy, complemented by LC-MS/MS, GC-MS and MALDI imaging. The role will investigate surface morphology, active-ingredient loading, distribution, retention, physical form and degradation through controlled sample preparation, washing and ageing studies. The successful candidate will integrate multimodal analytical data to support assessment of product performance, quality and regulatory readiness. The role will also involve developing reproducible analytical methods, SOPs and method-transfer protocols, alongside clear and robust scientific reporting. Applicants should have relevant laboratory experience in analytical chemistry, materials science, chemistry or a related discipline, with relevant specialist training in electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. Key responsibilities will include: Surface chemistry, fibre morphology and phase characterisation Develop and apply Cryo-SEM/EDS workflows to characterise fibre and yarn morphology, surface deposits, active-ingredient presentation and elemental signatures in untreated, washed and aged materials. Apply Raman confocal microscopy to identify crystalline, polymorphic and amorphous forms and generate spatial chemical maps across material surfaces; correlate Raman and microscopy findings where informative. Develop and optimise sample-preparation workflows for fibres, polymers and coatings, including sectioning, punch sampling, washing and ageing protocols, with appropriate controls and longitudinal sample tracking. Quantitative chemical profiling and multimodal integration Develop and apply quantitative LC-MS/MS and, where appropriate, GC-MS workflows to measure active-ingredient loading and retention and to characterise degradation products, impurities and formulation components. Integrate Cryo-SEM/EDS and Raman outputs with LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, MALDI imaging and other complementary measurements generated with collaborating facilities to resolve surface-to-core distribution and chemical change. Interpret relationships between active-ingredient loading, distribution, physical phase, ageing and degradation, and relate the resulting analytical evidence to material and product performance. Work closely with LSTM, IVCC and Materials Innovation Factory scientists to plan platform use, troubleshoot analytical challenges, review data quality and deliver integrated analytical packages against agreed milestones. Reproducibility, data integrity and research outputs Plan experimental work against agreed milestones, maintaining complete and traceable records of sample history, methods, imaging and spectroscopy metadata, raw and processed data, and analytical decisions. Develop SOPs, acceptance criteria, QC method, method-transfer documentation and reproducible workflows for surface, spectroscopy and complementary analytical platforms, consistent with research integrity requirements. Prepare integrated datasets, project reports, presentations and peer-reviewed manuscripts, clearly reporting data quality, analytical limitations and technical risks to the PI, collaborators and funders. Contribute to training, knowledge transfer and method transfer across LSTM and collaborating facilities, and support the development of new analytical approaches, research proposals and grant applications where appropriate. Ideally you will demonstrate: PhD in analytical chemistry, materials chemistry, surface science, physical chemistry, chemical biology or a closely related discipline. Relevant specialist training in electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, materials analysis or analytical quality systems. Substantial hands-on experience in surface or materials characterisation using SEM/EDS, Raman spectroscopy or a closely related high-resolution microscopy or spectroscopy platform, with the ability to interpret morphological, elemental or chemical-mapping data Strong knowledge of analytical and materials chemistry, including molecular interactions, surface phenomena, phase or polymorph behaviour and the chemistry of polymers, fibres, coatings or other solid materials. Experience developing or optimising sample-preparation workflows for solid materials, including sectioning, surface sampling, extraction, washing, ageing or related controlled-treatment procedures. items.desc: As a Senior Machine Learning Platform Engineer (m/f/d), you will design and build the platform that turns large-scale UxV and sensor data into validated, reproducible machine learning models. You will own and improve the end-to-end ML lifecycle—from data processing, selection, and annotation through distributed model training, experiment tracking and validation. Your work will enable ML engineers to develop autonomy and perception capabilities efficiently, reliably, and at scale. Beyond conventional platform engineering, you will also apply modern AI models to our internal data workflows. This may include semantic dataset search, automated metadata generation, data curation, and auto-labeling using foundation and multimodal models. By creating the foundations on which our AI teams build and validate models, you will directly contribute to Quantum Systems’ next generation of autonomous UxV solutions. What is your Day to Day Mission: Design, implement, and operate scalable ML and data pipelines covering ingestion, dataset creation, training, and model validation. Build a reliable ML platform for reproducible experimentation and training across local, on-premises, and cloud GPU infrastructure. Develop efficient systems for large-scale multimodal datasets, including imagery, LiDAR, odometry, ground truth, and simulation data. Establish dataset and model versioning, metadata management, quality checks, and traceability from raw sensor data to validated model artifacts. Build and optimize distributed training workflows, job scheduling, GPU resource allocation, caching, and high-throughput data access. Develop AI-powered tools for internal data engineering, including semantic data search, metadata enrichment, automatic annotation, and quality assessment using foundation or multimodal models. Improve platform reliability, observability, security, cost efficiency, and developer experience. Collaborate with ML, data, and engineering teams to translate their technical needs into scalable platform capabilities. Mentor engineers, contribute to architectural decisions, and establish engineering standards for production-grade ML systems. What you bring to the team: You hold a degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Engineering, or a related technical discipline. You have strong software engineering skills in Python and experience building reliable, maintainable software and automated workflows for data-intensive machine learning systems. You have several years of hands-on experience building production ML platforms, MLOps systems, or large-scale data and training pipelines. Solid knowledge of machine learning fundamentals and hands-on experience training and evaluating ML models. You have a deep understanding of the ML lifecycle, including dataset preparation, distributed training, experiment management, model validation, and reproducibility. You have experience with cloud platforms and containerized infrastructure using Docker and Kubernetes. You have worked with workflow orchestration, experiment tracking, and model or artifact management technologies such as Argo Workflows, Kubeflow, Metaflow, Airflow, MLflow, or comparable solutions. You have practical experience with large datasets, object and shared storage, data formats, partitioning or sharding strategies, and high-throughput data loading. You are familiar with CI/CD, infrastructure as code, monitoring, logging, access control, and operating reliable production systems. You communicate confidently in English and collaborate effectively across research, product, and infrastructure teams. You are highly self-motivated and take technical ownership from architecture through operation. Why Quantum-Systems: We believe in the power of combined efforts: straightforward tech expertise paired with a customer-centric focus. We are industry pioneers who are ambitious, bold, and visionary. We push limits, think outside-the-box and strive for technological excellence to shape the future of aerial data. We promise to be your runway for individual and professional growth. Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance.
