items.desc: Research at the Department of Molecular Biosciences, The Wenner-Gren Institute (MBW) experimentally addresses fundamental problems in molecular cell biology, integrative biology, and infection and immunobiology. State-of-the art and advanced methodologies are applied in a professional research environment characterized by its well-established international profile. The institute has 30 research groups with a research staff of 180, of which 65 are PhD students. More information about us, please visit www.su.se/mbw. Project description This PhD student position is available in the Martin Jastroch laboratory. The project addresses molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial bioenergetics, combining molecular simulations and systems levels-models with biochemical, physiological, and metabolic data. The project will be conducted in collaboration with the Ville Kaila (DBB) and Ilaria Piazza (MBW) labs, as well as with other members of the newly founded Strategic Research Center (SFO) on “Modelling Life at the Membrane with AI” (https://cemerai.se) to integrate data across scales within our interdisciplinary collaborative research center. Central publications from previous projects linked to the current PhD project: Divakaruni and Jastroch (2022) Nature Metab .; 4(8):978-994. Keipert et al. (2024) Science ; 384(6700):1111-1117. Pöverlein MC et al. (2026) eLife .;13:RP102104. Beghiah A, et al. (2026) Nature Comms ;17(1):5737. Badolato S et al. (2026) JACS 148(20):21056-21068. Beghiah A et al (2026) PNAS , 123(16):e2534025123. Beghiah A et al. (2024) Nature Comms ;15(1):9098. D. Riepl et al. (2024) Nature Comms 15(1), 5276. Mateus, A. et al. (2021). Mol Sys Biol 17(7). Qualification requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be met by the deadline for applications. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. Specific entry requirements are described in the general syllabus for doctoral studies in the field. The applicants should have prior training in computational/biochemical/biophysical methods applied to mitochondrial proteins and biological membranes. These skills should be described in the Research/Project Proposal. Selection The selection among the eligible candidates will be based on their capacity to benefit from the training. The following criteria will be used to assess this capacity: Documented knowledge in a relevant field of research Capacity for analytical and creative thinking Initiative Independence Ability to collaborate Written and oral proficiency in both Swedish and English. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About the employment We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Recent graduate or up to 1 year of experience . Basic understanding of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning concepts. Good knowledge of programming fundamentals. Basic proficiency in Python. Understanding of mathematics and statistics relevant to machine learning. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and teamwork abilities. Eagerness to learn emerging AI technologies. Preferred Skills Familiarity with Python , NumPy, Pandas, and Scikit-learn. Basic understanding of supervised and unsupervised learning. The successful candidate will work across statistical modelling, machine learning, data engineering and analytical problem-solving. You will contribute to the development of predictive models, classification solutions and scalable data pipelines. The role offers the opportunity to work closely with product, engineering and customer-facing teams while helping turn large and complex datasets into practical insights and reliable technical solutions. Key Responsibilities Investigate open-ended data problems, define an appropriate approach and independently develop solutions through testing and iteration. Design, develop and maintain machine learning models and production-grade data pipelines. Prepare, clean and structure large, complex and sometimes unstructured datasets for analysis and modelling. Develop and improve predictive, classification and entity-resolution models. Measure model performance against real-world outcomes and refine solutions using data-led feedback. Work with product, engineering and business stakeholders to translate commercial or methodological questions into clear technical solutions. Provide understandable explanations of areas such as model performance, bias, data confidence and coverage limitations. Use Python, machine learning libraries, databases and querying tools across the full development lifecycle. Explore new technologies and AI-assisted workflows that can improve delivery speed and quality. Maintain clear documentation covering methodologies, code, models and data structures. Experience and skills Approximately three to five years of experience in applied data science, machine learning or a closely related technical role. Strong Python development skills, with experience using libraries such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, TensorFlow or PyTorch. Good understanding of database design, data schemas, efficient querying and reliable pipeline development. Practical experience deploying machine learning models into production and monitoring their ongoing performance. Ability to work across data preparation, modelling, engineering and production implementation. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions and trade-offs to non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage work independently, maintain momentum and follow tasks through to completion. Degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics or another relevant discipline. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered. Experience with REST API development, Django REST Framework or a comparable framework would be advantageous. The person The ideal candidate will be comfortable working in an environment where every problem does not arrive with a predefined solution. You will be proactive, commercially aware and confident making informed technical decisions. You should enjoy delivering an effective first version, evaluating it against real data and improving it through iteration. Curiosity around emerging tools, machine learning techniques and AI-enabled development approaches will be particularly valuable. What The Role Offers A high-ownership position within a growing product and data function. The opportunity to work across machine learning, data science and data engineering. Exposure to complex datasets and meaningful production use cases. Collaboration with international product, engineering and business stakeholders. A primarily remote working arrangement, with occasional in-person sessions in Dublin.

items.card: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial
items.desc: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time. The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data. The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project. Responsibilities Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data. Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction. Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits. Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities. Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging. Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects. Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations. Qualifications You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English. To succeed in this position, you are expected to have: A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models. Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks. A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations. Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion. Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning. Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling. Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction. Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Le groupe SII est au cœur de l’innovation au service de grands comptes dans des secteurs d’ingénierie variés. En 2026, pour la 9ème année consécutive, SII France a obtenu le label Great Place To Work®. Ce succès est le reflet de notre culture basée sur notre volonté de proposer à tous nos salariés un cadre de travail épanouissant pour le développement de leurs compétences et carrières. Rejoindre SII, c’est s’engager dans une aventure collective : Let’s Tech Together ! Cette promesse représente notre ambition commune : construire un futur technologique ensemble, dans un cadre où l'expérimentation et l'autonomie sont encouragées, où les innovations sont au cœur de nos actions, et où chaque collaborateur trouve épanouissement professionnel et responsabilisation au sein d'un collectif enthousiaste et inclusif. En tant que société à fortes valeurs humaines, nous sommes signataires de la Charte d'engagement LGBT+ avec l'Association l'autre Cercle et sommes une entreprise Handi-accueillante. Let’s Tech Together incarne ce que nous sommes et ce que nous aspirons à être : une entreprise dynamique, innovante et humaine. Alors si ces valeurs vous parlent, rejoignez-nous !

items.desc: Job advertisement Vacancy ID: 290/2026 Closing date: 2026-11-09 The Friedrich Schiller University Jena is a dynamic and innovation-driven university centrally located in Germany. With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light – Life – Libert y, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. Through close collaborations with leading research institutions, innovative companies, and renowned cultural organizations, it advances interdisciplinary developments. With around 17,000 students and approximately 10,000 employees, it defines Jena as a vibrant, internationally connected city of science and innovation. The Institute of Computer Sciences at the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science seeks to fill the position of a Doctoral Researcher in Machine Learning for Virus Data Integration (m/f/d) commencing on 01 January 2027. We offer a part-time position (50% or 75%, 20 or 30 hours per week), with a fixed-term employment until 30 June 2030. The DFG-funded Collaborative Research Centre 1768 “VirusREvolution: Decoding tools for virus research” is a highly ambitious research centre at Friedrich Schiller University with the joint goal to develop novel tools for virus discovery, characterisation, regulation, interaction, and visualisation ( https://virusrevolution.uni-jena.de/ ). Its integrated research training group is educating doctoral researchers in a structured, interdisciplinary training program and invites applications for doctoral and postdoctoral researcher positions in various fields of research. In this doctoral project within the Junior Research Group “Machine Learning data integration from photonics to genomics”, you will design and train representation models and combine two or more of them in predictive deep fusion models. The goal of the project is the integration of different data that can describe viruses, from various omics to microscopy and Raman spectroscopy, in a common predictive deep learning framework. Your responsibilities: Research in multi-modal representation learning and deep fusion models for data integration Participation in the Collaborative Research Centre VirusREvolution and close collaboration with the project partners Engage in regular discussions with other group and project members Collaborate with BSc and MSc students working in associated projects Publish papers and present your work at national and international scientific meetings Your profile: A highly motivated candidate with a Master of Science or equivalent degree in computer science, bioinformatics, computational biology, or a related discipline Solid programming skills and experience with machine learning or deep learning are required Knowledge in data integration across different data modalities and virus biology is desirable Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving Ability to work independently and in a collaborative team Excellent skills in English are required, both written and spoken We offer: Embedding in a cross-disciplinary, young research group and a large, ambitious research consortium Affiliation to an Integrated Research Training Group, offering close support and a comprehensive education program for hard skills and transferable skills, supported by the Jena Graduate Academy A family-friendly working environment with a variety of offers for families University health promotion and a wide range of university sports activities Remuneration based on the provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Sector of the Federal States (TV-L) at / up to salary scale E13 — depending on the candidate’s personal qualifications—, including a special annual payment in accordance with the collective agreement. 30 days of vacation per calendar year plus two days off on December 24 and 31 Candidates with severe disabilities will be given preference in the case of equal qualifications and suitability. Are you eager to work for us? Then apply by November 9, 2026 using our online form. For further information for applicants and the information on the collection of personal data, please refer to Data privacy and information for applicants

items.desc: Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities. We’re looking for a Field Application Engineer who’s wired for AI/ML, fluent in real-world problem-solving, and excited to build with the people actually using what we make. You will collaborate closely with the sales team and enterprise customers, leveraging your deep technical knowledge in AI to drive the adoption of our products and solutions. This is a customer-facing role that requires both technical expertise and excellent communication skills to convey complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. This role is remote or hybrid based out of Belgrade, Serbia. We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting. Who You Are You’ve lived in the AI/ML trenches, whether as a field engineer, a solutions architect, or the one tapped in when things needed to “just work.” You speak both machine and human. Whether it’s a researcher or a skeptical executive, you know how to break things down and bring them to life. You’re fired up about generative models, LLMs, and the edge of what’s possible when software meets purpose-built silicon. Work directly with customers in meetings, presentations, and workshops to understand their technical challenges and provide effective solutions. items.desc: Starting date: 16/10/2026 Job Reference 446_26_ES_AC_RE2 Position Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2) Closing Date Monday, 19 October, **** Reference: 446_26_ES_AC_RE2 Job title: Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries. Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic research engineer to join the Atmospheric Composition (AC) group within the Earth Sciences department at the BSC-CNS. The AC group is currently composed of about 50 people among researchers, engineers and students of different nationalities. It aims at better understanding and predicting the spatio-temporal variations of atmospheric pollutants along with their effects upon air quality, weather and climate. This is addressed through the continuous development and application of numerical models over multiple scales, from weather to climate and from global to urban scales. The AC group develops and maintains its own forecast model MONARCH, which is a coupled meteorological-chemistry model that can be run at global and regional scales to simulate gaseous chemistry and aerosols plus their feedbacks on radiation. MONARCH is also coupled to a data assimilation scheme for gases and aerosols that is used to initialize forecasts or produce reanalyses of the atmospheric composition. The AC group operates several operational forecasting systems in the framework of the World Meteorological Organization Sand and Dust Storm Advisory System (SDS-WAS, the Copernicus atmospheric monitoring services (CAMS, the Spanish air quality forecasting system CALIOPE ( and the International Cooperative for Aerosols Predictions (ICAP). The successful candidate will join the Data Assimilation Forecasting and Application team of the AC group and will play a key coordinating role in the production and continuous improvement of the team's operational forecasting and reanalysis systems. The activities will be carried out mainly in the framework of the Copernicus CAMS2_40bis international project, with contributions to the CAMS2_82bis project and to the activities of the Barcelona Dust Regional Center (BDRC). The candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment, with tight links with researchers and engineers in the AC group. The candidate will have the opportunity to follow multiple training activities, including those aimed at improving coding and data analysis, project writing abilities, or project management. All this will be implemented via the formal courses organized by the Education and Training team and Human Resources, and the participation in the regular seminars organized by the department. Key Duties Manage the team's technical activities within CAMS2_40bis and its contributions to CAMS2_82bis and the BDRC, including planning, follow-up of tasks and milestones, and reporting. Coordinate the preparation and timely delivery of project deliverables, and represent the team in international project meetings. Coordinate the upgrades of the production systems: define and evaluate target model configurations, organize the e-suite experiments, and ensure successful operational deployments. Coordinate the production of atmospheric composition reanalyses, from planning and set-up to monitoring, validation and dissemination. Oversee the overall quality assurance of the forecast and reanalysis products, including routine evaluation against in-situ and …

items.desc: Data Scientist - Broker Flow Team Hybrid in London, United Kingdom We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Flow team. You'll own the experiments that shape the journey brokers use to apply on their clients' behalf. Brokers are one of iwoca's main routes to new customers. The Company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team Broker Flow, a new team in iwoca's third-party acquisition department, owns the journey for businesses that come to iwoca through a broker – from before they apply to a completed credit assessment. Its aim is to get more of those businesses to an offer. Broker Terms, a separate team, then sets the price, amount, and duration of each offer. The team works on three parts of that journey: Broker engagement. Working with brokers and their clients before an application starts. The application. Making it smooth to complete, and collecting the data a credit decision needs. Operations. Running the CRM tools iwoca's teams work in, and automating operational processes. The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use. The role As the Data Scientist in Broker Flow, you'll give the team the evidence behind its product decisions. The core of the work is experiment design and causal inference, with modelling and analysis alongside it. You'll own each project end to end. You'll frame the problem, choose the method, build the model or run the test, and take the answer to the commercial and strategy colleagues who act on it. You'll also meet brokers in person, which gives you the context to ask the right questions. The team is new, so its methods are yours to shape. You'll see the effect of your work in how many businesses reach an offer, and in their lifetime value. You'll work with data scientists in iwoca's other broker and partner teams, and join the analytics guild – iwoca's data science community – to compare methods and build your expertise. Your results reach the wider business through Learnings, short write-ups that iwoca shares at weekly and fortnightly sessions. Live project examples: Refinancing. Modelling which businesses would benefit from refinancing their existing borrowing, and testing a product for them. Stalled applications. Finding where broker applications stall, and testing fixes – from clearer emails and portal updates to an early offer that encourages document upload. Reintroductions. Testing the best moment for brokers to bring existing iwoca customers back to borrow. Approval probability. Measuring how well the estimate brokers see in the Introducer Portal predicts actual credit decisions, and making it more accurate. Measuring impact. Designing early signals – at sign-up and once documents are in – that predict a business's lifetime value, so the team can judge its changes quickly. The Requirements Essential: Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work. Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it. Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries. AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it. Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles. Bonus: Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them. …

items.desc: Join Jus Mundi – To Power Global Justice 🚀⚖️ Founded in 2019 and recognized as a mission-led company, Jus Mundi is pioneering legal technology to power global justice through artificial intelligence. 🌍 Headquartered in Paris, with additional offices in New York, London, and Singapore, Jus Mundi serves over 150,000 users, including top law firms, multinational corporations, government bodies, and academic institutions in more than 90 countries. By combining legal expertise with cutting-edge AI technology, we provide global legal intelligence, data-driven arbitration professional selection, and business development services. What Makes Jus Mundi the Place to Be 🌟 🧬 Our Values: With core values as Listen (Solve for the Legal Community), Iterate (Start Sharp, Stop Smart), Commit (Step In, Own the Outcome), Belong (Build together through diversity), Uphold (Aim for Justice with Integrity), we cultivate a dynamic environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and continuous growth. 🚀 Legal Is the Next Frontier for GenAI: Legal is one of the top industries ready to be transformed by GenAI. At Jus Mundi, we’re building transformative AI where it has the power to make the most impact. 🌐 Proven Product Market Fit: Jus Mundi has secured product-market fit in global markets since launch, partnering with top-tier law firms, government bodies, and major corporations, including: Freshfields, Quinn Emanuel, Wong Partnership, Total Energies, Canada, UK, and Japan. 💸 Strategic Investment: In 2024, we raised over $20 million in Series B funding from prominent strategic international investors, including Acton Capital, True Global Ventures, C4 Ventures, and FJ Labs, fueling our growth and innovation. 🤖 Legal Meets Tech: Our engineers and former lawyers collaborate closely with large language models (LLMs) to pioneer the future of generative AI and reshape professional services. 🌟 Exceptional Team: Work with talented professionals from industry leaders, including engineers, legal experts, and AI specialists from companies like Google and Amazon who are pushing the boundaries of legal tech. 📌 About the Role LLMs are confidently wrong. In international law and arbitration, a wrong date, party name or tribunal in front of a lawyer is not an acceptable error. Jus Mundi is building the AI layer for international law. We are now expanding into new areas of law, and each one brings new sources with thousands of documents in different languages. To handle that, we built a Data Platform : a pipeline of AI agents that finds legal documents on court and institution websites, downloads them, reads them and describes them, and has to prove every value it extracts. What it produces feeds our Search and Jus AI products, which lawyers use to prepare international disputes. It Already Runs End To End. Several Design Questions Are Still Open, And The Engineer Who Joins Now Will Help Answer Them Alongside The EM And Senior Engineers How should a workflow recover from a partial failure without repeating expensive model calls? How should evaluation gates balance automation, human review, quality and throughput? How should we version documents, prompts, models and extracted evidence so reprocessing stays safe? 🌟Your mission at Jus Mundi You own the delivery of your area, from design to production. Architecture decisions are made together with the Engineering Manager and senior engineers, and you take part in them. Agents, end to end. Each pipeline step is an agent: crawl a court website, download, read, classify, extract metadata, summarize, index for search. You add capabilities, make them reliable, and onboard new sources. Within your first six months, you take a new source or jurisdiction from first crawl to searchable document, with a senior engineer reviewing the design. Proof, not confidence. Every extracted value is tied to a quote from the source text, so we can always show where it came from. A quote alone does not prove the value was read correctly, so we also measure quality on evaluation sets and route doubtful cases to a human reviewer. You build and improve these checks, with lawyers from our Legal Content team defining what "correct" means. Cost and failure as design inputs. Every document has a processing cost, and every model call is paid for. Jobs fail and get retried. You build and improve retry-safe workflows that never create duplicate documents, keep repeated model calls to a minimum, and make processing cost observable. Lineage for every value. A FastAPI service and a Postgres catalog hold every document, its versions, and where each value came from: which source, which model, which prompt, which reviewer. You add endpoints, write migrations and keep that lineage complete and consistent. What you ship, you run. You deploy, watch logs, metrics and traces, fix what breaks, and know what each document costs to process. Your first 90 days Ship a fix or improvement to an existing agent in your first two weeks. items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Niveau d'expérience souhaité : Jeune diplômé Contexte et atouts du poste The position will be in the framework of the ERC Starting Grant DYNASTY (Dynamics-Aware Theory of Deep Learning). The position might include traveling to conferences for paper presentation. Travel expenses will be covered within the limits of the scale in force. Mission confiée We are seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to design and develop a Python software library for evaluating theoretical generalization bounds in deep learning. The objective is to bridge the gap between theoretical advances in learning theory and practical deep learning by providing a modular, efficient, and user-friendly framework for computing and comparing generalization bounds on modern neural networks. Principales activités Conduct experiments for empirical verification Prepare software libraries Write scientific articles Disseminate the scientific work in appropriate venues. Compétences Strong Python programming skills and experience with PyTorch. Solid understanding of machine learning and deep learning. Experience in scientific software development, testing, and version control. Familiarity with statistical learning theory and generalization bounds is a plus. Ability to work collaboratively with researchers and translate mathematical concepts into reliable software. Avantages Subsidized meals Partial reimbursement of public transport costs Leave: 7 weeks of annual leave + 10 extra days off due to RTT (statutory reduction in working hours) + possibility of exceptional leave (sick children, moving home, etc.) Possibility of teleworking and flexible organization of working hours Professional equipment available (videoconferencing, loan of computer equipment, etc.) Social, cultural and sports events and activities Access to vocational training Social security coverage Informations générales Thème/Domaine : Optimisation, apprentissage et méthodes statistiques Ingénierie logicielle (BAP E) Ville : Paris Centre Inria : Centre Inria de Paris Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 2026-12-01 Durée de contrat : 2 ans Date limite pour postuler : 2026-11-13 Attention : Les candidatures doivent être déposées en ligne sur le site Inria. Le traitement des candidatures adressées par d'autres canaux n'est pas garanti. Consignes pour postuler Sécurité défense : Ce poste est susceptible d’être affecté dans une zone à régime restrictif (ZRR), telle que définie dans le décret n°2011-1425 relatif à la protection du potentiel scientifique et technique de la nation (PPST). L’autorisation d’accès à une zone est délivrée par le chef d’établissement, après avis ministériel favorable, tel que défini dans l’arrêté du 03 juillet 2012, relatif à la PPST. Un avis ministériel défavorable pour un poste affecté dans une ZRR aurait pour conséquence l’annulation du recrutement. Politique de recrutement : Dans le cadre de sa politique diversité, tous les postes Inria sont accessibles aux personnes en situation de handicap. Contacts Équipe Inria : SIERRA Recruteur : Simsekli Umut / umut.simsekli@inria.fr A propos d'Inria Inria, l'institut national de recherche dans les sciences et technologies du numérique, est en appui de l’État pour les stratégies nationales de recherche et d’innovation du numérique en tant qu'Agence de programmes. Inria mène plus de 300 projets de recherche et d’innovation avec ses 3500 scientifiques, ingénieurs et personnels d’appui, en partenariat avec les universités et l’écosystème numérique (entreprises, entrepreneurs, acteurs publics). Ensemble, nous explorons des domaines clés comme l'intelligence artificielle, la cybersécurité, l’informatique quantique, le Cloud, la transformation numérique de la santé, les jumeaux numériques ou encore les technologies numériques pour la défense. Nous construisons des solutions concrètes telles que des logiciels, des startups technologiques, des partenariats avec les entreprises du tissu national et des formations de pointe. Notre objectif : l’impact scientifique, technologique et industriel au service de la souveraineté numérique de la France.

items.desc: On-site Bonn, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany UNU-EHS / UNU-VIE Job description United Nations University (UNU) The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States. For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit http://unu.edu UNU-EHS is one of 13 research and training Institutes that comprise the think tanks in the UNU system. UNU-EHS The United Nations University’s Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS) was established in 2003 in Bonn, Germany. The institute conducts research work focusing on advancing human security and well-being by addressing present and future risks arising from environmental hazards and climate change. Its main areas of work are risk & adaptation and transformation. In addition to its research activities, UNU-EHS offers educational opportunities at the master’s level and hosts a number of international PhD projects and capacity-development courses on global issues related to environmental risks and sustainable development. More information about UNU-EHS can be found here: https://unu.edu/ehs. Well-being and Equity (WE) Division “Well-being and Equity (WE)” is a pioneering science-to-policy research area of the United Nations University – Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS). WE aspires towards a holistic assessment of the preconditions for well-being, sustainability and equity, including leveraging on different knowledge systems that go beyond current predominantly monetary assessments. To transform towards a WE society, this emerging initiative intends to bring together a broad range of interdisciplinary scientific expertise and diverse knowledge necessary to understand the interface between well-being, sustainability and equity. The division aims to develop holistic data and policy models to weigh all dimensions of well-being, sustainability and equity for decision makers; leverage change towards a sustainable and equitable society focusing on well-being and to develop a compelling narrative for a holistic framework. . Responsibilities Under the authority of the Director of UNU-EHS and the direct supervision of the Academic Officer (Head of FAST) , the successful candidate will be entrusted with the following tasks: 1. Contribute to transformation research and theory building on Well-being and Equity Contribute to the development of research frameworks supporting the strategic approach of WE and UNU-EHS’ Transformation Department; Contribute to advancing innovative research topics including, but not limited to GDP discourse, alternative socio-ecological models and approaches for assessing well-being and equity; Contribute to theory and policy development, including identifying linkages to risk, adaptation, and transformation research and related frameworks to actively build connections to other divisions within UNU-EHS; Support the design, review, and application of qualitative, quantitative, and creative research methodologies for transformative research on well-being and equity. 2. Contribute to strategic engagement and proposal writing Support the establishment and development of the Well-being Alliance for Research, Policy and Practice through the coordination of assigned activities, meetings and events, and by engaging stakeholders and partners to strengthen the division's global network; Assist senior staff in identifying and evaluating funding opportunities from various sources and in compiling and maintaining information on funding trends, donor priorities, and emerging opportunities; Contribute to and support the Head of Division and/or PI in the preparation and drafting of project proposals to different donors and partners, liaising with partners and consortium set-up; Contribute to the implementation of new projects by performing assigned research and reporting as needed. 3. items.card: Ihre Aufgaben Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems. Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA
items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) Göttingen At HAWK University of Applied Sciences and Arts Hildesheim/Holzminden/Göttingen, Faculty of Engineering and Health, Göttingen campus, the following position in the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS is to be filled at the earliest possible date, for a fixed term of three years: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) Within the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS, we are developing novel photonic and molecular analytical methods for the high-resolution investigation of dynamic protein-DNA interactions. Femtosecond laser-based crosslinking (fliX) is combined with complementary methods in quantitative and structural proteomics (LC-MS/MS), genomics and sequencing (ChIP-Seq, nanopore sequencing), and bioinformatics for multiomics data integration and analysis to characterise protein–DNA interactions at the structural and functional levels. The aim is to make previously inaccessible dynamic molecular processes experimentally measurable and thereby establish new foundations for investigating regulatory mechanisms in biological and disease-relevant systems. A central focus is the development and physicochemical characterisation of novel irradiation and measurement approaches based on ultrashort laser pulses. For this research area, we are seeking a highly motivated scientist with strong experimental expertise in non-linear optics and ultrashort-pulse laser systems who can independently develop, implement, and characterise complex optical setups and, together with an interdisciplinary team, investigate the underlying femtochemical processes. The work combines fundamental research in ultrafast physics and femtochemistry with applications in molecular bioanalytics and biomedical research. It will open up new opportunities for the structural and functional analysis of protein–DNA interactions and for understanding disease-relevant regulatory processes. Ihre Aufgaben Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems. Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA damage. Systematically investigating and optimising relevant laser and process parameters, such as wavelength, pulse duration, pulse energy, repetition rate, temporal pulse separation, and irradiation dose. Characterising, validating, and standardising the optical setups and measurement methods developed, including benchmarking, reproducibility assessments, troubleshooting, and the preparation of SOPs. Working closely with experts in physics, molecular biology, proteomics, sequencing, and bioinformatics; jointly interpreting results and integrating them into experimental planning. Contributing to scientific publications, project communication, and, where results are eligible for intellectual property protection, invention disclosures and patent applications. Ihr Profil A completed university degree at Master’s or Diploma level in physics, photonics, physical chemistry, or a related natural science; a completed doctorate is desirable. Excellent theoretical and practical knowledge of non-linear optics and ultrashort laser pulses and extensive experience with sophisticated experimental laser setups. Demonstrated experience in the independent design, alignment, characterisation, and operation of complex optical and/or spectroscopic experimental setups. Experience in photochemistry, femtochemistry, time-resolved spectroscopy, or related fields is advantageous. Strong analytical and independent scientific thinking, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and develop solutions to scientific and methodological challenges. A strong interest in biological and biomedical research questions, together with a willingness to acquire expertise in protein–DNA interactions and molecular analytical methods. Enthusiasm for method and technology development, systematic optimisation, and experimental troubleshooting, as well as an independent, structured, and responsible working style. Excellent teamwork and communication skills, together with an enthusiasm for close collaboration in an interdisciplinary team. A demonstrated record of scientific publications; experience with invention disclosures, intellectual property rights, or patent applications is desirable. Very good English skills for scientific communication and laboratory work and very good German skills for handling administrative matters are expected. items.desc: On the 1 August 2026, the University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South-East (LASE) University Group. Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Greenwich academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities. Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact. This is an opportunity to join a particularly vibrant research environment. The university’s Centre for Sustainable Cyber Security is recognised by the UK government as one of only nine Academic Centres of Excellence for both Research and Education in Cyber Security: https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/case-study/the-university-of-greenwich This position is part of EU project GANNDALF and relates to studying and addressing the privacy-explainability tradeoff of explainable AI use in modern cyber crime investigations. Through agency-to-agency data sharing mechanisms and the deployment of a decision-support toolbox to identify cyber threats, GANNDALF is delivering a customisable and collaborative crime investigation sandbox for scenarios for sophisticated crime investigation. The role holder will help advance our existing work in optimising explainability strength in cyber crime investigations, taking into account privacy. The role holder will also take on the corresponding pilot implementations and evaluations. The role holder is expected to have a PhD in computer science or equivalent and a strong publication record in privacy-enhancing technologies or explainable AI. See the job specification for more details. The post is until the end of the project (end of September 2027), but there is scope to extend further. Background Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGL) are rare neuroendocrine tumours arising from chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla and sympathetic/parasympathetic paraganglia. Approximately 35% of patients carry germline mutations in one of over 20 known PPGL predisposition genes, with mutations in SDHx genes ( SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2) being most common. Patients with SDHB-associated tumours are more likely to develop metastatic disease than patients with sporadic tumours or tumours associated with other predisposing genes. Once disease is metastatic, there are currently limited therapeutic options creating an urgent unmet clinical need. Despite a sophisticated molecular understanding of SDHB mutation driven tumours, the field lacks validated human cell models - a fundamental barrier to translating insights into new treatments for patients with SDHB-deficient disease. This project will continue our drive to develop much-needed novel cell models of PPGL, with the aim of establishing a comprehensive human PPGL cell resource with a particular focus on SDHx-deficient tumours. The post holder will use these models to investigate aspects of SDH-deficient cell metabolism that has the potential to uncover novel therapeutic targets within the metabolic network. The postholder will work alongside others in a dynamic and ambitious research group led by Professor Tennant, and in addition to their own project will have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects within the group. The postholder would be expected to progressively take more responsibility for the direction of their research project as they develop their specific expertise in the project area, will want to explore multiple research strands in parallel. For example, alongside deriving new models of SDB-deficient cancers from clinical material, the postholder will also investigate aspects of the metabolic dysfunction observed in these cancer to identify routes towards better treatments. The postholder should be fluent in the subject matter relevant to the post, including techniques or methods. If they are not already proficient, the postholder will be expected to rapidly acquire the technical skills required for the post, as well as the ability to analyse data arising from these methods. items.desc:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Munich. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

 - Are fluent in both German and English

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. You’ll help build the next generation of native mobile apps that connect millions of customers to their NETGEAR devices. You’ll work alongside experienced mobile engineers across the full product life cycle, from requirements through build and test to release and the production data that follows. That ownership is the fastest way to earn trust and take on bigger work. You’ll join our mobile engineering team in Cork, which is part of NETGEAR’s global engineering organization. The team is hybrid, and you’ll spend at least two days a week in the office to collaborate, learn and share ideas. What You Will Be Doing Building features in our native Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) applications, from ticket to release. Owning the quality of what you build, including functional QA, regression testing and release validation. Testing on real devices to make sure setup flows, error states and edge cases work for the person holding the phone, not just for the test suite. Writing and maintaining automated unit, integration and UI tests, so the same bug is never found twice by hand. Working AI-first, using agentic coding tools to plan, write, test, review and refactor, and helping the team get better at it. Real ownership of quality, which is the fastest route to trust and scope on this team. A deep understanding of mobile architectures, UI frameworks and platform APIs. Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing and modern DevOps practice. Fluency in AI-assisted development using Claude Code, Copilot and ChatGPT. A structured graduate onboarding path with a named mentor and a defined first-year development plan. Room to grow within NETGEAR’s global engineering organization. What We Are Looking For A Level 8 honours degree (or an equivalent honours bachelor’s degree) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronic Engineering or a related discipline. A hands-on attitude. Our best engineers pick up whatever the release needs rather than waiting for it to be assigned. Clear written and spoken communication. Knowledge of REST APIs and mobile architecture fundamentals such as MVC or MVVM. Interest in networked applications, IoT or connected devices. We assess aptitude, not a checklist. If you have shipped something you are proud of in any stack, apply. With several roles available, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. Why Join NETGEAR Build mobile apps that help millions of users manage and connect their devices worldwide. Start your career alongside a Cork-based team that values innovation, craftsmanship and continuous learning. Work on mobile and IoT technology at global scale. Learn and deliver faster with leading AI development tools. Competitive salary, pension, healthcare and share scheme. Key Details Start date: November 2026 Closing date: 1st November 2026. Join us to: Help build the future of online trading Be part of a culture driven by integrity and global impact Become part of an award-winning company - check out our full list of awards here We are only as good as our people. Luckily, our people are the best. Join us! How do we work? Hello ASO Experts! We are looking for a forward-thinking AI ASO Specialist to join our Warsaw team. You won’t just be "adjusting keywords" - you will be bridging the gap between traditional App Store/Play Store discovery and the new era of AI-driven app recommendations. As part of our global Marketing Department, you will join our currently 2-person SEO & ASO Team which we are expanding to support our growing digital footprint. We work in a hybrid model - we'd love to meet you in the office 2 times a week with respect to your own commitments. In this role, you will: Execute an AI-enhanced metadata strategy by leveraging internal AI tools to research, test, and craft high-converting app titles, subtitles, and keyword-rich descriptions for both iOS and Android. Drive strategic off-page link building by securing high-quality backlinks for our app store listings and landing pages, effortlessly distinguishing between authoritative traffic sources and low-quality link networks or spammy APK mirrors. Lead Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) by auditing visual assets (icons, screenshots, preview videos) and running structured A/B tests via Apple Product Page Optimization and Google Play Store Listing Experiments. Pioneer App Engine Optimization (AEO) by experimenting with how mobile apps are indexed and cited across AI-generated search tools (Perplexity, Gemini, ChatGPT) to ensure OANDA is recommended for intent-based user queries. What skillset do you need to be successful in this role? Hands-on experience acquiring quality backlinks to drive store authority and support web-to-app conversions; impact matters more than years. Strong understanding of keyword ranking algorithms and indexing mechanics for both Apple App Store (iOS) and Google Play Store (Android). Practical knowledge of App Store Connect and Google Play Console, including deep-linking concepts (Universal Links, App Links). Fluent English. Proven experience using AI tools with the ability to rapidly produce optimized metadata and localized drafts via AI-assisted workflows. Genuine interest in how LLMs and NLP are reshaping app discovery, combined with the adaptability to respond quickly to algorithm updates and store policy changes. Nice to have: Basic scripting skills (Python or JavaScript) to automate competitor keyword tracking, review scraping, or store data analysis. Familiarity with low-code/no-code automation tools (Zapier, Make.com) to streamline keyword monitoring or app-featuring alerts. Your perspective matters. items.desc: Overview: V-Nova is a London-based technology company specialising in visual data architectures for AI, media and immersive applications. Its hierarchical, compute-aware data formats bring structure and intelligence to video, images and point clouds, enabling systems to access and process only the visual information they need. This can reduce data movement, decoding and compute across demanding visual workflows and make large scale AI processing more efficient. V-Nova has contributed key IP to internationally standardised technologies including MPEG-5 Part 2 LCEVC and SMPTE VC-6 (ST 2117), and also develops PresenZ for volumetric and 6DoF experiences. With a portfolio of more than 1,600 international patents, V-Nova combines deep-science R&D with highly optimised software products and integrations that bring its technology into real-world media, cloud and AI systems. We are committed to the extraordinary and rely on talented, high-performing teams to solve difficult problems and deliver what we promise. Our culture values individual empowerment, excellence, intellectual curiosity and teamwork. Across research, engineering, product and commercial teams, we make active use of the latest AI tools to accelerate analysis, development, writing and experimentation. With ground-breaking technology, a fast-paced collaborative environment and ambitious growth plans, this is an opportunity to make a visible contribution to an emerging category of Visual AI infrastructure. The Visual AI Analyst will join V-Nova's Strategic Analytics & Business Insights (SABI) team and work at the intersection of analytics, product development and business development. The role will help turn V-Nova's hierarchical visual data technologies into measurable performance advantages and compelling customer propositions for Visual AI workflows. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Integration and Commercial teams to develop, validate and take to market Visual AI acceleration solutions based on V-Nova technologies such as VC-6, LCEVC and emerging AI solutions. The work is deliberately varied: one week you may be analysing GPU benchmark logs and isolating a pipeline bottleneck; the next, building an AI-assisted dashboard, assessing caption or embedding quality, researching a new AI framework, or translating technical results into a partner facing business case. This is not a role for somebody who needs a tightly defined playbook. We are looking for a high-learning-velocity analyst who enjoys unfamiliar problems, can structure ambiguity, figures things out with limited supervision and is motivated by getting to a useful result. Deep prior knowledge of video compression or Visual AI is not required; curiosity, analytical rigour and the ability to learn fast are more important. Responsibilities: Designing, supporting and analysing benchmarks and experiments across visual AI training and inference workflows, quantifying the impact of V-Nova technologies on quality, latency, throughput, compute, storage and cost. Turning raw test artefacts into insight, spotting anomalies and bottlenecks; forming hypotheses; and working with engineering colleagues to validate root causes and optimisation opportunities. Building practical internal analytics tools such as dashboards, parsers, report generators, scripts and automations, using modern AI coding agents to extend your own capabilities and make experimentation faster and easier to interpret. Working with Product and Engineering to translate evidence into decisions: defining useful test plans and acceptance criteria, identifying optimal configurations, prioritising follow-up work and producing clear recommendations. Supporting V-Nova's Visual AI go-to-market and business development through use-case and ecosystem research, competitor analysis, market sizing, pricing and business-case work, and by turning technical evidence into concise partner and customer materials and integration priorities. Collaborating with Marketing, other internal teams and external partners to turn technical evidence into high-quality thought-leadership and market-facing content, including blogs, articles, social media communications, scientific publications and event materials. Owning the practical discipline around experiments and analysis: coordinating datasets and cloud GPU resources where needed, keeping results and artefacts reproducible and well documented, communicating progress clearly, and following issues through to resolution. The role offers unusual breadth and exposure for an analyst. You will work directly with senior V-Nova product and engineering specialists and with external technology partners, including NVIDIA and major cloud and hyperscale companies, on projects at the leading edge of Visual AI infrastructure. You will also receive close coaching from V-Nova's SVP Strategic Analytics & Business Insights, a senior strategy leader with a McKinsey background. The environment is demanding, collaborative …

items.desc: About the Role We are looking for an Electronics Design Engineer to take ownership of PCB design, system wiring, cable harnesses, connectors, electronics integration, microcontroller interfaces, and the surrounding charging and support infrastructure for our Counter-UAS interceptor platform. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who is comfortable moving between schematics, PCB layouts, lab debugging, cable harnesses, embedded firmware, EMC topics, production constraints, and system-level integration. You will design, build, debug, and improve the electronics backbone of the interceptor system. Your work will connect flight computers, guidance computers, ESCs, sensors, batteries, charging systems, connectors, cable harnesses, and ground infrastructure into one reliable and production-ready system. What is your Day to Day Mission: Design PCBs using Altium Designer, KiCad, or comparable tools , from schematic capture to layout, manufacturing data, and bring-up. Create and maintain electronics architectures for the interceptor platform, including power distribution, signal routing, communication interfaces, and system wake/sleep behavior. Support PCB prototyping, assembly, rework, debugging, revision management, and preparation for production. Design and specify cable harnesses, connectors, pinouts, contact systems, and mechanical-electrical interfaces. Select connectors and wiring concepts that are robust, compact, and as error-proof as possible during assembly. Work on EMC-related topics, grounding concepts, shielding, signal integrity, and robust communication under demanding operational conditions. Implement and debug simple microcontroller firmware for functions such as battery management interfaces, power-state control, wake-up logic, charging interfaces, and system supervision. Work with communication protocols such as CAN, UART, SPI, I²C, Ethernet , or similar embedded interfaces. Support electronics integration inside the drone across multiple sections, including flight computers, guidance computers, ESCs, batteries, sensors, and antennas. Support external system infrastructure, including charging electronics, multi-vehicle charging concepts, umbilical interfaces, and communication between ground infrastructure and drones. Work closely with mechanical design and production teams to ensure electronics can be assembled quickly, reliably, and repeatedly. Support field tests and flight tests by debugging electronics, wiring, logs, and hardware failures. What You Bring to the Team Degree in electrical engineering, electronics, embedded systems, mechatronics, or a comparable field. Strong practical experience with PCB design, schematic capture, layout, bring-up, and debugging. Experience with lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, and soldering/rework tools. Understanding of embedded communication protocols, power distribution, connectors, cable harnesses, and electronics integration. Ability to write or debug basic embedded firmware in C, C++, Rust, or Python . Practical mindset: you are comfortable building, measuring, debugging, and iterating quickly. Structured approach to documentation, pinouts, revision management, BOMs, and production handover. Ability to work across electronics, mechanics, software, production, and testing. Experience with UAVs, robotics, automotive electronics, aerospace electronics, or defense systems. Experience with high-current systems, battery interfaces, chargers, ESCs, or propulsion electronics. Familiarity with EMC testing, environmental testing, or safety-critical hardware. Experience designing electronics for mass production. Hands-on hobby projects involving drones, RC aircraft, robots, embedded boards, or custom PCBs. Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. Be at the forefront of next-generation Defence innovation . Work in a fast-paced, agile environment where your ideas make an impact. Collaborate with a team of industry pioneers who are ambitious, bold, and visionary. Opportunities for individual and professional growth in a globally recognized organization. items.desc: An exciting opportunity has arisen within the Plain Film X-Ray Imaging department at South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. We are seeking a Band 5 Diagnostic Radiographer to work within the radiography team. The department includes the provision of plain film x-ray, dental (including cone beam CT) and theatre services as well as specialist modalities, including US, CT, MRI and fluoroscopy/interventional radiology. The successful candidate will be a role model for demonstrating our Trust's values through their leadership attributes and be committed to providing high quality, patient focussed patient care. Although the successful candidate will be employed by South Tees Foundation Trust, there will be an expectation of collaborative working across the Tees Valley in the future should the need be required. However, this role is primarily for South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust , The James Cook University Hospital Plain Film services. The successful candidate will join the James Cook Plain Film roster South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and work across all service sites. Successful candidates will be an employee of South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and managed as per the governance arrangements currently in place for Radiology and the organisation. The Radiology service is dedicated in facilitating continuous professional development and role extension/advanced practice. There are more than 30 Advanced Practitioners within the service, with specialist experience in fluoroscopy/interventional radiology, ultrasound, CT, MRI and plain film radiographer reporting. South Tees Hospitals is the largest hospital trust in the Tees Valley with two acute hospitals and services in a number of community hospitals. South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is already nationally recognised as one of the leading healthcare providers in England for the quality of our services. The Trust is a designated regional Major trauma centre with a 24-hour acute admissions unit and specialised services in cancer, neurosciences, vascular surgery, spinal injuries, cardiology and renal medicine. Please note this post will close at sufficient applicants. South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust have come together to form University Hospitals Tees. As a result, post holders may be required to work across sites within both organisations. Across University Hospitals Tees, our ambition is to be the best place to work, ensuring we have the right staff in the right roles at the right time to deliver outstanding patient care and experience. We are committed to supporting our staff through an inclusive and supportive working environment, offering health and wellbeing initiatives, staff benefits, and opportunities for personal and professional development. We support the 'Making Every Contact Count' approach to behaviour change in the promotion of health and wellbeing of individuals and communities. Please see the full job description and person specification document(s) attached for main responsibilities of the role.
