items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



About The Job

 

Mistral AI is seeking a Applied AI Engineer to facilitate the adoption of its products among customers and collaborate with them to address complex technical challenges.

 

The Applied AI team is Mistral's customer-facing technical organization. We work directly with enterprise clients from pre-sales through implementation to deploy cutting-edge AI solutions that deliver measurable business impact.

 

Our team combines deep ML expertise with strong customer engagement skills, operating like startup CTOs who own end-to-end project execution. By joining the team you'll will bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and real-world enterprise applications, ensuring our solutions are robust, scalable, and aligned with both customer needs and Mistral's technological vision.

 

What you will do

 

- You’ll individually help deploy into production use cases with a considerable business impact across various industries.

- You’ll work on state-of-the-art GenAI applications from consumer products to industrial use cases, driving with our customers a crucial technological transformation.

- You’ll work in collaboration with our researchers, other AI engineers, product engineers on our most complex customer projects involving complex fine-tuning, state-of-the-art LLM applications, and contributing to our open-source codebases our open source codebases for tasks such as inference and fine-tuning.

- You’ll be involved in pre-sales calls to understand potential clients' needs, challenges, and aspirations. You will provide technical guidance on our products and explain Mistral technologies to various stakeholders.

- Your collaboration with our product and science team to improve continuously our product and model capabilities based on customers’ feedback

 

How We Work in Applied AI

 

- We care about people and outputs.

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

- No politics. Low ego, high standards.

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

 

About you

 

- You are fluent in English

- You have 2+ years as a technical individual contributor (data scientist or software engineer) on AI-based products

- You have proven experience in AI or machine learning product implementation with APIs, back-end and front-end interfaces.

- You have experience in Fine Tuning LLMs, tackling advanced RAG or agentic use cases

- You have deep understanding of concepts and algorithms underlying machine learning and LLMs

- You have strong technical coding skills in Python

- You hold strong communication skills with an ability to explain complex technical concepts in simple terms with technical and non-technical audiences

 

Ideally you have:

- Contributed to open-source projects in particular in the space of LLMs

- Experience as a Customer Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect or Technical Product Manager

- You have experience with deep learning with Pytorch

Why join us?

 

You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of AI adoption in enterprises, work with a world-class team, and contribute to open-source projects that impact millions. If you’re excited about leading technical innovation and solving real-world challenges with AI, we’d love to hear from you!




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.

items.desc:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.



We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.



Here’s what this particular role covers.



🛠️ About our Robotics Team

The Robotics team is responsible for bridging the gap from our model to our vehicle platforms, in order to let the model focus on making driving decisions. We aim to provide high quality data to the model for making such decisions, whilst abstracting away platform-specific aspects.



🧠 Your day-to-day

 - Define the technical architecture and roadmap for Wayve’s offline 3D reconstruction system.

 - Lead the development of MVPs that unblock high-priority internal use cases, while guiding the transition to a robust internal platform.

 - Establish the core technical interfaces, output representations, and tools needed to support internal customers.

 - Partner with calibration, sensor fusion, perception, data, infrastructure, and validation teams to align requirements, resources and ownership boundaries.

 - Set technical standards for reconstruction quality, failure analysis, uncertainty measurement, and dataset suitability and execute strategies to validate them

 - Mentor and provide technical leadership to engineers contributing to the 3D reconstruction effort.

 - Communicate technical tradeoffs, limitations, and progress clearly to engineering leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.



🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Leading the development of an offline 3D reconstruction capability that builds high-quality 3D world geometry from vehicle sensor data in dynamic scenes. The system will draw on localization and mapping, state estimation, and sensor fusion to produce offline 3D geometric reconstructions and best-estimate ego motion from heterogeneous vehicle platforms and sensor suites. The work will support internal validation, data enrichment, and model development by turning raw sensor data into reliable, quality-assessed 3D ground-truth outputs. This is a principal-level technical leadership role for someone who can set the technical direction, build early prototypes, and align cross-functional teams around a shared reconstruction capability.



🙌 You should apply if you have:

Required Skills/Experience

 - Deep technical expertise in SLAM, 3D reconstruction, mapping, state estimation, or closely related robotics/perception fields.

 - Strong hands-on experience with lidar-based reconstruction, point-cloud registration, pose estimation, and real-world robotics sensor data.

 - Experience building offline reconstruction, mapping, or perception systems that operate on large volumes of sensor data.

 - Strong software engineering skills in C++, Python, or similar robotics/perception environments.

 - Experience taking research or prototype algorithms into reliable production systems.

 - Comfortable defining technical strategy, roadmaps, and milestones in ambiguous problem spaces

 - Strong cross-functional technical leadership in ambiguous, multi-team environments.

 - Clear communication of algorithmic tradeoffs, limitations, confidence, and failure modes to technical and cross functional stakeholders.

 - Systems-level understanding of sensor calibration, timing, synchronization and quality issues, and ability to define requirements and work with specialist teams to achieve them



Desired Skills/Experience

 - MS/PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, State Estimation, Sensor Fusion, SLAM, 3D Reconstruction, or a related technical field; or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience with autonomous vehicles, robotics, mapping, or ground-truth data pipelines in a production setting.

 - Experience with GNSS/INS fusion, sensor based odometry, or other high-accuracy position estimation approaches

 - Experience with nonlinear optimization techniques such as pose graph optimization, factor graphs, bundle adjustment, ICP etc

 - Experience apply modern machine learning approaches to 3D reconstruction, mapping, or scene understanding, including foundation models or learned 3D representations

 - Familiarity with robotics tooling such as ROS, PCL, OpenCV, CUDA, or similar.

 - Familiarity with ML data enrichment, autolabelling, annotation workflows, or validation-data generation.

 - Experience designing quality metrics, validation evidence, or credibility arguments for reconstructed data.

 - Experience leading small expert technical teams from early-stage concept to production use.



🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to lead the design of end‑to‑end services that support some of the UK’s most critical missions? At Leonardo UK, our Service Designers bring human‑centred, evidence‑based design leadership to multi‑disciplinary delivery teams, shaping services across the full lifecycle — from Discovery through to Live. You will provide expert professional advice, influence decision‑making, and lead complex design work that transforms how users interact with our services and how those services operate behind the scenes. 
 Your work at Leonardo UK will see you take the lead in solving customer problems in an agile, innovative and team-centric manner. The role may involve a blended hybrid working model, with a mixture of working from home and working on site at our Bristol office to ensure close collaboration with the wider team and with our customers. 
 What you will do as a Service Designer 
 Lead service design activities across Discovery, Alpha, Beta and Live. 
 Produce service maps, journeys, blueprints, and end‑to‑end service models. 
 Work collaboratively across multi‑disciplinary teams to align user needs, business goals and technology constraints. 
 Provide professional advice on service design approaches, risks and opportunities. 
 Coordinate service design work to time, quality and business expectations. 
 Facilitate workshops, co‑design and decision‑making forums. 
 Support the development of service design practice and mentor junior team members. 
 What you’ll bring 
 Strong expertise across the DDaT service design lifecycle. 
 Ability to influence decisions with evidence, research and clear rationale. 
 Experience delivering complex service design in multi‑disciplinary teams. 
 Strong communication skills and confidence in simplifying complexity. 
 Ability to contribute to planning, strategy and roadmap discussions. 
 Experience coaching or supporting others in service design. 
 Core areas (must have): 
 Proven experience in end‑to‑end service design (DDaT). 
 Ability to produce service artefacts at multiple levels (journeys → blueprints → ecosystems). 
 Skilled in evidence‑based design: insight synthesis, problem framing, prioritisation. 
 Ability to influence stakeholders across engineering, product and policy domains. 
 Experience coordinating service design delivery across phases and teams 
 Desirable: 
 Exposure to operational service management (ITIL, SLAs, support models). 
 Experience in defence, government or regulated environments. 
 Working knowledge of adjacent roles (UR, BA, Product, Interaction Design). 
 Experience in agile or SAFe delivery environments. 
 Professional training/accreditation in service design or human‑centred design. 
 Contribution to communities of practice or internal capability uplift. 
 This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn. 
 Security Clearance 
 This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.

 Secure your Future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution. 
 Your Wellbeing Matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity). 
 Rewarding Performance : All employees at management level and below are eligible for our bonus scheme. 
 Never Stop Learning : Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning. 
 Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme. 
 Tailored Perks : Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more. 
 Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role. 
 For a full list of our company benefits please visit our website.

items.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in acoustics, building physics, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or related disciplines. A research-oriented attitude. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). The following experience could be considered an advantage and may be highlighted in your motivation letter: Affinity for building acoustics, vibro-acoustics, or structural dynamics Previous experience with/affinity for computational methods Previous publications and scientific communications Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. items.desc: The Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology (IMBIM) at Uppsala University provides a broad international environment for research and teaching. IMBIM conducts basic research in biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, tumor biology, comparative genetics, functional genomics, immunology, bacteriology, and virology. The department's research is primarily basic in nature, but its applications have a clear connection to, and significance for, health and disease in both animals and humans. A more detailed description is available at Research – Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology – Uppsala University. The Medical Inflammation Research (MIR) Group led by Prof. Rikard Holmdahl at the department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology (IMBIM), Uppsala University, aims to improve human health by identifying the regulatory pathways of autoimmune diseases. A basis of this research some of the major genetic polymorphic alleles associated with autoimmune diseases in experimental animals have been identified and unique mouse strains developed. We are looking for an experienced researcher to lead and coordinate projects with a focus in driving the research, development, and validation of the humanized mouse model. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts, access cutting-edge resources, and contribute to transformative discoveries that can shape the future of autoimmune disease treatment. Your mission You will be involved in collecting and synthesizing existing scientific evidence and generating new data to characterize the asset for key stakeholders in rheumatology research, as well as exploring broader applicability across other research areas, as well as in overseeing and manage the animal model platform for other scientists and researchers. You will lead the design, execution, and reporting of in vivo and in vitro experiments to characeterise and validate the humanized mouse strains as a model to evaluate the efficacy and generate mechanistic insights of candidate immunotherapies targeting autoimmune diseases and other conditions, and to address key questions that shape the future of autoimmune disease treatment. You will be working with immunology-oriented research including in vivo experiment, immune assays and flow cytometry, and expression analysis. In addition, the role includes developing experimental proposals for other users, with the aim of attracting new scientific interest, collaborators, and funding opportunities. You are also expected to contribute to scientific publications and participate in the supervision of master students and teaching. Required Qualifications Doctoral degree, or a foreign degree deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree, in Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology or a related field. This eligibility requirement must be fulfilled at the latest at the time of the employment decision. It is considered an advantage if you have and a long experience with animal models. Relevant advanced research experience in mouse handling, mouse breeding and genotyping, animal experimentation (including surgical procedures), disease models, as well as experience with laboratory cellular biology work. Strong background in genetics, immunology, biochemistry, biostatistical analysis, flow cytometry, antibody based immune assays as well as in vivo autoimmune disease models will be considered valuable. Proficient knowledge of English We place great importance on personal suitability and are looking for highly creative and motivated employees who appreciate working in a team. We expect the applicants to show good collaboration skills and at the same time great independence. About the position Fixed-term employment for one year, full-time. Starting date by agreement. Background In line with the Institute’s efforts to enhance its training activities, the Multilateral Diplomacy Programme is developing an unprecedented amount of online and face-to-face activities offered to the diplomatic community based in Geneva, New York and elsewhere. items.desc: Developer Experience / DevEx Location: Bristol / London About Fractile Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world's most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. The Role About the Software organisation at Fractile Developer Experience sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing. About the team and role The Developer Experience team at Fractile helps shape how our customers interact with the Fractile inference accelerator. We work across the company to identify, create, and present information on how the system is being used, as well as providing the tooling to help optimise our customers' usage of the system, while keeping a shallow learning curve. As a member of the Developer Experience team you will need to understand the current state of development for inference hardware. You will need to be able to identify what will work well for engineers wanting to identify potential opportunities for performance improvements, while knowing what tooling will fit into an existing LLM engineer's workflow with the minimal amount of disruption and effort. About you We're looking for someone who is self-driven and capable of identifying tooling opportunities, designing those tools, and delivering them in a way which will fit in with an LLM engineer's existing toolset. You will have worked in this area before, possibly as an FDE or at a company that provides inference services using their own models, and have the ability to develop new tools that are designed to be functional and easy to learn and use. Key Requirements Experience with inference frameworks such as JAX and/or PyTorch Experience of software development in Python, Rust, C/C++, or a similar language Experience monitoring and optimising code written in CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, or similar Experience monitoring and optimising LLM deployments with 50+ billion parameters Experience working with stakeholders across multiple teams What We Offer Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We've recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us! items.desc: The Oliver McGowan Programme Administrator will provide comprehensive administrative and coordination support to the delivery of the Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training on Learning Disability and Autism across Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust and partner organisations. The post holder will play a key role in supporting the implementation, rollout and ongoing delivery of a collaborative Greater Manchester training model, working closely with Facilitating Trainers, Co-Trainers, Experts by Experience and colleagues across partner NHS trusts, local authorities and wider health and social care organisations. The role will be responsible for coordinating training activities, maintaining accurate records, supporting communication with stakeholders, arranging venues and resources, and ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the training programme. The post holder will also support arrangements for Experts by Experience and Co-Trainers, including assisting with travel, venue access requirements, reasonable adjustments and logistical arrangements to enable participation in training delivery across multiple locations. To provide comprehensive administrative support to the Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training Programme, ensuring the smooth planning, scheduling and coordination of training sessions across Pennine Care and partner organisations. Responsibilities include processing bookings, cancellations and amendments for training events, producing attendance lists, registers, certificates and evaluation reports, and monitoring training capacity to support the effective allocation of places. Maintaining accurate records and providing efficient administrative coordination, ensuring the successful delivery of the training programme and support compliance with organisational training requirements. We are proud to provide high quality mental health and learning disability services, both inpatient and in the community across five boroughs of Greater Manchester - Bury, Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside and Glossop. Our vision is for a happier and more hopeful life for everyone in our communities and our staff work hard to deliver the very best care for the people who use our services. items.desc: Agentic Systems Designer Full-time · Copenhagen, Lisbon, or remote within the EU Applicants must currently reside in the EU. NORDFY works with architecture, AEC and creative companies to build AI capability their teams can own. We are part of Verka Collective, a group of independent European design practices. We’re hiring someone to own the architecture and delivery of internal agents, integrations and systems across those practices. “Designer” here means designing how software systems work and building them through to production. You’ll make decisions about architecture, reliability and where human judgment belongs, then deliver systems another team can operate. What you’ll work on: • Build internal systems that help firms run their operations with AI. • Connect tools, data and models through integrations and agentic workflows. • Make systems reliable when third-party APIs are inconsistent, documentation is thin or problems only appear in production. • Design retries, state management and delivery guarantees appropriate to the work. • Decide where people stay involved and how systems should fail safely. • Document the architecture, put backup and recovery arrangements in place, and hand over the work so it remains operable without you. What you need to bring: • Experience building and operating consequential production systems. • A working understanding of idempotency, retries, state and delivery guarantees, including what exactly-once execution actually requires. • Experience with MCP servers, agent orchestration or long-running autonomous workflows. You do not need experience with all three. • Regular use of agentic coding tools, with a clear understanding of their capabilities and limits. • The ability to explain architecture decisions and write software other people can maintain. • Confidence taking responsibility for a substantial area of work. Useful additional experience • Working with architecture, AEC or other design-led organisations. • Delivering software to professional-services firms. • Working across languages and markets in the Nordics or DACH region. Working at NORDFY: You’ll join a small senior team with direct access to the collective’s leadership. You’ll work with frontier AI tools, have time to develop your practice, and take part in gatherings with teams across the collective, including AI Coordinators and Champions. Salary is agreed individually, based on the role, experience and local market. Employment is arranged locally, directly or through an Employer of Record. Contract terms, benefits and pension arrangements follow the rules of your country of residence. How to apply: Tell us about the least reliable system you have ever made reliable, and how you did it. Send your application to info@nordfy.dk with “Agentic Systems Designer” in the subject line. Include a GitHub profile, a write-up or other evidence that shows how you approach these problems. We need to see evidence of delivered work. A general cover letter alone won’t give us enough to assess your application.

items.desc: If you are here, it is because you know that we are looking for a Forward Deployed AI Engineer . indigo.ai is the leading platform in Italy for building next-generation AI Agents that transform the way companies communicate with their customers. Since 2016, we’ve been helping enterprises in industries such as finance, insurance, utilities, retail, and e-commerce to evolve their Customer Experience through conversational AI. We don’t just “sell software”: we enable a shift in how organizations interact with people, automating millions of conversations every year, reducing operational costs, improving conversion rates, and creating more personalized, scalable, and compliant customer journeys. Backed by a recent €10 million investment from Azimut, we are on a mission to take this technology global. This is a unique opportunity to join a well-funded, highly ambitious team and play a direct role in shaping the future of enterprise AI. To make this happen, we are looking for a Forward Deployed AI Engineer to support our Chief AI Officer in designing AI Agents and taking them live, side by side with our clients in Spain. What are we looking for? We are looking for a Forward Deployed AI Engineer to take our AI Agents from design to production, working side by side with our enterprise clients. We are growing our team in Madrid to support new projects in the Iberian market, and the role reports directly to our Chief AI Officer. It is a cross-functional role for a T-shaped profile, between technology and business: your value lies in deciding how an assistant should work (its architecture, flows and behavior) and in making it work with real users and traffic, while Product and AI tools handle low-level configuration and detailed debugging. With the right fit, the role can grow into delivery leadership: defining how we design AI Agents, mentoring new hires and helping build our AI implementation team as we expand in Europe. Key Responsibilities: Design the agentic architecture: decide how to frame each problem (for example, a router agent that hands off to specialized agents) and where gates and guardrails are needed, such as user recognition, queue management and handover to a human agent. You design the structure before building it, for both chat and voice, which follow the same logic. Keep hallucinations under control: define the boundaries of each agent, deciding when it answers, when it retrieves information and when it must say “I don’t know” instead of making up a plausible answer. Translate business goals into agent behavior: turn objectives such as “reduce waiting times” or “never share internal details with the user” into precise rules, flows and guardrails. Take care of the user experience: design tone, messages and channel adaptation (voice, chat, messaging) from the end user’s point of view, because perceived quality is part of the solution. Build with AI: use agentic coding tools such as Claude Code to build, read and validate what they produce, framing problems so that the tools execute them well and judging when the output is correct. Go live and iterate: monitor performance and KPIs, handle edge cases, check the quality and reliability of answers and keep improving the solution after go-live. You own the outcome. Guide clients’ decisions: act as the point of reference who helps clients make the right choices and turns them into implementation. Coordinate the right people: work closely with Product, DevOps, Customer Success and Technical Support to stay aligned, manage dependencies and remove blockers quickly. Enable clients: provide training, documentation and ongoing support so that clients can manage and optimize their AI Agents on their own. You will need: Agentic architecture judgment: you can design an agentic system end to end (framing it, deciding where and how to use tools and context retrieval, designing the flows) and explain why you made those choices. Reliability control: you know how to recognize and prevent hallucinations by setting boundaries and understanding when an agent should retrieve, answer or admit it doesn’t know. You treat answer quality as a design responsibility. A functional, product and UX mindset: you design from the end user’s point of view and act as a bridge between business and solution, translating a goal into concrete agent behavior. Hands-on use of AI to build: you use agentic coding tools such as Claude Code every day to move faster, framing problems for the tools to execute and reading and judging the output well enough to work autonomously. We don’t expect you to write production code yourself. Proven experience designing and running virtual assistants, agents or AI products, or a concrete portfolio of things you built yourself. Your track record matters more than your degree: in your application, tell us about an assistant, agent or flow you designed, the decisions you made, where it could fail and how you made it reliable. items.desc: About Us: ClearRoute is an engineering consultancy bridging Quality Engineering, Cloud Platforms and Developer Experience. We help enterprises reliably bring high-impact digital products to market faster, cheaper, and safer, working with technology leaders facing complex business challenges. We take as much pride in our people, culture and work-life balance as we do in making better software. We’re not just making better software. We’re making the making of software better. Collaborative, entrepreneurial and dedicated to problem solving, we bring the step change our customer need to sustain innovation. Our values challenge us to do the best we can for ClearRoute, our customers and most importantly our team. This is an opportunity for you to build the organisation from the ground up, use your voice to drive change and help transform organisations and problem domains. Role This role sits apart from our traditional cloud security engineering positions: it is centred on AI and agentic systems rather than infrastructure alone. You will test and secure AI use cases across an account, not one application or user set, building a broad, first-hand picture of how ClearRoute should approach testing, risk and governance for agentic AI. You will work across teams rather than within one delivery stream, owning the question of what "good" looks like for agentic security testing across the account, and helping ClearRoute build a repeatable, defensible approach that other engagements can adopt. The role is deliberately hands-on in its first phase: you will implement and run the testing yourself, so you understand the detail before asking anyone else to follow it. As that practice matures, the role shifts toward governance across the account, training and upskilling existing security engineers to implement and automate the strategy themselves, so agentic security testing becomes something the wider team can run, not something that depends on one person. Key Responsibilities Agentic Red Teaming & Adversarial Testing: Design and run red-team exercises against AI agents and agentic workflows, probing for prompt injection (direct and indirect), tool-call and argument manipulation, agent hijacking, memory/context poisoning, and privilege or credential escalation. Build repeatable evaluation approaches for non-deterministic systems, including how to test, measure and report against outputs that vary run to run. Define and own an approach for detecting, measuring and mitigating hallucinations in agent and LLM outputs, distinct from traditional functional-testing methods. Agentic Governance & Risk: Own agentic AI risk identification and governance across an account, not one application: build the risk view, the test strategy and the tooling recommendations that other teams can reuse. Map findings and controls to recognised external frameworks (for example OWASP's agent-specific risk taxonomy, NIST's AI Risk Management Framework Govern function, and MITRE ATLAS) so ClearRoute's approach is defensible and auditable, Distinguish and design controls for internal versus external (client-facing) views of agent behaviour, including how outputs are reviewed, sanitised or gated before release. Define rollback and incident-response procedures for agentic systems, so a compromised or misbehaving agent can be safely withdrawn or reverted. Track emerging regulatory expectations relevant to AI testing (for example EU AI Act provisions on adversarial and robustness testing) and translate them into practical test and governance requirements. Cross-Team & Organisational Scope: Work across delivery teams and accounts, acting as the connective view on agentic security testing rather than being embedded in one application or team Recommend and help select tooling for agentic security testing and monitoring, and advise delivery teams on how to embed it into their workflow Represent ClearRoute's agentic security posture with internal stakeholders and, where relevant, clients Train and upskill existing security engineers over time so agentic testing and automation becomes a capability the wider team owns, not one specialist Required Skills & Experience Must Have: Hands-on experience red-teaming or adversarially testing LLM or agentic AI systems, including prompt injection, jailbreaking and tool-misuse scenarios Practical understanding of how to test non-deterministic systems and how to detect, quantify and mitigate hallucination Working knowledge of agentic-AI-specific risk frameworks and taxonomies, such as OWASP's agent risk categories and MITRE ATLAS Experience with the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, including prompt injection and system-prompt-leakage risk categories Experience designing or applying an AI governance framework (for example NIST's AI Risk Management Framework) to translate identified risks into organisational controls Ability to operate across accounts and teams, building test strategy and tooling recommendations that generalise …

Lieu : Brest, France 
 Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance 
 Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. ​
 Nos engagements, vos avantages 
 Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée
 Un package de rémunération attractif
 Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes
 Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs
 Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu
 Votre quotidien 
 Votre quotidien 
 Afin de renforcer nos équipes sur notre site de Brest nous sommes à la recherche d’un Ingénieur Data Scientist (F/H).
 Vos missions, en collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe de la DI DAI :
 Accompagner nos clients dans leurs projets de valorisation de données en proposant des solutions techniques innovantes et pertinentes,
 Sélectionner, concevoir, implémenter et valider des solutions data science dans des domaines variés (Industrie, Spatial, Défense, Santé),
 Participer aux réflexions sur la gestion du cycle de vie des algorithmes et des données en production,
 Contribuer à l’intégration et au déploiement en production des solutions développées (conteneurisation, services managés, APIs),
 Assurer la veille technologique pour suivre les évolutions dans tous les domaines de l’IA (Machine Learning, Deep Learning, IA générative),
 Participer aux actions d’avant-vente à destination de nos clients (présentation de nos offres, qualification des besoins),
 Etre proactif et moteur pour communiquer et partager votre expertise
 Votre Profil 
 De formation Bac +5 minimum, vous possédez une grande maitrise des outils et concepts liés à la data et à l’intelligence artificielle (écosystème technique et littérature scientifique, maitrise du fonctionnement et de l’entrainement des algorithmes IA) et possédez de bonnes connaissances en ingénierie logicielle.
 Vous disposez des compétences suivantes ? :
 Vous maitrisez des langages de développement logiciel (Python, Spark, Scala, Java, C/C++ …) 
 Tensorflow, Keras, PyTorch, ScikitLearn ou Pandas n’ont plus de secrets pour vous
 Vous connaissez les principaux frameworks d’IA générative (Langchain, Ollama, etc)
 Vous avez de l’expérience sur une plateforme Cloud (Azure/AWS/GCP) et/ou sur une plateforme Data (Dataiku, Databrics). Des certifications sont un plus (GCP / Dataiku).
 Vous souhaitez mettre en application vos compétences pour la résolution de problèmes complexes
 Vous aimez transmettre vos savoirs faires et accompagner les utilisateurs dans la prise en main de vos solutions innovantes 
 Vous aimez travailler en équipe au quotidien et vous savez interagir en mode « Agile ».
 Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais est indispensable pour interagir efficacement avec nos équipes et nos partenaires.
 Alors ce poste est fait pour vous !
 Le mot de l'équipe 
 Dans le département Data & Intelligence Artificielle, nous nous intégrons pleinement dans la quatrième révolution industrielle portée par l'essor de l'IA et du big data. Nous déclinons ces avancées technologiques aux domaines critiques (Défense, aéronautique, santé, industrie) qui sont l'ADN du groupe THALES, afin de proposer à nos clients des IA de confiance et des pipelines de traitement de données sécurisés.
 Nous recherchons des collaborateurs enthousiastes et désireux de s'impliquer sur des projets data avec un fort niveau de challenge et d'exigence, mais aussi en capacité de suivre l'évolution des nouvelles technologies dans ce domaine en pleine mutation. Le partage est primordial pour que chacun développe ses compétences.
Thales, entreprise Handi-Engagée, reconnait tous les talents. La diversité est notre meilleur atout. Postulez et rejoignez nous !

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Zur Verstärkung der Abteilung "Operationelle Analyse und Studien" in der Organisation "Studien und Simulation" suchen wir für Airbus Defence and Space in den nächsten Monaten in Friedrichshafen einen
 Study Engineer - GenAI & Agentic AI (KI) (d/f/m) 
 Wir entwickeln militärische Simulationsumgebungen für Studien und Forschungsprojekte, welche für Analysen und zum KI-Training verwendet werden. Mittels Machine Learning/Deep Learning Ansätzen entwickeln wir KI-Verfahren zur autonomen Planung und Entscheidungsfindung unter unsicheren Bedingungen und in komplexen operationellen, militärischen Situationen.
 Wir suchen einen "Study Engineer - GenAI & Agentic AI (KI) (d/f/m)", der uns bei der Übertragung der Ergebnisse der akademischen Forschung auf reale Systeme unterstützt. Du arbeitest in unserer agilen Studienabteilung an interessanten Studien- und Forschungsprojekten der Bundeswehr, NATO, sowie Europäischen Union im Bereich Sicherheit und Verteidigung.
 Respekt, Teamwork und Kreativität sind die Schlüsselwerte unserer Abteilung. Bei uns findest du das richtige Umfeld, um deine innovativen Ideen voranzutreiben und in die Realität umzusetzen. 
 Dein Standort 
 Am Airbus-Standort in Immenstaad am Bodensee arbeitest du dort, wo die Zukunft von Connected Intelligence, Space und Air Power entsteht. In einer Umgebung, die Weitblick bietet, gestaltest du technologische Innovationen über Domänen hinweg.
 Unser Standort lebt vom Dialog: Auf dem Campus triffst du auf ein einzigartiges Netzwerk aus Experten für Satellitentechnik, militärische Luftfahrt, Cyber-Security, Künstliche Intelligenz sowie Combat Cloud und Ground Support von morgen. Auch unsere Zusammenarbeit ist geprägt von Dynamik – in agilen Teams widmen wir uns den komplexesten Fragestellungen, von KI-gestützter Erdbeobachtung bis zur sicheren Cloud-Architektur. Wer technologische Exzellenz und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit sucht, findet hier das ideale Umfeld.
 Unsere Benefits für dich 
 Faire Vergütung & Extras: Attraktive Vergütung und individuelle Zusatzleistungen, z. B. betriebliche Vorsorgemodelle, Mobilitätsangebote (bspw. Fahrradleasing) oder Mitarbeitervorteile bei kooperierenden Unternehmen gemäß unseren jeweils gültigen Richtlinien. 
 Zeit für dich (und deine Angehörigen): 30 Tage Jahresurlaub gem. Tarifvertrag (35h/Woche); Vereinbarkeit von Familie & Beruf (Gleitzeit, mobiles Arbeiten, Teilzeit, Jobsharing, Sabbatical) 
 Weiterkommen leicht gemacht: Ausgezeichnete Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und internationale, konzernweite Entwicklungsperspektiven 
 Wohlfühlen am Arbeitsplatz: Betriebsarzt; umfassendes Gesundheitsangebot (Sportkurse, Präventionsangebote, uvm.), Kantine und Cafeteria, Kindertagesstätte am Standort 
 Vielfalt verbindet: Arbeiten in einem diversen Umfeld, mit mehr als 140 Nationalitäten, in dem Austausch, Unterstützung und Vielfalt gelebt wird 
 Deine Aufgaben und Verantwortlichkeiten 
 Technische Leitung in der Entwicklung und Erprobung von KI-Ansätzen zur autonomen Planung und Entscheidungsfindung im militärischen Umfeld
 Verantwortung für die Umsetzung von einer Studie mit einem kleinen Studienteam in Zeit, Kosten und Qualität
 Vorbereitung und Durchführung von Kundenpräsentationen und Besprechungen
 Erstellung von Software Architekturen und sowie von Agentische KI-Frameworks auf modernen Container/Kubernetes Umgebungen und Verteilsystemen
 Führung des technischen Austauschs mit anderen Fachabteilungen und Projektpartnern (Industrie, wissenschaftliche Institute)
 Technische Angebotsleitung für ein/e Studie/Projekt (Scope, Zeit, Kosten)
 Praxisnahe Umsetzung und Erprobung in Kooperation mit anderen Fachabteilungen sowie industriellen und wissenschaftlichen Partnern (Universitäten, Fraunhofer Gesellschaft)
 Erforderliche Qualifikationen 
 Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium (Diplom/Master) oder Promotion der Informatik oder Ingenieurwesen mit Vertiefung in Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) und/oder Simulation
 Du verfügst über gute praktische Programmiererfahrung in Python und entsprechenden sowie Single- und Multi-Agent-Systemen. 
 Solide Erfahrungen im Bereich Simulationsentwicklung / Game Engines mit Python und/oder C++ (oder vergleichbar) wären von Vorteil
 Idealerweise, verfügst Du über gute praktische Erfahrungen im Software-Engineering (u.a. Erstellung von Software-Architekturen);
 Praktische Erfahrung im Umgang mit Container/Kubernetes/Docker Umgebungen und Verteilsystemen (z.B. Ray)
 Sicherer Umgang mit CI/CD-Umgebungen wie z.B. GitHub/Gitlab, PyCharm, Visual Studio, etc. (idealerweise auf Windows und Linux)
 Du hast solide Erfahrungen im Bereich des agilen technischen Führens von Projektteams; gute Kenntnisse im Umgang mit dem ATLASSIAN Toolstack (JIRA, Confluence) sind von Vorteil
 Nationale und internationale Reisebereitschaft
 Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse 
 Bei umfangreicher Erfahrung ist die Übernahme eines größeren Aufgabenspektrums möglich.

items.card: you will design, build, test and deploy AI-powered agents and intelligent automation solutions that help transform the way clinical and corporate services operate. items.desc: We are seeking experienced and innovative AI Agent Developers to join our growing Automation and AI team at Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust. This is a 12-month fixed-term opportunity funded through an approved investment to establish and grow the Trust's internal AI delivery capability. As part of this programme, the Trust has identified an initial pipeline of AI use cases designed to improve productivity, reduce administrative burden and support staff in delivering high-quality patient care. Working with Microsoft Copilot Studio and the wider Microsoft Power Platform ecosystem, you will design, build, test and deploy AI-powered agents and intelligent automation solutions that help transform the way clinical and corporate services operate. From supporting frontline teams with routine administrative activities to helping services access information more effectively, your work will contribute directly to improving the experience of both staff and patients. This role forms part of a newly established nine-person multidisciplinary team responsible for delivering end-to-end AI solutions. There are three AI Agent Developer positions available, offering a unique opportunity to join at the beginning of an exciting new journey. Successful candidates will help establish the technical foundations, reusable components and development standards that will shape how AI capabilities are delivered and scaled across the Trust in the years ahead. Be responsible for delivering AI agent solutions throughout the full development lifecycle, from discovery and requirements gathering through to design, build, testing, deployment and ongoing support. Working within the Trust's AI governance framework, develop AI agents, integrations and automated workflows using Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Dataverse & related Microsoft technologies. The role requires close collaboration with stakeholders across clinical, operational and corporate services to understand business challenges, analyse existing processes and identify opportunities where AI can deliver meaningful improvements. You will produce technical specifications, development documentation, testing evidence and deployment records, whilst ensuring solutions meet information governance, cyber security and data protection requirements. Support implementation and release activities, monitor the performance of deployed solutions, investigate issues and deliver enhancements where required. In addition, contribute to the development of reusable components, technical standards and governance artefacts that support the wider Automation and AI function. Work alongside business analysts, solution designers, change specialists & other developers, you will play a key role in establishing a sustainable internal AI capability and delivering innovative solutions that improve the experience of both staff and patients. Our ambition is to deliver excellent local and specialist services, to improve the health and well being of our patients, and provide a vibrant place for staff to develop, innovate and build careers. We aim to make the most of our skills and experiences so we can become the best we can be. As one organisation we will recruit the finest and retain more specialist staff due to more employment opportunities across our Trust For full details about this varied and rewarding role, please see attached job description. We look forward to your application. Please be aware that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a suitable number of applications.

What you will do: – Implement client features in Unity 6.3 (C#, URP, FMOD) for a cloud-streamed party
items.desc: Remote Games Project Based Magic Media is a pioneering media, entertainment and tech group powered by creativity and innovation. We have a physical presence in 15 countries and expertize in the areas of art, animation, cybersecurity, game development, software development, VFX and video production amongst others. We work with leading developers and publishers within the games and tech industry, providing support and solutions designed around individual needs and carried out by global experts. The ideal candidate will have solid full-time Unity programming experience in games. As a Mid Unity developer, you will build and maintain client features for a cloud-streamed party game played on a TV, with phones acting as controllers, under the guidance of the lead and senior developers. This includes development, coding, testing, and debugging. You will also estimate your own tasks and write technical documentation. What you will do: – Implement client features in Unity 6.3 (C#, URP, FMOD) for a cloud-streamed party game, working inside an existing codebase and the client’s SDKs. – Build gameplay and UI features such as challenge modes, trophy and progression screens, and themed content. – Build content authoring tools and add telemetry events. – Integrate audio in FMOD (events and banks) for assets supplied by an audio team. – Fix bugs, support client QA through alpha, regression and release, and prepare documentation. Your Profile: – 3+ years of experience as a Unity game developer. – Worked on at least one shipped game title. – Availability for daily working-hours overlap with Helsinki (EET/EEST). – A passion for video games. – Strong skills in Unity and C#. Unity 6 and URP are a plus. – Able to take a well-defined feature through to delivery, asking questions early when information is missing. – Familiar with performance bottlenecks and ways to resolve them. – Strong debugging skills. – Basic understanding of multiplayer concepts and client-server communication. – Willingness to learn FMOD, the client’s SDKs and the existing tooling. – Good communication skills in English, and good reporting and documentation skills. – Flexibility and ability to adapt to changing priorities. Desirable Pluses: – Experience with multiplayer, party or casual games. – Experience with FMOD or other audio middleware. – Experience building game tools or adding analytics and telemetry. – Familiarity with TypeScript or React. – Solid technical foundation (e.g. Computer Science / Maths Degree or equivalent). items.desc: PhD fellowship in climate and health epidemiology A 3-year PhD fellowship is available at the Work, Environment and Cancer group at the Danish Cancer Institute. The position We are seeking a PhD student to work on a large EU-funded consortium project, Understanding and Preventing Climate-Related Health Risks through Mediating Pathways (U-PATH) . Europe is the fastest-warming continent, yet evidence that separates direct heat effects from effects mediated by other environmental exposures, such as air pollution, aeroallergens, noise, and indoor overheating, is still lacking. U-PATH brings together 15 international research institutions to investigate how climate exposures relate to cardiovascular and respiratory disease, with a particular focus on the mediating role of environmental exposures. The Work, Environment and Cancer group’s main tasks in U-PATH include: coordinating the harmonization of epidemiological data from cohorts in five countries contributing data and analyses from a Danish nationwide cohort conducting measurement campaigns of indoor summer temperatures, which will be used to develop a model for indoor heat exposure assessment coordinating analyses of associations between long-term residential indoor and outdoor heat events and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease across the cohorts The Work, Environment and Cancer research group is a dynamic multi-national team of researchers dedicated to studying the effects of environmental and occupational exposures on the development of cancer and other diseases. Your main responsibilities Conduct indoor temperature measurement campaigns Contribute to developing a model for indoor exposure assessment Link climate exposure data to Danish residential addresses Generate analysis-ready datasets with climate and environmental exposures, health outcomes, and potential confounders for the Danish population Analyze associations between climate and environmental exposures and risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease, in collaboration with key U-PATH partners Write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals Present results at U-PATH consortium meetings and international conferences PhD enrolment You will be enrolled as a PhD student at a Danish university and supervised by researchers from the Work, Environment and Cancer group. Enrolment is subject to approval by the relevant PhD school, and it is a prerequisite for receiving the stipend that you are enrolled as a PhD student. Your progress as a PhD student will be assessed at regular intervals. As part of your PhD studies, you will be required, among other things, to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS and to undertake a research stay of 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. Qualifications Required A master’s degree (completed or nearly completed) in public health, epidemiology, statistics, or related discipline Experience in statistical programming, preferably in SAS and/or R A systematic and well-organized work approach, with strong planning and collaboration skills Excellent written and spoken English An advantage Experience with statistical analyses in quantitative epidemiological research Experience with large datasets and register-based data Experience with GIS software, such as QGIS Experience with contributing to peer-reviewed publications Interest in or experience with field data collection We offer An inspiring and dynamic working environment in an interdisciplinary research center (biologists, human biologists, public health scientists, medical doctors, data managers, psychologists, statisticians, etc.) where we work with many different epidemiological and biological topics. The research department regularly hosts interdisciplinary seminars with external lecturers on biological and epidemiological research areas and internal courses on relevant topics. Also, we have a Postdoc network that arranges regular meetings and seminars. Salary, pension, and conditions of employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish government and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). We offer canteen, fruit scheme, sports- and art clubs as well as physiotherapy. You will initially be employed as research assistants to allow time for enrollment as PhD students at the University. You are expected to write your PhD application with support from your supervisor. The Danish Cancer Society of course has a no smoking policy during working hours. Start date: The position is a 3-year full-time position and is open from January 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. More information For specific information about the project or the position, please contact Group Leader and Professor Mette Sørensen, mettes@cancer.dk, +45 3525 7626 Application and deadline Submit your application no later than 15th of November 2026 . The PhD project explores the dynamic relationships between people, places, and material environments and is situated within an emerging research agenda investigating how design thinking and planning practices can support circularity and sustainability initiatives in cities. This PhD position, funded by the project “Co-creating regenerative green-social infrastructures for urban circular economies” ( WeGrowCircle ) through the Driving Urban Transitions Partnership, is part of a new interdisciplinary thematic research initiative addressing Urban Social Resilience (USR) with particular attention to care ethics, participatory processes, and social innovation as guiding perspectives. The successful candidate will contribute to interdisciplinary research activities, empirical studies, and scholarly publications in close collaboration with other members of the USR initiative across the Department of Sustainability & Planning and the Department of Architecture, Design & Media Technology. The position further offers engagement in a wider research network spanning urban sustainability, innovation, planning, design, and architecture. The position is available from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter, and with employment in the Sustainability, Innovation and Policy research group. The duration of the position is three years. Research Focus The PhD project addresses the pressing challenge of developing urban social resilience in cities, with a particular focus on how social actors, relations, and practices can gain agency in resilience-building processes through inclusive, collaborative, participatory, and planning-based approaches across actors, organisations, and institutions. The project is grounded in a socio-material planning and design perspective, where urban resilience is understood as an emergent quality produced through interactions between social dynamics, institutional frameworks, and material and spatial configurations. Within this framework, the PhD project must in particular contribute to: establishing a shared conceptual and methodological foundation for the WeGrowCircle project, e.g. as a Resilient Urban Commons Framework mapping and analysing actor landscapes, relations, and key dynamics in the development of urban social resilience and regenerative green-social infrastructures (GSIs) developing and testing an inclusive co-creation process for GSI design, exploring stewardship and governance models for resilient and collective land management, evaluating how GSIs can improve biodiversity, circular practices, sufficiency, and social well-being; and generating evidence and recommendations for integrating GSIs into local planning, climate action and community practice. The PhD project may adopt different disciplinary perspectives, empirical focus areas, and methodological approaches within the broader field of urban social resilience and planning. At the same time, it is expected that the project will relate to and further develop the research environment’s work with socio-material approaches, participatory and interactive planning, as well as co-design and co-production in the context of urban resilience. Applicants are therefore expected to develop and outline a preliminary research proposal (1–3 pages) that presents their initial considerations regarding research focus, research design, and methodological approach in relation to urban social resilience within a planning and design perspective. Research Context The specific empirical context of the PhD project is closely linked to the WeGrowCircle project and thus mainly to the Aalborg Living Lab. However, engagement with one or more of the other three living labs (Brussels, Gothenburg, Bucharest) in the project is expected. Decision about which one(s) is intentionally left open at this point, and need not be considered in the application. Your Competences Applicants should demonstrate a strong interest in exploring how urban resilience is shaped through the interplay between social and material dimensions. items.desc: We are recruiting one doctoral researcher (3 years) to the AEGIS network AEGIS — Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets — is a European research and training network. It is funded by the EU through a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network, runs from 2026 to 2030, and trains 15 Doctoral Candidates (PhD students). The DN targets developing software-defined technologies that turn edge data centers from passive electrical loads into active, carbon-efficient and grid-interactive resources. The project has three layers: A programmable infrastructure layer gives safe, runtime-verified control of a site’s power electronics, cooling, and AI hardware. An intelligence layer reads real-time grid signals and turns a request such as “reduce power by 20%” into the detailed actions that hardware and facilities must take, without breaking service. A fleet orchestration layer coordinates many sites, even when they have different owners, using trusted and privacy-preserving methods, so the whole fleet can act as one Virtual Power Plant. Read more about the project and other participants here: https://aegis-dn.eu/ Your role: You will be working on “End-to-End Energy Modeling for Distributed AI Services”. To make carbon-aware decisions, both orchestrators and developers need to see the real energy cost of an AI workload. In this project you build analytical models and systems that make energy and carbon metrics visible. You will create compositional energy models that span the radio network, the transport network, and the datacenter hardware, and expose them through a fast query interface so any tool can ask, “what does this AI service cost in energy?” You will be responsible for: Developing compositional energy models for disaggregated radio (RAN) components, transport networks, and datacenter hardware. Building a low-latency query API that returns the end-to-end energy cost of an AI service. What you will deliver: Validated models with less than 10% prediction error on the Aalto and Ericsson testbeds. A query API that returns end-to-end energy-cost estimates in under 100 milliseconds. A doctoral dissertation that you will defend. Secondments: You will spend two research visits with partners in the network: Ericsson (Finland) — 3 months from around May 2028 (industry), with Tomas Mecklin: test the energy models on Ericsson’s infrastructure testbeds. TU Wien (Vienna, Austria) — 3 months from around May 2029 (academic), with Ivona Brandić: combine the digital-twin models with the end-to-end energy models. The position requires: Master's degree in computer science, communications engineering, telecommunications, or a related field (with a CGPA of at least 4/5) Experience (e.g. coursework, projects, etc.) in AI and machine learning, including understanding of various DNN architectures, training models, and applying them for different tasks Understanding of computer and telecom networks (for example RAN) Experience with empirical measurements (Prior work on energy or power measurement is strongly preferred) Data analysis and analytical modeling — identifying the features that drive system behaviour and building compositional or analytical models from measured data (an interest or aptitude here is enough; we don’t expect prior demonstrated experience) Good programming skills – you are required to provide a sample of your code during the recruitment process Fluency in written and spoken English. See https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering#8-required-language-proficiency for information on how you can demonstrate proficiency in English. This is required when officially applying for doctoral studies at the School of Electrical Engineering in Aalto University (within 6 months after starting in the job). Please note that you do not need official proof when applying for this job. If you are chosen for this position, you will apply for the study right in doctoral studies at Aalto University School of Electrical Engineering. Thus, please see the student information and admission criteria at https://www.aalto.fi/en/study-options/aalto-doctoral-programme-in-electrical-engineering. MSCA eligibility You must meet the following requirements: No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment, you must not yet hold a PhD. Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Finland for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited, unless as part of a compulsory national service or a procedure for obtaining EU temporary protection or refugee status under the Geneva Convention. Short stays such as holidays do not count. All nationalities welcome. The positions are open to applicants of any nationality. items.desc: L'école MIRA est une 'école d'ingénieur·e·s, accréditée par la Commission des Titres d'Ingénieur et reconnue par l'État. Implantée à Ajaccio et à Bastia, elle forme en robotique, intelligence artificielle, cybersécurité, marketing et innovation. Depuis 2010, sa raison d'être est de contribuer au développement économique et social de la Corse en développant les compétences sur l'île et en y ancrant les talents. Son équipe de recherche MIRA-Recherche, travaille sur la robotique interactive : elle étudie les usages pour intégrer l'IA, l'IoT, la robotique dans des interactions humain-machine utiles aux organisations (cobotique, jumeaux numériques, objets connectés). Le contexte Le poste associe des activités d’enseignement, de recherche, de formation professionnelle, d'animation d'ateliers et de représentation de l'école. Les activités pédagogiques. Les activités pédagogiques portent sur les programmes dispensés au sein de l’école. Les activités de recherche s’inscrivent dans le cadre d’un projet financé consacré à la transition des entreprises corses vers l'industrie 5.0 : une industrie qui associe robotique, objets connectés et intelligence artificielle tout en plaçant l'humain au centre des systèmes. Ce que nous proposons Un poste varié qui associe recherche appliquée avec des entreprises partenaires, enseignement en formation initiale et professionnelle, ateliers et représentation de l'école. L'accès au LabTech de MIRA : impression 3D, découpe laser, CNC 4 axes, atelier PCB, matériel IoT et Arduino, réalité virtuelle, drones et rovers. Un travail en réseau avec les partenaires de MIRA-Recherche. Une équipe à taille humaine et un cadre de vie à Ajaccio, entre mer et montagne. Avantages : Mutuelle Formation Vos activités Activités de recherche Concevoir les cellules robotisées des lignes de production : choix des robots et des effecteurs, préhension de produits variés, planification de mouvement, commande, sécurité des installations collaboratives. Intégrer robots mobiles et convoyeurs dans les flux internes, et spécifier le raccordement aux automates et aux systèmes de pilotage de la production. Valider les solutions en conditions réelles avec l’équipe projet. Rédiger les livrables et réaliser des publications. Proposer des sujets de stage et de thèse ; co-encadrer des doctorants, ou les diriger si vous êtes titulaire de l'HDR ; contribuer au montage de nouveaux projets. Activités d'enseignement Assurer des cours, TD, TP et projets dans le programme Ingénieur et dans le parcours CLIC. Encadrer des stages et des missions de fin d'études ; participer aux jurys ; faire évoluer les contenus de robotique industrielle. Intervenir en formation professionnelle auprès des entreprises et des salariés. Vous enseignerez dans le programme Ingénieur en Robotique & Informatique (titre d'ingénieur accrédité CTI, Bac+5), dans le parcours CLIC — Conception Logicielle, IA & Cybersécurité (Bachelor DIAC, Bac+3, et Master of Science BIHAR, Bac+5,), ainsi qu'en formation professionnelle. Les enseignements confiés seront définis avec la Direction des études. Domaines d'enseignement : robotique, automatique, informatique industrielle et robotique mobile, du cycle préparatoire au cycle ingénieur, ainsi que des enseignements scientifiques et de gestion de projet dans le parcours CLIC. Animation d'ateliers Animer des ateliers au LabTech de MIRA et avec les entreprises partenaires, pour des publics étudiants, professionnels et scolaires. Manifestations et représentation Présenter des démonstrations lors des journées portes ouvertes, des salons d'orientation et des événements de l'école. Représenter MIRA dans les salons professionnels, les conférences et auprès des industriels. Diplômes et expérience Doctorat en robotique, automatique ou mécatronique. Une expérience post-doctorale ou industrielle est appréciée. La qualification en tant que maître de conférence est recommandée. Une HDR est un plus. Expérience de projets collaboratifs avec des industriels ; une expérience de projets européens est un atout. Expérience d'enseignement dans le supérieur, de préférence en école d'ingénieurs. Compétences scientifiques et techniques Robotique, modélisation, commande, planification de mouvement, préhension. Cobotique industrielle et robotique mobile : intégration de cellules, robots mobiles autonomes, sécurité des installations collaboratives. Perception pour la robotique : vision 2D/3D appliquée à la saisie et à la localisation. Outils : ROS 2, simulation robotique (Gazebo, Isaac Sim ou équivalent), Python et C++ ; communication avec les automates et les systèmes de production. Qualités attendues Capacité à animer une équipe pluridisciplinaire et à travailler en collaboration avec des industriels. Sens pédagogique, goût pour la transmission auprès d'étudiants de Bac+1 à Bac+5. Autonomie, rigueur, aisance dans la relation avec les entreprises. Français et anglais courants (enseignement possible en anglais).

items.desc: CDI / Gard / YELLOH VILLAGE SIÈGE [CDI] Data & IA Platform Product Owner (H/F) Créé en 2000, Yelloh! Village est un réseau de franchise spécialisé dans l’hôtellerie de plein air haut de gamme. Avec plus de 100 campings en France, en Espagne et au Portugal, notre réseau s’appuie sur des femmes et des hommes passionnés, qui œuvrent chaque jour pour faire grandir la marque et accompagner nos établissements. Missions Au sein de la DSI, vous faites le lien entre les équipes métiers et data pour construire une nouvelle plateforme Data & IA Yelloh. C’est une création de poste, il faudra construire les fondations et promouvoir les nouveaux usages. L’ambition de la plateforme Data & IA est de fournir un puit de données fiable, multi sourcé, afin d’alimenter les processus de décisions et de pilotage de nos équipes siège et campings. L’IA doit aider à « faire parler » la donnée, et de déployer des agents intégrés au SI Yelloh pour automatiser des actions de commercialisation. Pilotes IA, industrialisation: cadrer les cas d’usage IA, validation avec des prototypes, conception de harnais Yelloh, mesurer la rentabilité, suivre les déploiements et l’amélioration continue. Votre environnement : Snowflake, BigQuery, Power BI, SQL, ELT/ETL, data quality, data governance, solutions d’automatisation et d’orchestration, IA générative et agentique. Les domaines : Pilotage commercial, marketing, relation client et opérations.
