items.desc: Entreprise Établissement d'enseignement supérieur, l'Université d'Orléans est présente sur 7 sites en région Centre Val de Loire. Elle compte 18 000 étudiant.e.s, 141 diplômes nationaux, 2000 personnels et 24 unités de recherche. Lieu d’exercice : Université d’Orléans – Laboratoire d'Economie d'Orléans (LEO) Prise de poste : Poste à pourvoir à partir de janvier 2027 Type de contrat/Statut : Post - doc, temps plein Poste Présentation du service/laboratoire : Le chercheur postdoctoral rejoindra le Laboratoire d'Économie d'Orléans (LEO) et travaillera en collaboration avec des partenaires académiques et institutionnels. L'environnement favorise la recherche de qualité, avec accès à des ressources informatiques performantes, à des données propriétaires en fraude, et à une équipe multidisciplinaire. Le laboratoire soutient la publication scientifique et la participation à des conférences internationales. Une attention particulière sera accordée à la confidentialité des données, à leur usage responsable et à la reproductibilité des résultats. Présentation du projet : La fraude financière génère des coûts majeurs, financiers comme sociaux, et évoluent constamment avec la numérisation et l'émergence de nouveaux canaux de paiement. Le projet développe des méthodes interprétables et opérationnellement pertinentes pour détecter la fraude dans l'assurance, les cotisations sociales et la banque. La recherche s'appuie sur des données volumineuses, hétérogènes et souvent sensibles pour identifier des comportements anormaux, des réseaux suspects et des schémas de fraude émergents, tout en maîtrisant les faux positifs et en préservant l'interprétabilité des modèles. Les travaux porteront sur la modélisation avec déséquilibre de classes, l'apprentissage (semi-)supervisé et sensible au coût, les méthodes de réseau et graphique pour découvrir les schémas coordonnés, ainsi que le développement de modèles explicables et robustes adaptés aux environnements régulés. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux stratégies adaptatives face à l'évolution des techniques frauduleuses et aux dynamiques temporelles. Missions : Nous recherchons un chercheur postdoctoral pour développer des modèles de machine learning et deep learning appliqués à la détection de fraude dans l'assurance, les cotisations sociales et la banque. Le travail comprendra le développement et la mise en œuvre de méthodes interprétables de ML/DL pour la détection d'anomalies, l'analyse et le prétraitement de datasets volumineuses provenant de secteurs financiers divers, des études comparatives des méthodologies de détection, la collaboration avec des partenaires industriels pour valider les modèles sur données propriétaires. Le candidat contribuera à 2-3 publications dans des revues internationales à comité de lecture et à des présentations en conférences majeures. Il disposera d'une autonomie scientifique significative, avec mentorat de chercheurs seniors et accès aux infrastructures du laboratoire. Profil Formation et expérience professionnelle : Doctorat (Ph.D.) en Data Science, Machine Learning, Économétrie, Finance, Statistiques ou dans un domaine connexe ; Expertise en économétrie, machine learning et deep learning, notamment en détection d’anomalies, classification et séries temporelles ; Solides compétences en programmation (Python, R, SQL) ; Expérience en analyse de données volumineuses et en feature engineering, ainsi que connaissance des méthodes d’IA explicable ; Une expérience en analyse de réseau ou de graphique est un atout ; Expérience antérieure avec des données d’assurance, bancaires ou de protection sociale, ainsi que des compétences en français, sont des atouts ; Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Dossier de candidature : un CV incluant la liste des publications ; une lettre de motivation présentant les intérêts de recherche du candidat et l’adéquation de son profil avec le poste (2 pages maximum) ; un article scientifique représentatif. L’UNIVERSITE D’ORLEANS C’EST AUSSI : Une université européenne, des valeurs partagées, un plan égalité professionnelle femme/homme, diversité et non-discrimination, inclusion, qualité de vie au travail et engagement dans la transition écologique Un cadre de travail respectueux de l’équilibre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle : Développement de ses compétences à travers une large offre de formation Accompagnement des personnes en situation de handicap et adaptation des postes de travail Télétravail possible selon nécessité et organisation du service (1 à 2 jours/ semaine) -57 jours de congés annuels - dont 10 jours de RTT - pour un temps plein actif dès la prise de poste Et des avantages … Activités sportives et culturelles Restauration collective Forfait mobilité durable (vélo, covoiturage) Prise en charge partielle des transports Aides et prestations d’actions sociales : aide à la famille, aux vacances et séjours pour enfants, Aides aux parents d’enfants en situation d’handicap …

items.desc: Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation. Sous la responsabilité fonctionnelle de Luiz ANET NETO (Maître de conférences du département Optique) vous assurerez le maintien en condition opérationnelle et l’évolution matérielle et logicielle de la plateforme vers le standard XGS-PON, développerez des activités de Machine Learning et d’apprentissage par renforcement profond pour l’optimisation autonome des réseaux, et participerez à l’industrialisation ainsi qu’à la valorisation des logiciels et des jeux de données ouverts. Consultez la fiche de poste détaillée ✔️ Compétences requises en technologies et architectures d’accès optiques (G-PON, XGS-PON), en programmation Python (et idéalement C/C++), ainsi qu'en environnements de développement logiciel (Git, Docker, CI/CD, Linux). ✔️ Expérience attendue en développement d'algorithmes d'apprentissage automatique ou profond, en architectures SDN (modèles YANG, interfaces RESTCONF) ou en intégration avec des piles 5G/O-RAN. ✔️ Qualités recherchées : rigueur, méthode, pragmatisme, fort esprit d'initiative et curiosité scientifique pour l’expérimentation. Goût prononcé pour le travail en équipe pluridisciplinaire et excellentes qualités de communication orale et écrite en français et en anglais. Titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master 2 (Bac + 5) en télécommunications, réseaux, informatique ou traitement du signal, ou d’un doctorat (Ph.D.) en réseaux optiques ou intelligence artificielle appliquée aux réseaux. POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE : Environnement exceptionnel de travail : Intégrez le campus d'IMT Atlantique à Brest (Plouzané), au cœur d’un pôle d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche d’excellence en technologies de l’information. Écosystème d’innovation stimulant : Collaborez au sein du Lab-STICC (CNRS UMR 6285) et du laboratoire commun Lab’Optic (en partenariat stratégique avec Orange Innovation et l’Institut Foton), au contact direct de chercheurs, de doctorants et de partenaires industriels majeurs. Recherche à forte visibilité : Contribuez à des projets d'envergure nationale et européenne (tels que le PEPR 5G Photonique) et participez activement à la production de publications et de jeux de données ouverts pour la communauté scientifique internationale dans une démarche de science ouverte. items.desc: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project (Full-Time / Part-Time) Location: Frankfurt Employment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are available Type of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 years Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13 The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level. The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine. The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow . The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners. Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis. Your profile Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience. Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar). Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design. Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus. Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch). Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask). Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets. Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible). items.desc: for english version, see below - Die Technische Universität Nürnberg (UTN) bietet eine inspirierende und interdisziplinäre Forschungsumgebung mit Zugang zu modernsten Ressourcen. Sie ist der ideale Ort, um zukunftsträchtige Entdeckungen zu machen und einen bedeutenden Beitrag zu spannenden Forschungsfeldern zu leisten. Promotionsstelle an der UTN im Bereich Mathematische Optimierung für Multi-Roboter-Systeme (m/w/d) Das Department Liberal Arts & Social Sciences bietet derzeit eine Promotionsstelle (vollfinanziert, 3 Jahre, 100 %, Vergütung nach TV-L E 13) in der von Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin geleiteten Analytics and Optimization Group an. Wir suchen eine hoch motivierte und qualifizierte Person zur Verstärkung unseres dynamischen und internationalen Forschungsteams. Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird Teil eines interdisziplinären Forschungsteams, das neue Ansätze für Multi-Agent Path Finding in großen robotergestützten Lagersystemen entwickelt. Die Stelle ist im Bereich der mathematischen Optimierung angesiedelt und umfasst eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus Robotik und Business Intelligence. Sie forschen unter anderem zu gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding, Optimierung unter Unsicherheit und optimierungsbasierter Konfliktlösung und bringen Ihre Expertise in mathematischer Optimierung in das interdisziplinäre Team ein. Die entwickelten Methoden werden sowohl in Simulationen als auch auf realen Robotersystemen evaluiert. Eine komplementäre, im Bereich Robotik angesiedelte Promotionsstelle wird in der von Prof. Dr. Wolfram Burgard geleiteten Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Group ausgeschrieben. Weitere beteiligte Forschungsgruppen sind die von Dr. Tanja Kaiser geleitete Multi-Robot Systems Junior Research Group, die von Prof. Dr. Johannes Thürauf geleitete Discrete Optimization Group sowie die Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Freimut Bodendorf. Ihre Aufgaben: Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird im interdisziplinären Projekt „Real-World Multi-Agent Optimal Path Finding under Uncertainty“ mitwirken. Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören: Durchführung innovativer Forschung zur mathematischen Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding in enger Zusammenarbeit mit einem interdisziplinären Forschungsteam. Entwicklung mathematischer Optimierungsmethoden, insbesondere gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierungsansätze, für die Pfadplanung von Multi-Agenten-Systemen und die Lösung komplexer Konflikte in realen Robotersystemen. Implementierung und rechnergestützte Evaluation der entwickelten Optimierungsmethoden, einschließlich ihrer Erprobung auf realen Robotersystemen. Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus der Robotik sowie der Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU, um Optimierung, Robotik und Business Intelligence miteinander zu verbinden. Veröffentlichung von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden internationalen Fachzeitschriften und auf renommierten Konferenzen sowie Präsentation der eigenen Forschung auf internationalen Konferenzen. Mitwirkung in der Lehre und Betreuung von Studierenden, z. B. im Rahmen von Lehrveranstaltungen, Abschlussarbeiten und Forschungsprojekten. Mitwirkung an Outreach-Aktivitäten und Kommunikation von Forschungsergebnissen gegenüber Wissenschaft, Industrie und Öffentlichkeit. Ihr Profil: Wir erwarten: Einen qualifizierenden Hochschulabschluss (M.Sc. oder vergleichbar) in Mathematik, Informatik, Operations Research oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet, einschließlich Natur- und Ingenieurwissenschaften Motivation, Engagement und ein hohes Maß an Verantwortungsbewusstsein Solide mathematische Kenntnisse und ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an mathematischer Optimierung Ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinärer Forschung Programmiererfahrung, z. items.desc: Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) has a vacancy in the Computer Security research group for a talented PhD student (m/f/x) on the subject of formal methods and design automation for cryptography and hardware security Job description Cryptographic protocols and secure hardware are increasingly deployed in settings where mistakes are costly and hard to detect, yet designing, optimizing, and verifying them still relies heavily on manual expert effort. In this PhD project, you will develop formal methods and design automation techniques for cryptography and hardware security, making secure systems both more efficient and more trustworthy. The position is part of the NWO Gravitation program Challenges in Cyber Security (CiCS), which brings together leading security research groups across the Netherlands. Possible research directions include (but are not limited to): Logic synthesis for secure computation. Paradigms such as multi-party computation (MPC) and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) have cost models very different from conventional hardware. You will develop new cost metrics for specific paradigms and platforms, together with synthesis methods that optimize circuits toward them. Computer-aided cryptography and hardware security. Security arguments for cryptographic protocols and their hardware implementations are still largely constructed and checked by hand. You will explore how formal methods and automated reasoning tools can support the design, analysis, and verification of cryptographic constructions, as well as hardware security properties such as resistance to side-channel leakage. Privacy-preserving formal verification. In many settings, a party needs to convince others that a hardware or software design meets its specification without disclosing the design itself. You will study how verification techniques can be combined with cryptographic tools such as zero-knowledge proofs to establish correctness and security properties of confidential designs. The exact focus will be shaped together with you, based on your interests and background. Examples of our recent related work include “Proving Circuit Functional Equivalence in Zero Knowledge” (ACM CCS 2026) and “Think Locally Before Computing Jointly: Efficient Secure Multi-Party Computation via Maximizing Local Processing” (IACR TCHES 2027). As a PhD student on this project, you will: develop the theoretical foundations of new methods, such as formal models, algorithms, and security proofs; implement prototype tools and evaluate them on realistic benchmarks; collaborate with researchers in the CiCS consortium and with international partners; present your results at international conferences and publish them in leading venues. You will be part of the Computer Security group at CWI, headed by Prof. Marten van Dijk, and supervised by Dr. Chenglu Jin. Requirements Candidates are required to have a Master’s degree in computer science, mathematics, computer engineering or a related discipline. A strong theoretical foundation (e.g., in logic, discrete mathematics, cryptography, or formal methods) and well-developed analytical skills. Programming skills, e.g., in Python and/or C++, and willingness to build research prototypes. Knowledge of formal methods (e.g., model checking, SAT/SMT, theorem proving), logic synthesis, secure computation (MPC, FHE, zero-knowledge proofs), or hardware security (including side-channel analysis) is an advantage. Preferable qualifications for candidates include proven research talent, an excellent command of English, and good academic writing and presentation skills. Ability to work in an international, interdisciplinary team, and interest in collaborating with partners in the CiCS consortium and abroad. Terms and conditions The terms of employment are in accordance with the Dutch Collective Labour Agreement for Research Centres ("CAO-onderzoeksinstellingen"). The initial labour agreement will be for a period of 18 months. After a positive evaluation, the agreement will be extended by 30 months. The gross monthly salary, for a PhD student on a full time basis, is € 3,115 during the first year and increases to €3,989 over the four year period. Employees are also entitled to a holiday allowance of 8% of the gross annual salary and a year-end bonus of 8.33%. CWI offers attractive working conditions, including flexible scheduling and help with housing for expat employees. Please visit the CWI website for more information about our terms of employment’, or go to the working pages of the NWO website Information and application All applications should include a detailed resume, motivation letter, list of your MSc courses and grades, copy of your Master’s thesis and preferably a list of publications. The deadline for applications is 31 December 2026. Evaluation of candidates will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. The starting date is flexible. items.desc: Your function We offer a PhD position on the physics of synthetic molecular motors and the machines built from them within the international consortium ‘Joining Forces for Human-Made Molecular Machines’. Scientific programme: Molecular motors are intriguing nanomachines that convert fuel to useful work and directed motion despite the large random fluctuations that are inherent to the molecular building blocks of our world. Over the past decade there has been a surge of new synthetic unidirectional rotary motors powered by light (2016 Nobel prize) that have enormous potential to actuate new types of designer molecular machines and materials. Now, it is time to use single-motor measurements to uncover how these motors can generate force and how they can efficiently move along tracks. Within this programme, we will take the next leap forward: to go from single motors to molecular machines in which motors work together to effectively transport cargo or perform dedicated tasks beyond the limitations of biological systems. In this PhD project , you will investigate the physics of light-driven synthetic molecular motors and of the transport machines built from them, using advanced single-molecule techniques. We will develop and apply single-molecule fluorescence microscopy and optical tweezers to quantify how human-made rotary-motor-based walkers translocate along DNA-based tracks. You will explore how multiple motors, for example interlinked walkers or motors on a surface, can cooperate to perform dedicated tasks. Specifically, your experiments will quantify how motor-track design and coupled motor operation in simple molecular machines determine speed, processivity and directionality. Together with the theorists in the consortium, you will thus link the thermodynamic performance of synthetic motors to molecular design principles and contribute to the development of the first generation of functional molecular machines. Your PhD project is embedded in a strong collaborative consortium funded by NWO-XL, with the pioneers of light-driven rotary molecular motors of Nobel-laureate Ben Feringa (RUG), with single-molecule experimentalists Iddo Heller (VU) and Jan Lipfert (UniA), with theoretical physicist Chase Broedersz (VU), and with theoretical/computational chemists Jocelyne Vreede (UvA) and Shirin Faraji (HHU). Your duties develop and optimize single-molecule experiments and instrumentation based on fluorescence microscopy and optical tweezers design, set up, and optimize assays to manipulate and/or observe individual light-driven motors and coupled motors along DNA tracks and/or within DNA-origami architectures quantify force generation, motion, and processivity of molecular walkers and transporters at the single-molecule level, as a function of motor-track design and experimental conditions analyze experimental data and connect results to theoretical models and molecular design in collaboration with the consortium’s theoretical and computational researchers collaborate closely with theorists, chemists and DNA-origami experts within the consortium and contribute to publications and presentations Your profile a master’s degree (MSc) in physics, biophysics, nanoscience, or a closely related discipline experience with experimental research, preferably in molecular biophysics, soft condensed matter, single-molecule fluorescence, force-spectroscopy, or advanced optics/microscopy experience or affinity with data analysis and scientific programming (e.g. Python, Matlab) strong motivation to work in an interdisciplinary research environment excellent command of English, both written and spoken We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. We believe that trust, respect, interest and differences lead to new insights and innovation, to excellence and a broader understanding. We stand for an inclusive community and believe that diversity and internationalisation contribute to the quality of education, research and our services. items.desc: Your job Are you interested in the role of mountains in the global hydrological cycle? And in what happens to downstream water supply when mountains change? Do you like working with numerical models? Then this PhD might be your next step! A large part of the freshwater that sustains human societies is generated in the mountains. The seasonal melting of snow and ice supports agriculture, industries, households and the environment downstream. However, mountainous regions are changing rapidly, as they are hit hard by climate change. The impact of these changes on downstream water users is poorly understood. Global hydrological models rarely account for complex mountain processes. However, understanding how mountain processes influence global water availability is important to address sustainable water use. We are looking for a PhD student who is interested in the link between changing mountain processes and increasing water use downstream. This position is part of the project ‘MountAInWater’ in which a consortium of international, interdisciplinary researchers collectively aims to answer the question How is the water supply from the world’s mountain ranges changing and which non-linear feedbacks may cause unprecedented societal impacts? As a PhD student at Wageningen University you will apply a large scale hydrology-crop model in river basins that are originating from snow and ice covered mountains. Your duties and responsibilities include: Analyse how missing complex mountain processes in global precipitation products and hydrological models affect water availability estimates. Quantify the importance of mountainwater for agriculture and ecosystems globally, by analyzing how meltwater flows interact with crop growing seasons and environmental flow requirements in basins with large irrigation demand and high meltwater flows. Run the hydrology-crop model in combination with mountain streamflow (from high resolution mountain hydrology models) for selected basins to analyse mountain water contributions to downstream river flow, agricultural water use, and sustaining ecosystems for hotspot areas. Using a global mountain reanalysis dataset to evaluate for all mountain areas globally their contribution to downstream river flows, agriculture and ecosystems. You will publish your research findings in high ranking scientific journals and present it at conferences. You will also be asked to contribute occasionally to education, by helping in the supervision of MSc students that work on their thesis projects, and supporting in courses. You will work here The research is embedded within the chair Water Systems and Global Change. You will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Hester Biemans, Dr. Manoj Khaniya and a third supervisor tbd. Your qualities You are / You have: enthusiasm for the research topic; a MSc degree in the field of Hydrology, Crop Science, Earth System Science, Environmental Science, Climate Science, or a related field; a MSc thesis related to quantitative assessment of water- and/or food security; demonstrated experience in working with large datasets and large-scale numerical modelling in context of global change; experience with scripting and programming, eg in R, Python or Matlab and the willingness to learn a new programming language (C); creativity in communication and visualisation of model results in maps and figures; some experience with numerical modelling on High Performance Computing Platforms is a pre; willingness to work in multidisciplinary and internationally teams; a high level of English, both oral and written. For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level. Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment. A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. Project description Project title : AI for Multimodal Biology and Microscopy The Computational Microscopy for Cell Biology (CMCB) laboratory, led by Assistant Prof. Juliette Griffié, is recruiting a highly motivated PhD student to develop next-generation generative AI approaches for multimodal biological data integration and interpretability. The proposed project focuses on developing AI strategies for the analysis of complex biological datasets, with a particular emphasis on microscopy. The PhD candidate will explore how representation learning and generative AI can be leveraged to uncover fundamental biological mechanisms from large-scale, multi modal and/or heterogeneous datasets. This PhD project sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, computational biology, and computer vision. It is designed for candidates excited about applying advanced AI methods to frontier problems in biology. Experience with generative AI or interpretable machine learning is highly desirable. A genuine interest in biology and interdisciplinary research is essential. The selected candidate will join an interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment composed primarily of physicists, engineers, biochemists and computational scientists. The CMCB laboratory scilifelab.se/researchers/juliette-griffie/ develops cutting-edge computational and AI-driven approaches for extracting biological insight from microscopy and multimodal datasets. items.desc: Stockholm Resilience Centre (SRC) is a leading international centre in sustainability science at Stockholm University. The Centre advances scientific understanding of the dynamic interactions between people and nature in the biosphere, trains the next generation of sustainability researchers and leaders, and engages in collaborations with change agents. It is a joint initiative between Stockholm University and the Beijer Institute of Ecological Economics at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. The SRC currently employs around 165 members of staff. More information about us, please visit: Stockholm Resilience Centre. The SRC aims to foster new generations of researchers and academic leaders through our Resilience Research School. The school equips students with a theoretical and practical foundation in Sustainability Science with a focus on resilience in social-ecological systems. Students are encouraged to develop new approaches that integrate methods and concepts from the social, natural and applied sciences. Emphasis is placed on developing student ability to define a problem, develop research methods, and communicate research findings within international scientific and science-policy discussions. Project description This PhD position is part of Mistra Finance to Revive Biodiversity, an interdisciplinary research programme hosted by the Stockholm Resilience Centre that investigates the relationships between biodiversity, nature, and the financial system. FinBio brings together researchers across sustainability science, ecology, economics, finance, and related disciplines with financial-sector and other societal partners to develop science-based, decision-relevant approaches for integrating nature into financial decision-making. The programme takes a systems perspective, examining both how finance influences nature and how changes in nature generate risks, resilience, and opportunities for economic and financial systems. We seek an independent and highly motivated PhD candidate to contribute to the development of next-generation approaches for understanding and managing nature-related financial risks. The project is based on the recognition that nature is not only affected by economic activities, but also plays a critical role in shaping financial risks and opportunities for building long-term resilience. Degraded ecosystems can amplify climate-related hazards such as floods, droughts, wildfires, and pest outbreaks, while healthy ecosystems can reduce vulnerability and strengthen the resilience of both societies and economic systems. The PhD research will focus on how nature-related risks and resilience can be integrated into financial decision-making, with particular emphasis on the real estate and agrifood sectors. The project will include systematically mapping of the mechanisms through which changes in nature influence economic activities and financial risks. Building on this foundation, the PhD candidate will develop research on how resilience perspectives can be incorporated into financial risk assessment to improve both the credibility and practical usefulness of nature-related risk analyses. The PhD will be a key member of FinBio’s research on risk and resilience which is led by Prof Beatrice Crona. The PhD research will develop a stronger scientific basis for understanding how ecological processes can amplify, transmit, or mitigate financial risks, and how these insights can be incorporated into financial risk assessment. The PhD research will focus on the real estate and agrifood sectors as case studies to contribute to 1) scientific understanding of nature-related financial risk and resilience and 2) the development and testing of methods, models, and decision-support approaches that can be applied in financial practice. In the real estate domain, this will involve investigating how nature-related risks and nature-based solutions influence property valuation, credit assessment, and financial stability. Within the agrifood sector, the PhD candidate will analyze how investors, lenders, and companies can promote more sustainable and resilient supply chains through governance mechanisms, incentives, and the monitoring of relevant sustainability indicators. The research is being conducted with FinBio partners, including various institutional investors, banks companies, and other societal stakeholders. The PhD candidate is therefore expected to contribute both to academic publications and to the development of practical methods, recommendations, and decision-support tools for the financial sector. Applicants should have an academic background in a field such as sustainability science, economics, finance, geography, environmental science, systems analysis, or related disciplines. The workplace is located at the Biomedical Centre (BMC) in Lund. We work closely with the Memory Clinic at Skåne University Hospital in Malmö, where several of our researchers also work clinically. We strive for a workplace that is developing and stimulating for all employees, and we work continuously to create conditions that promote well-being, development and participation. We safeguard both physical safety and the psychosocial work environment. What we offer Lund University is a public authority, which means that you will have special benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension. We also have a flexitime agreement that creates good conditions for work/life balance. Read more on the University’s website about being a Lund University employee, Work at Lund University Project Description The position is primarily associated with a five-year multicentre project (2026-2031) funded by the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) through a U01 grant for the clinical validation of the blood biomarker MTBR-tau243 in Alzheimer's disease, conducted in collaboration with Washington University in St. Louis, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Alabama at Birmingham. However, the work will encompass the activities of the entire research group and involve longitudinal data from several thousand participants in the BioFINDER studies, including blood and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers, PET and MRI imaging, cognitive assessments, genetics, and proteomics. The primary task is to plan and carry out statistical analyses for scientific papers and to compile data across projects. The duties include: planning and carrying out statistical analyses for scientific publications together with the group's researchers, for example regarding diagnostic accuracy (ROC analysis, cutoffs, calibration, prediction models) and longitudinal data (mixed models, time-to-event, etc.) compiling and quality-controlling analysis datasets from the group's databases across projects producing clear, publication-quality figures and tables from the data writing reproducible, well-documented analysis code in R contributing to the U01 project's statistical analysis plan and pre-specified analyses, together with the Principal Investigator and statisticians at the US partner sites drafting methods and results sections and reviewing the statistical parts of manuscripts providing statistical advice on study design, power calculations and choice of methods following methodological developments in the field and introducing new tools and ways of working in the group. Qualifications Requirements for the position: a PhD in statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology or another relevant field with a clear statistical focus. The PhD must have been awarded by the time the employment decision is made. excellent command of R, including data handling and programming of reproducible analyses. a strong ability to visualise data and produce clear, publication-quality figures. good knowledge of statistical modelling, in particular regression models, methods for diagnostic accuracy and analysis of longitudinal data. excellent command of English, spoken and written (English is the group's working language). great importance will be attached to personal qualities. We are looking for someone who is meticulous and structured, able to explain statistical methods and results to clinicians and researchers, service-minded and able to handle several parallel projects and deadlines. items.desc: DevSecOps Engineer - FlatPlan UK-based remote model Work hours: 10am–6pm GMT, Monday to Friday Summary FlatPlan is the leading Apple News technology and strategy provider, working with 230+ consumer publishers including The Atlantic, The Athletic, Vox Media and the Premier League. We're a preferred provider to Apple, helping the world's biggest publishers reach hundreds of millions of readers through Apple News and beyond. We're profitable, growing, and scaling sanely: a sharp team doing meaningful work at pace. The Role: We're hiring a DevSecOps Engineer to support our growth in building out and harden the foundations our platform runs on whilst having a close eye and mindset about security. This is a hands-on engineering role with a security mindset at its core. You'll own how we build, deploy, run and secure our platform: support the build of our future pipelines that ship our code, the cloud services it runs on, the way we keep it reliable, and the way we keep it safe. Security at FlatPlan is a shared responsibility and we want the whole team writing secure code, but you are the person who owns the standard, keeps us honest, and is accountable for it. We are looking for somebody to help us grow our pipelines, automation and cloud tooling deliberately as we scale, so there's real room to shape how we do it. When there's focused security or hardening work to do, you lead it: assessing what we run, closing the risks that matter, and raising the baseline. When that's in good shape, you keep adding value on the robustness, performance and reliability of the platform our publishers depend on. We expect you to be fluent with AI development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or equivalent) and to use them daily, for writing and reviewing code, automating work, and finding ways to ship faster and safer. What you'll own will include a mix of: CI/CD pipelines and deployment: building, automating and improving how our code ships Cloud infrastructure on AWS: configuration, automation, and sensible, secure operations Security across the platform: secure coding standards, the OWASP Top 10, hardening, secrets, and staying on top of vulnerabilities and updates Reliability and robustness: observability, alerting, and a steady pair of hands when an incident needs handling Making secure, reliable practices part of how the whole team builds Bringing AI assisted approaches into how we build, automate, harden and ship How we're setup We build primarily with JavaScript and TypeScript, using Node.js. We use a JSON format called Apple News Format for Apple News delivery, which we will provide training on. Our data runs on MongoDB, and we use AWS for our cloud services. We are building out our pipelines, automation and infrastructure as we grow, so you'll have genuine ownership to shape how we do it rather than inheriting a fixed estate. We're always open to innovation and opinions on the tooling and approaches that will serve us best, and you'll be supported by a team with a strong understanding of our current product and great ideas for the future. Why you should apply FlatPlan is a small, lean team with backgrounds at Stripe, New York Times Company and Apple. We're fully remote but intentional about connection: randomised social 1:1s, Friday socials, a virtual office and optional UK meet ups four time a year. We share knowledge openly and regularly, and genuinely care about each other. We are a profitable company, formed in 2019 and backed by TinySeed. Our relationship with Apple runs deep: we are Apple's preferred provider for Apple News, and following a period of assessment, a direct supplier to Apple. We want this team to reflect the breadth of the publishers and audiences we serve. We strongly encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds to apply. All qualified candidates will be considered regardless of race, gender, identity, orientation, disability or background. Requirements Must-haves: Significant commercial DevOps experience: building and running CI/CD pipelines, deployment, and cloud infrastructure in production Strong AWS: configuration, automation, and the security basics done well, including IAM, secrets handling and least privilege A genuine security mindset: fluent in secure coding practices and the OWASP Top 10, and able to spot and fix real risk across code and infrastructure Comfortable automating with infrastructure as code and scripting, and keeping systems robust, observable and up to date MongoDB, ideally Atlas, with a sense of how to secure, configure and operate it safely Able to read and work in a JavaScript and TypeScript codebase well enough to review it, secure it, and support the engineers building it Sound instincts for reliability and incident response: monitoring, alerting, and staying calm when something breaks Comfortable making technical decisions with minimal oversight, and bringing the rest of the team along with you Daily, practical use of AI tooling in your workflow …

Making things is no longer the hard part. Knowing which ad earns the click, which page earns the enquiry and what's quietly costing a client leads is. Designers with taste who use AI to ship are replacing designers who don't. We're looking for a designer who is passionate about design and about what it does for a business: the ad that stops the scroll, the landing page that converts, the website that ranks and generates leads. items.desc: Who we are Since 1843, The Economist Group has championed independence, excellence and openness, helping people understand and tackle the critical challenges shaping the world. Today, we are building on that legacy as a global media and information-services company powered by digital innovation, analytical rigour and evidence-based insight. Across our three businesses - The Economist, Economist Enterprise and Economist Education - we deliver trusted analysis and insights to individuals and organisations in more than 170 countries. United by a shared purpose to drive progress, we empower decision-makers to make sense of change and chart a course through an increasingly complex world. As a colleague, you will be part of a culture that values ideas, encourages ownership and holds itself to high standards. We invest in people who are curious, thoughtful and adaptable, whether they are launching new products, reporting on global events or harnessing emerging technologies such as AI to improve how we work. Here, fresh thinking is taken seriously, ambition is matched by integrity, and great work is recognised. Working across disciplines, geographies and perspectives, we are united by a commitment to innovation, excellence and creating meaningful impact. Want to discover more about life at The Economist Group? Follow @EconomistCareers on Instagram to discover the people, stories and opportunities that make TEG unique. The role The Economist is consolidating Product, Engineering, Delivery, Design and Quality into a single Technology organisation built around durable, cross-functional teams aligned to coherent product and platform domains. Alongside the accountable leaders who run each domain, a small number of Distinguished Engineers hold technical authority across them: they set architectural direction, own the hardest technical problems and raise the engineering bar, without line-management responsibility. Web is one of those domains. economist.com is where readers discover, subscribe to and engage with The Economist, and where advertising is delivered. The reader experience and advertising need to be designed together, so that each strengthens the other. items.desc: Job Description The Enterprise Machine Learning team drives organizational value through scalable ML solutions and data-driven insights, fundamentally changing how business decisions are made. We collaborate closely with stakeholders, applying the latest advances in machine learning and statistical modeling to create highly impactful outcomes. Our commitment is to advance the state of applied science and robust system design to enhance and expand our core business capabilities. Role Overview We've spent the past year consolidating and validating our revenue data, most signals now live in one place. The next step is building a customer intelligence layer: systems that dynamically learn which signals drive outcomes, adapt as the business evolves, and surface insights that change how we act. As an Applied Machine Learning Scientist, you will be the person who makes that happen. You will train models, design experiments, and uncover the patterns that connect customer behavior to revenue outcomes.Then ship those insights as production systems that the business relies on daily. You own problems end-to-end: from formulating the right question, to training and validating models, to deploying them and measuring whether they actually moved the needle, in a closed feedback loop. You will work alongside a team of AI/ML Engineers, Data Engineers, and Analysts as part of the Enterprise Data & Analytics department. Your focus is the science: understanding what drives outcomes, building models that learn from data, and turning that understanding into systems that work. Key Responsibilities Design, train, evaluate, and deploy machine learning models that predict and explain revenue-related outcomes, including churn, expansion, conversion, and customer engagement. Build and own end-to-end ML systems, from data preparation and experimentation through production deployment, continuous retraining, monitoring, and performance optimization. Develop intelligence from structured and unstructured data, applying statistical modeling, modern NLP, embeddings, LLMs, and deep learning where they create measurable business value. Design and run experiments to uncover the relationships between customer behavior, product usage, and business outcomes, translating model outputs into actionable insights. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and business stakeholders to identify high-impact opportunities, prioritize ML initiatives, and embed intelligence into decision-making workflows. Measure and maximize business impact by monitoring model performance, detecting drift, validating outcomes, and continuously iterating based on real-world results and feedback. This Role Is For You If… You have 3–5 years of experience in Applied Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of building models that deliver measurable business impact. You bring foundation in machine learning and statistics, with hands-on experience training models on messy, real-world data. You're comfortable dealing with label noise, class imbalance, feature leakage, data drift, and designing robust validation strategies. You are experienced in applying ML to both structured and unstructured data, including modern NLP techniques, embeddings, LLMs, or deep learning where they create meaningful business value. You have production-grade engineering skills, including Python, SQL, software engineering best practices, and experience deploying, monitoring, and maintaining ML models. You have pragmatic, product-oriented mindset. You get more satisfaction from shipping a simple model that improves a business metric than building a complex one with marginally better offline performance. You think in terms of business outcomes, user behavior, and measurable impact—not model sophistication alone. You proactively identify high-impact opportunities, form opinions based on data and user understanding, and continuously iterate on your work. items.desc: In the time it takes you to read this job description, RapidSOS will have handled ~1,380 emergencies. At RapidSOS, we are committed to using technology to build a safer, stronger future and working together to save lives. We're in an exciting phase of growth, welcoming new members from across the globe to our mission-driven, ambitious, and inclusive team. Our work is founded on our values of trust and safety , pioneering , urgency , and purpose over pride , all of which support a company culture where people can innovate, collaborate, grow, and, above all, make an impact. RapidSOS is the leading public safety AI company that unlocks mission-critical intelligence for emergency response. It harnesses artificial and human intelligence to fuse life-saving data from the world's largest safety network, which includes over 700M+ connected devices and 200+ global technology companies. This intelligence is delivered to 23,000+ federal, state, and local agencies, serving one million first responders. RapidSOS has supported over one billion emergencies in 16 countries, powering RapidSOS HARMONY, the first purpose-built AI for public safety, designed to save critical time by automatically detecting emergencies, unifying real-time data and video streams, and coordinating a faster, more effective response. Learn more at www.RapidSOS.com. What this role is about: Our Voice AI team is building the next generation of intelligent safety technology. We build AI agents that triage incoming alerts in seconds, relieve the burden on emergency telecommunicators by handling non-emergency calls, and provide real-time translation between callers and call-takers. As an AI Engineer on this team, you'll own core capabilities end to end—from model behavior and backend architecture to evaluation tooling. Every improvement you ship shaves seconds off a response, and in an emergency, seconds are what save lives. What you'll do: End-to-end product delivery: Own Voice AI agent(s) capabilities from problem discovery and rapid experimentation through architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, and measurement of impact across the real-time agent, APIs, web application, and cloud infrastructure. Improve conversational quality: Improve the caller experience—including latency, turn-taking, barge-in, speech recognition, multilingual behavior, protocol adherence, and transfers—using production evidence and reproducible experiments. Safety and reliability: Design fail-safe behaviors, strengthen service resilience and observability, and respond to production issues through contributing factors analysis, mitigation, and prevention. Evaluation and continuous improvement: Build and use automated evaluations, call-replay tools, production metrics, and controlled traffic trials to identify regressions, quantify trade-offs, and improve model and system behavior. Work across the full stack, from Python backend and AI model behavior to the React/TypeScript UI that customers and operators use to configure and monitor their AI agents. Use AI tools daily to move faster on code, testing, call analysis, and incident triage, while keeping full ownership of architecture, safety boundaries, and production decisions. items.desc: Job Description UE09: £63,606 - £78,469 per annum College of Science and Engineering / School of Informatics Full-Time: 35 hours per week Open-Ended (permanent) The Opportunity We are seeking current and emerging leading researchers in the field. The successful candidate will have a PhD (or be close to completing one), a strong research agenda, and the enthusiasm and ability to undertake original research, teach courses, and supervise student projects. We seek candidates with research interests in the development of cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence methods and models, particularly in the joint space of perception (e.g., computer vision) and action (e.g., interactive decision-making systems). We are interested in candidates motivated to establish and expand the principles underlying such methods and models in the context of high-impact application domains (e.g., robotics, health, environment, society, etc.). The candidate's research focus may align with the following, non-exhaustive, list of topics (in no particular order): Continual, open-ended, self-improving AI Agentic AI, world models, and generative models Embodied perception and action Learning from interaction and reinforcement Decision-making under uncertainty Long-duration autonomy Candidates should have a strong research track record. They should also demonstrate interest and ability to teach undergraduate (UG) and master's (MSc) level courses, and to supervise projects for UG, MSc, and PhD in areas related to their research. items.desc: Am Fraunhofer IAIS erforschen und entwickeln rund 360 Mitarbeitende individuelle Lösungen zur Integration und Analyse von Daten für unsere Fördergeber*innen und unsere Kund*innen aus der Wirtschaft. Künstliche Intelligenz, Machine Learning, Big Data, Multimedia Content Analytics, Information Integration sowie Unternehmensmodellierung und -analyse sind die inhaltlichen Schwerpunkte unserer Arbeiten. In der Abteilung AI Assurance and Assessments (AAA) operationalisieren wir KI-Vertrauenswürdigkeit entlang von drei Schritten: Wir analysieren Anforderungen an KI-Systeme aus Gesetzen und Standards. Wir setzen diese Anforderungen um, indem wir technische Absicherungsmethoden für KI-Systeme entwickeln und diese auf organisatorischer Ebene durch effektive KI-Governance Mechanismen komplettieren. Wir entwickeln Prüfkriterien und Testverfahren für KI-Systeme und forschen zu der Frage, wie sich solche Prüfungen und Tests automatisieren lassen. Hierbei beschäftigen uns Fragestellungen wie: Wie lassen sich a priori inkommensurable KI-Risiken, etwa die Verletzung von Persönlichkeitsrechten und Safety-Risiken zu einem Gesamtrisiko aggregieren? Wie lassen sich die Unsicherheiten von Transformer-Modellen messen? Welche Controls in KI-Managementsystemen operationalisieren den AI Act? Wie lassen sich KI-Prüfworkflows automatisieren? Was sind die besten Redteaming Ansätze, um die Safeguards von LLMs zu testen? Wie lassen sich KI-Agenten im Betrieb absichern? Bei Fraunhofer IAIS zu arbeiten, heißt unternehmerisches Denken mit Spitzenforschung zu verbinden: Unsere Abteilung AAA hat weltweit Kunden, die von großen Technologiekonzernen bis hin zu Start-ups reichen. Auch viele Behörden zählen zu unseren Auftraggebern. Gleichzeitig entstehen aus unserer Forschung wissenschaftliche Publikationen und Doktorarbeiten. Unser interdisziplinäres Team hat Abschlüsse in Informatik, Naturwissenschaften, Rechtswissenschaften und Psychologie und freut sich auf Sie! Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung Übersetzung von regulatorischen Vorgaben, wie etwa der KI-Verordnung, in technische Anforderungen an KI-Systeme Konzeption und Entwicklung von technischen Lösungen zur Absicherung von KI-Systemen Konzeption und Entwicklung von KI-Governance Frameworks Konzeption und Durchführung von KI-Prüfungen für konkrete Use Cases Entwicklung von Methoden zur Messung und Quantifizierung von Unsicherheiten in KI-Modellen (z. B. Transformer-Architekturen) Durchführung von Redteaming- und Stresstests zur Absicherung von LLMs und KI-Agenten im produktiven Einsatz Automatisierung von KI-Prüf- und Testworkflows Beratung von Kund*innen aus Wirtschaft und öffentlicher Verwaltung zur regulatorischen Einordnung und Absicherung ihrer KI-Systeme Hiermit bringen Sie sich ein Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master, Diplom) der Informatik, Physik oder Mathematik mit sehr gutem Abschluss an einer Universität mit internationalem Renommee, gerne mit Promotion. Bei guter Passung zu einem der oben genannten Themen kommen auch andere Abschlüsse (z.B. Rechtswissenschaften, Psychologie) in Betracht Sehr gute Vorkenntnisse in den Bereichen Maschinelles Lernen, Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) und Agentische KI Sehr gute Kenntnisse zu Programmierung (insb. Python und ML-Frameworks with pytorch und tensorflow) und technischer Implementierung (Docker/Podman und Containerisierung, Azure, AWS oder andere Cloudprovider, Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD) und im Umgang mit Agent Frameworks/Harnesses (z.B. ClaudeCode, OpenAI Codex oder LangGraph) oder KI-Regulierung und Standardisierung (KI-Recht, insb. AI Act, internationale Standardisierung bei ISO, IEC und ITU, europäische Standardisierung bei CEN, CENELEC, ETSI, harmonisierte Normen) Exzellente analytische Fähigkeiten und Freude an abstraktem Denken Hohe Belastbarkeit sowie die Bereitschaft, sich schnell in neue Sachverhalte einzuarbeiten Freude daran, komplizierte technische Zusammenhänge für unterschiedliche Stakeholder aufzubereiten Ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative und Hands-on Mentalität Strukturiertes Arbeiten und professionelles Auftreten Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und Englischkenntnisse (beides mind. auf Niveau C1) Bitte gehen Sie in ihrem Anschreiben darauf ein, welche Themenschwerpunkte der Abteilung AAA Sie besonders interessieren, welche Vorerfahrungen Sie hierfür mitbringen, was Sie bei Fraunhofer IAIS erreichen möchten und warum wissenschaftliche Exzellenz und unternehmerisches Talent in ihrer Person vereint sind. Was wir für Sie bereithalten Wir bieten Ihnen vielfältige Angebote für Ihre persönliche Weiterbildung in den Bereichen Führung, Kommunikation, Projektmanagement, Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie, Gesundheit, Kultur und Sport. Die Förderung der Chancengerechtigkeit unserer Mitarbeitenden ist ein wichtiges Ziel von Fraunhofer. Wir fördern die berufliche Entwicklung von Frauen in unserem Institut und ermutigen sie nachdrücklich, sich zu bewerben. Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen …

items.desc: Description Du Poste leboncoin is France's leading classifieds platform for peer-to-peer transactions, the market leader in real estate and automotive, and a key player in jobs and holiday rentals. Every month, leboncoin is the go-to platform for 28 million French users who value the breadth of its listings and the simplicity of everyday transactions. At leboncoin, data is at the heart of every decision. By joining the Recommerce Data Analytics team, you will directly contribute to accelerating the growth of the Recommerce business through analytical and predictive models with a strong business impact. Your scope: Recommerce The Recommerce scope covers all physical goods bought and shipped via leboncoin (electronics, books, cultural products, home décor, etc.). It is a fast-growing market, rooted in circular economy trends, with strong challenges around profitability, user retention, and logistics optimisation. The key challenges of this scope are: Measuring and maximising the long-term value (LTV) of buyers and sellers Understanding the true incrementality of marketing, CRM and promotional actions Predicting and optimising logistics costs and delivery times You will join a Data Analytics team of 8+ Data Analysts and 2 Data Engineers, working closely together on the Recommerce scope. Exigences du poste Minimum 6 years of experience as a Data Scientist Strong expertise in causal inference and experimentation (A/B test design and analysis) Proficiency in Python and SQL; hands-on experience with Databricks and Airflow is a plus Experience in predictive modelling (ML, segmentation, time series) Ability to translate complex results into actionable recommendations for non-technical stakeholders Curiosity and drive for concrete business impact Autonomy, rigour and strong analytical mindset Fluent in English Fluent in French Responsabilités liées au poste Incrementality measurement and causal analysis : Design methodologies to measure the incrementality of promotional initiatives Conduct exploratory and correlation analyses on historical data (revenue, GMV, supply/demand indicators…) to inform re-pricing and promotional initiatives decisions Strengthen performance measurement with forecasting models and robust baseline definition LTV (Lifetime Value) and segmentation : Identify highest-LTV segments and its drivers to improve prioritization of CRM campaigns and promotional initiatives Compute CAC/LTV for CRM Introduce and test a trajectory-based user segmentation to react quickly to decline and churn in the top buyer and seller segments Prototyping and Discovery : Collaborate with Product MLE and DS on prototyping IA features (weight suggestion, delivery times…) Run exploratory analysis around improving sell-through (= time between an ad listing and its sale) Avantages du poste Company health insurance 50% reimbursement of your public transport pass 25 days of annual leave and 12 RTT days (additional rest days) A Swile meal card worth €9 per day At leboncoin, we believe that diversity in backgrounds, experiences and perspectives is essential. This commitment is reflected in our recruitment process: we assess every application solely on the basis of skills, experience and motivation, without any form of discrimination. If you need any specific accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know. We’ll be happy to support you.

items.desc: Що варто знати про SKELAR? Це венчур-білдер — іншими словами, компанія, яка будує компанії. З нами фаундери створюють consumer-бізнеси, які стають лідерами на глобальних ринках EdTech, Mental health, Petcare, FashionTech та інших. Скеларівці будують tech-продукти, які здобувають відзнаки від Product Hunt, The Webby Awards та отримують тисячі позитивних відгуків на TrustPilot. Загалом tech-продуктами наших бізнесів користуються 10+ млн людей у світі. Усе завдяки сильним командам, бо наші спеціалісти — це ключова цінність SKELAR. Для професійної реалізації ми створили середовище з експертизою та необмеженими можливостями — і шукаємо тих, хто прагне викликів. Мене звати Віталій, я Marketing Design Lead у Dressly. Зараз я шукаю людину в свою команду, яка підсилить наш AI-напрям своїми знаннями, досвідом та бажанням експериментувати. Нам потрібна людина, яка не просто генерує відео по короткому промпту, а вміє створювати сильний візуальний контент, шукати нові підходи та впливати на бізнес-метрики через якісні AI-креативи. Про проєкт та твою роль: Dressly — це fashion-tech продукт, де ми допомагаємо користувачам краще підбирати одяг та стилістичні рішення за допомогою AI. У маркетинг-команді ми активно використовуємо AI-інструменти у виробництві performance creatives: від генерації реалістичних сцен, AI-креаторів та fashion-футажів до адаптації креативів під різні ринки, локалі та формати. Виклики, які чекають на тебе: Генерація відео та зображень на основі сценаріїв, робота з композицією, світлом, стилем, реалістичністю та емоційним тоном кадру. Написання структурованих промптів із розумінням руху камери, поведінки персонажа, атмосфери, fashion-візуалу та задачі конкретного креативу. Створення реалістичних AI-футажів для рекламних відео: fashion-сцени, lifestyle-кадри, AI-креатори, try-on/wardrobe/content-style scenes. Збирання окремих AI-генерацій у цілісні відео, робота з динамікою, таймінгами, ритмом та логікою відеоряду. Адаптація AI-контенту під різні мови та ринки, робота з lipsync та візуальною консистентністю персонажів. Що очікуємо від тебе: Досвід роботи з Kling, Veo, Seedance, GPT Image, NanoBanana, HeyGen, ElevenLabs або іншими AI-інструментами. Ти відчуваєш ритм, динаміку, монтаж та розумієш, як з окремих AI-кадрів зібрати відео, яке виглядає цілісно і може працювати в performance marketing. Ти розумієш принципи генерації, prompt engineering, ітеративність та вмієш доводити результат до стабільного й якісного рівня. Ти не чекаєш покрокових інструкцій, можеш самостійно розібратись у задачі, запропонувати рішення, протестувати кілька підходів і довести ідею до фінального результату. Тобі цікаво не просто створити якісне відео, а зрозуміти, чому один креатив може спрацювати краще за інший. У SKELAR ми побудували середовище для професійної самореалізації: SKELAR Platform. Це операційне ядро венчур-білдера, що допомагає фаундерам швидше проходити шлях від нуля до одиниці. Так команди бізнесів фокусуються на продукті — а 10+ команд в складі Platform закривають функції Legal, Finance, HR, Admin, Talent Acquisition, Employer Branding, IT та інші. Нетворк та обмін досвідом як частина культури. Серед наших колег — кофаундери, які запустили не один бізнес, а також найсильніші спеціалісти на ринку. Тож ми маємо доступ до необхідної експертизи на відстані витягнутої руки. Ексклюзивна доменна освіта. Ми створили власні навчальні програми для тіммейтів на вибір — від 2-місячної школи для менеджерів-початківців до інтенсивів про AI та професійних клубів з розробки, продакт-менеджменту тощо. Вплив на системну допомогу Україні. Маємо благодійний фонд SKELAR foundation, який створили самі скеларівці — і завдяки кожному співробітнику втілюємо важливі соціальні проєкти. Наприклад, заснували перший у Європі акселератор для ветеранів і формуємо майданчик для підтримки ветеранів на рівні держави. Екосистема для продуктивної роботи. Для скеларівців створені простори, які надихають на результат — з власним спортзалом, скеледромом, зеленими зонами Bali та бібліотеками. У спейсах, де сервіс, безпека та комфорт синхронізовані з темпом зростання команд, отримуємо вау-досвід та працюємо ефективніше. Більше розповімо на нашій зустрічі-знайомстві. Запрошуємо будувати the next big everything у SKELAR разом!

items.desc: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Trainers Network – Arabic based in Poland. Join a global network of language professionals and culturally aware contributors helping shape the future of artificial intelligence. In this flexible, remote opportunity, you can contribute to projects that improve the accuracy, relevance, and inclusivity of AI systems. Depending on your skills and availability, you may work on text, image, or audio annotation, content evaluation, and prompt creation. Your Arabic language expertise and cultural understanding will help make AI-generated content more natural, reliable, and representative of diverse communities. Projects vary in scope and duration, offering opportunities to gain experience with emerging AI technologies while working on your own terms. This is a talent network opportunity rather than an active job opening, meaning you will be contacted when a suitable project becomes available. Before each project begins, you will receive clear information about the tasks, timeline, and compensation so you can decide whether it fits your interests and availability. Accountabilities Responsibilities As a contributor to the AI Trainers Network, you will support projects designed to improve AI performance, language understanding, and content quality. Depending on the project requirements and your areas of expertise, your responsibilities may include: Annotating and labeling text, images, or audio to help train and improve AI models. Evaluating search results, advertisements, and chatbot responses for accuracy, relevance, quality, and usefulness. Creating, testing, and refining prompts to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs). Reviewing AI-generated content to ensure linguistic accuracy, natural Arabic expression, and cultural appropriateness. Identifying errors, inconsistencies, and potentially misleading or unsuitable content in AI outputs. Applying project-specific guidelines and quality standards while maintaining consistency and attention to detail. Contributing feedback that helps develop safer, more inclusive, and human-centered AI systems. Managing assigned tasks independently and meeting project deadlines according to agreed requirements and availability. Requirements We are looking for detail-oriented, curious, and adaptable contributors who are interested in language, technology, and the development of AI systems. The ideal candidate combines strong Arabic language skills with the ability to evaluate information critically and work independently in a digital environment. Native or near-native fluency in Arabic, with a strong understanding of grammar, vocabulary, and linguistic nuances. Current residence in Poland for this opportunity. Good English proficiency to understand project instructions and communicate effectively. Comfort using digital tools, online platforms, and web-based applications. Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify linguistic, factual, and contextual inconsistencies. Good analytical and critical-thinking skills, particularly when evaluating content for accuracy and relevance. Cultural awareness and an understanding of Arabic-speaking communities, communication styles, and regional language variations. Ability to follow detailed guidelines, work independently, and deliver consistent, high-quality results. Curiosity about artificial intelligence, language technologies, and how human feedback can improve AI systems. Flexibility to participate in projects of varying durations and complexity, depending on your availability. items.desc: Job Description The Enterprise Machine Learning team drives organizational value through scalable ML solutions and data-driven insights, fundamentally changing how business decisions are made. We collaborate closely with stakeholders, applying the latest advances in machine learning and statistical modeling to create highly impactful outcomes. Our commitment is to advance the state of applied science and robust system design to enhance and expand our core business capabilities. Role Overview We've spent the past year consolidating and validating our revenue data, most signals now live in one place. The next step is building a customer intelligence layer: systems that dynamically learn which signals drive outcomes, adapt as the business evolves, and surface insights that change how we act. As an Applied Machine Learning Scientist, you will be the person who makes that happen. You will train models, design experiments, and uncover the patterns that connect customer behavior to revenue outcomes.Then ship those insights as production systems that the business relies on daily. You own problems end-to-end: from formulating the right question, to training and validating models, to deploying them and measuring whether they actually moved the needle, in a closed feedback loop. You will work alongside a team of AI/ML Engineers, Data Engineers, and Analysts as part of the Enterprise Data & Analytics department. Your focus is the science: understanding what drives outcomes, building models that learn from data, and turning that understanding into systems that work. Key Responsibilities Design, train, evaluate, and deploy machine learning models that predict and explain revenue-related outcomes, including churn, expansion, conversion, and customer engagement. Build and own end-to-end ML systems, from data preparation and experimentation through production deployment, continuous retraining, monitoring, and performance optimization. Develop intelligence from structured and unstructured data, applying statistical modeling, modern NLP, embeddings, LLMs, and deep learning where they create measurable business value. Design and run experiments to uncover the relationships between customer behavior, product usage, and business outcomes, translating model outputs into actionable insights. Partner closely with Product, Engineering, and business stakeholders to identify high-impact opportunities, prioritize ML initiatives, and embed intelligence into decision-making workflows. Measure and maximize business impact by monitoring model performance, detecting drift, validating outcomes, and continuously iterating based on real-world results and feedback. This Role Is For You If… You have 3–5 years of experience in Applied Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, with a track record of building models that deliver measurable business impact. You bring foundation in machine learning and statistics, with hands-on experience training models on messy, real-world data. You're comfortable dealing with label noise, class imbalance, feature leakage, data drift, and designing robust validation strategies. You are experienced in applying ML to both structured and unstructured data, including modern NLP techniques, embeddings, LLMs, or deep learning where they create meaningful business value. You have production-grade engineering skills, including Python, SQL, software engineering best practices, and experience deploying, monitoring, and maintaining ML models. You have pragmatic, product-oriented mindset. You get more satisfaction from shipping a simple model that improves a business metric than building a complex one with marginally better offline performance. You think in terms of business outcomes, user behavior, and measurable impact—not model sophistication alone. You proactively identify high-impact opportunities, form opinions based on data and user understanding, and continuously iterate on your work. Je werkt met de nieuwste ontwikkelingen binnen het Microsoft AI-ecosysteem, waaronder Copilot Studio, Power Platform en Azure AI, en krijgt volop ruimte om te experimenteren en jezelf verder te ontwikkelen binnen agentic AI. Je ontdekt waar AI het verschil kan maken en vertaalt deze use-cases naar slimme agents die medewerkers ondersteunen en werkzaamheden eenvoudiger en efficiënter maken. Je bent betrokken van het eerste idee en prototype tot het bouwen, testen en doorontwikkelen van de agent. Crediamo che l'Intelligenza Artificiale stia ridisegnando il perimetro della sicurezza: agenti autonomi, LLM e sistemi decisionali intelligenti stanno entrando nei processi core delle aziende, e con loro nascono superfici d'attacco che non esistevano fino a ieri.
