items.desc: About Immunara Immunara is an AI biology lab building biological superintelligence. We're developing biological foundation models that learn how human biology works, and AI agents that reason over biological data to accelerate scientific discovery. Understanding disease means connecting what happens across molecules, cells, tissues, organs and patients. Today, much of that knowledge is fragmented and captured in forms that AI cannot readily interpret or reason over. We believe AI can bring these pieces together to reveal biology that existing approaches cannot. Our Approach We're building foundation models trained on large, proprietary, multimodal human datasets to model disease and predict how biological systems respond to interventions. Alongside this, we're developing AI agents trained through reinforcement learning to reason over data and models, generate hypotheses and design experiments. Our ambition is to build AI systems that can understand and discover biology - radically improving how we develop new treatments. We've raised a large funding round from leading Silicon Valley investors to achieve this goal. About the role We’re looking for a Founding Operator with a scientific background, commercial instincts and a strong bias to action. Someone who can wear many hats and make things happen. You’ll work directly with the founders on whatever matters most to the business. One week, you might map the global biobank landscape, find the right decision-makers and run outreach. The next, you might refine our GTM strategy, build a customer deck, represent Immunara at an industry event, help close a candidate or fix an operational process that's slowing the team down. You'll move between strategy and execution constantly. What you'll do Build partnerships - Source biobanks, hospitals and research institutions. Find the right people, execute on outreach and drive opportunities forward with the founders and scientific team. GTM - Map markets, identify customers, test commercial hypotheses and turn research into a focused GTM strategy. Get into the details of who buys, what they need and how we reach them. Create materials that win business - Build sharp customer decks, partnership proposals, briefs and follow-up materials. Translate complex science and technology into a clear reason to work with us. Represent the company - Attend relevant conferences and industry events, build relationships and turn conversations into concrete next steps. Help build the team - Help source exceptional people, support outreach and interviews, and keep hiring processes moving. Make the company run better - Take charge of operational processes across the business. Remove bottlenecks and build systems that work as we grow. What we're looking for You understand the science. You have a background in biology, medicine, bioengineering or a related field. You can engage with scientific ideas and communicate credibly with technical people. You've operated in a fast-paced environment. You have experience at MBB, in investment banking or at a high-growth startup. You default to action. You can turn an incomplete brief into a sensible first move, you have high agency and are comfortable with ambiguity. You have high standards and low ego. You care about the quality of the work. No task is beneath you if it moves the company forward. You want responsibility. You’re looking for a steep learning curve, proximity to consequential decisions and the chance to build something substantial. What’s in it for you We want Immunara to the best place in the world to do ambitious AI biology work. Early hires will receive exceptional support and significant ownership. Benefits include: Competitive, top-of-market compensation. Significant equity package to share in the upside of building a category-defining company. Comprehensive private medical & dental coverage. A significant budget to purchase best-in-class equipment, research tooling, software, and the infrastructure you need to do your best work. Access to the compute and petabytes of proprietary biomedical data required to train ambitious models. Opportunities to attend leading AI, biology, and scientific conferences - fully-funded. Regular team meals, a stocked office, and a working environment designed for elite perfotmance. Flexible time off with no strict limits.

items.desc: The Northern Care Alliance is delighted to offer an opportunity to join our Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) team. The post holder will be a registered nurse with leadership experience and significant expertise in Infection Prevention and Control. They will be able to demonstrate successful service improvement initiatives and possess an in-depth understanding of the partnerships and services that directly impact IPC. The post holder will act as deputy to the Band 7 and Lead Nurse when required and provide senior support to IPC staff across the care organisations. They will be expected to work flexibly across NCA sites, including OCO, SCO, BCO, RCO and Community services, depending on the needs of the service. This may require cross-site working to ensure the delivery of a safe, effective and responsive IPC service across the NCA. The successful candidate will be expected to develop practical and sustainable solutions, provide expert infection prevention and control advice, and demonstrate strong leadership skills. They will also provide professional leadership and support to junior team members, ensuring the delivery of a high-quality, proactive IPC service that complies with Care Quality Commission standards, the Health and Social Care Act, and the Code of Practice. The Band 6 Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Nurse will support the Band 7 IPC Nurses and Lead Nurse in delivering a high-quality, evidence-based Infection Prevention and Control service across the Northern Care Alliance. Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, the post holder will help maintain a safe, effective and responsive service that protects patients, staff and visitors while supporting the delivery of outstanding patient care. The successful candidate will provide specialist IPC advice, education and support to both clinical and non-clinical staff. They will undertake surveillance, audit and quality improvement activities, contribute to the prevention, investigation and management of infection prevention and control incidents and outbreaks, and support assurance and governance processes. The post holder will promote compliance with national guidance, legislation and local policies, act as a visible clinical role model, and contribute to the ongoing development and improvement of the Infection Prevention and Control service across the Northern Care Alliance. They will play a key role in fostering a culture of continuous improvement, supporting colleagues to embed best practice and achieve excellence in infection prevention and control. The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) provides hospital and integrated health and social care services to over one million people living across Greater Manchester. Our 20,000 colleagues care for people in hospital and in the community, working across Bury, Rochdale, Oldham and Salford, to save and improve lives. As a large NHS trust we are committed to enhancing the health of our local population by delivering consistently high standards of care and working closely with local authorities and key partners. We believe in our power and potential to make a difference and we’re always looking for people who demonstrate our three core values - care , appreciate and inspire – to join our team. In return, we can offer you a job role with purpose and flexibility. The size and scale of the NCA means we can provide more challenge and opportunities so your career can always be moving in the right direction. By joining us you can also access a competitive benefits package, including, a fantastic annual leave allowance, flexible working opportunities and protected hours for health and wellbeing activities, helping you to achieve more personal downtime and a better work-life balance. items.desc: Hillingdon Adult Community Mental Health Services are seeking a motivated and experienced Band 6 Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our new Assertive Outreach pathway. We are looking for someone who is passionate about delivering high‑quality care, proactive care. and is committed to supporting people in their mental health recovery. The successful candidate will join a wider Community Mental Health Hub OT service that prides itself on innovation, excellent service delivery and continued learning. This post is based at Mill House, but you will be required to visit patients across the Borough depending on service demand. View this webpage and video for more information about Occupational Therapy in CNWL Occupational Therapy :: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust CNWL Occupational Therapy Recruitment (FINAL) | Videos & Movies on Vimeo The post holder will manage a small, high-intensity caseload, delivering time-limited, occupationally focused interventions through proactive engagement. Practice will be guided by Assertive Outreach principles, with an emphasis on collaborative risk management, sustaining engagement and reducing barriers to recovery. Working with individuals presenting with complex mental health needs, the post holder will assess the impact of illness on occupational performance, daily functioning and participation. Interventions will be strengths-based and trauma-informed, supporting individuals to develop meaningful routines, increase independence, enhance community participation, and achieve their recovery goals. The role requires flexible working across a range of settings, including service users’ homes and community environments, to enable assessment and intervention within real-life contexts. The Assertive Outreach Team role is patient-facing, requiring proactive outreach, direct therapeutic intervention and consistent face-to-face engagement. As such, the role is not suitable for remote or hybrid working arrangements. Are you passionate about helping others live meaningful lives? Join us as an Occupational Therapist at CNWL. We are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive and reflective working environment where people feel valued, listened to and able to do their best work. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team that prioritises recovery-focused, person-centred care and values collaboration, curiosity and compassion. We recognise that high-quality care depends on staff wellbeing and support this through flexible working, regular supervision and protected reflective space. We are committed to developing our Occupational Therapists, offering role-relevant training, leadership development and opportunities to broaden or specialise practice within community mental health. As part of CNWL, you will also benefit from a wide range of staff wellbeing resources, award-winning staff networks, and an extensive NHS benefits package designed to support your work–life balance and overall wellbeing. See attached Job description and Person Specification for further information on the job role requirements. Key Responsibilities Clinical deliver specialist occupational therapy assessment and intervention for individuals with complex mental health needs provide assertive outreach interventions, including intensive and time-limited support during periods of risk or disengagement use proactive and persistent engagement approaches to maintain contact with individuals who are difficult to engage plan and deliver interventions with clear goals, outcome measures and structured transition planning contribute to risk assessment and management, balancing positive risk-taking with safety manage referrals and hold a small, high-intensity caseload within the multidisciplinary team prioritise work load and delegate appropriately to support staff apply occupational therapy models (e.g. MOHO) to inform clinical reasoning and interventions use outcome measures to evaluate effectiveness and inform care planning place service users at the centre of goal setting and involve carers where appropriate deliver culturally responsive and inclusive care prescribe equipment to support occupational performance in line with Trust policy

items.desc: he pharmacy department are delighted to be able to offer a vacancy for a Pharmacy Porter/Assistant where no two days will be the same! Why, you ask? There are a range of duties and responsibilities that you will receive training in. You could be providing a top up of medicine stock to our hospital wards one day and then dealing with our external customers the next processing their orders. In this role, you will need to be enthusiastic, motivated and demonstrate a desire to contribute towards developing our services. It would be an advantage if you had previous pharmacy or stores experience, however full training and support will be provided. Our core working hours are Monday to Friday (8am until 7pm), with weekends and bank holidays managed on a rota basis (9am until 6pm). All shifts are 7.5 hours with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break. For those applying for this part time role, please be aware that this requires committing to the same days each week Monday to Friday for a full 7.5 hour shift. Successful applicants will be funded to complete the Buttercups Level 2 – Support Staff Course for Pharmacy Assistants. Please be aware that large parts of this role involve working in our pharmacy stores warehouse and involves significant manual handling of products. These require onwards delivery to wards and departments throughout the hospital so our patients have access to the medicines they need. There is also a requirement to use both hand and electric pallet trucks. This post is an ideal stepping stone for those looking to progress in pharmacy. We have regular opportunities for you to develop yourself in this role particularly as our services continue to expand. So what will you be working on on a day to day basis? Your main duties within this role will include providing an effective medicine supply service to wards/departments across the Trust and to external customers such as Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Trust , Ambulance stations, Private hospitals and other NHS hospitals. You will process, pick, pack and deliver all pharmacy orders for the Trust and even be responding to any robot issues. Your days won't ever be boring! You will support training and development of other staff; maintaining quality and standards by contributing to the development and implementation of new services, processes and procedures to deliver services in line with professional, local and national directives. Further information can be found in the job description and if you would like to know more prior to interview, why not get in touch and come and visit us. We are more than happy for you to spend some time with us so that you can see what we do. If you are considering applying then please contact us for more information, we can also arrange a visit for a tour of our department! We have 10,000 fantastic people working hard to deliver quality services to our patients. Whatever your role, you help look after 370,000 people in our local area & give specialist care to 1.5 million people across Lancashire & Cumbria. Working with us gives you the knowledge and sense of pride that every activity you do genuinely does make a difference to support our patients & staff, ensuring we keep thriving & delivering outstanding healthcare right across our local towns. You’ll have access to varied development opportunities, learn new skills, meet fab people & do things you’d never have done. You’ll learn about working in a hospital, interacting with people from all different roles to build skills & enhance your career path. You’ll make an impact, be challenged to think differently, be bold & help innovate to keep improving things. Everything we do centres around patient care which means your role is pivotal and something really to be proud of. Duties to include, but not be limited to: Communicates all relevant information and advice to the pharmacy, nursing and medical teams; patients and service users; and with external organisations as required Provide an effective ward top up service to wards/departments of the Trust Provide an effective medicine supply service to external customers who include Lancashire Care, Ambulance stations, GP’s, Private hospitals and other NHS hospitals. items.desc: Job Description At Sage, we're redefining how solution design works in an AI-first world. We're building a new Solution Design capability within Domain Services, creating a profession that combines the strongest elements of business analysis, solution design and detailed product ownership. As a Solution Designer, you'll play a central role in shaping how ideas become scalable, reliable solutions that power products used by businesses around the world. Working at the intersection of Product, Engineering and Architecture, you'll take agreed product outcomes and transform them into clear, coherent, traceable solutions that teams can build with confidence. You'll lead discovery, model complex business and technical processes, maintain living specifications and ensure solutions remain aligned from concept through to delivery. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing team at an early stage, helping define new ways of working, influence best practice and shape the future of solution design at Sage. *** Please note that this role is hybrid and will require you to work 3 days a week from our Newcastle office. *** Key Responsibilities What You'll Be Doing Lead detailed discovery activities to build a deep understanding of customer needs, business processes, constraints, dependencies and outcomes. Translate product intent into clear, end-to-end logical solutions covering journeys, workflows, services, business rules, integrations, APIs, data flows and operational considerations. Facilitate collaboration across Product Management, Engineering, Architecture, Compliance, Support and other specialist teams. Create and maintain detailed, versioned specifications, acceptance criteria and decision records that provide a trusted source of truth throughout delivery. Identify risks, assumptions, dependencies and impacts early, helping teams make informed decisions. Ensure accessibility, operational readiness, support requirements, audit needs and failure scenarios are considered from the outset. Work closely with engineering teams throughout development, evolving specifications as new learning emerges. Use AI-powered tools to accelerate discovery, analysis, modelling and documentation while maintaining accountability for accuracy, quality and decision-making. Contribute reusable patterns, knowledge assets and best practices that strengthen the wider Solution Design community. What We're Looking For We're open to candidates from a variety of backgrounds. You may have worked as a Business Analyst, Solution Designer, Product Owner, Service Designer or in a similar role where you've been responsible for turning complex requirements into clear, deliverable solutions. You'll likely bring: Experience leading analysis and discovery activities from initial concept through to successful delivery. Strong facilitation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to bring diverse viewpoints together and create shared understanding. Experience creating detailed specifications, requirements, workflows, process models and acceptance criteria. The ability to model end-to-end solutions across processes, services, integrations, data flows and operational considerations. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the confidence to navigate ambiguity and make evidence-based recommendations. Experience working closely with Product Managers, Architects, Engineers and other cross-functional stakeholders. Understanding of APIs, integrations, logical data design and service-oriented solutions. The ability to communicate complex concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. An appreciation for accessibility, operational readiness, supportability, compliance and risk management. A collaborative mindset and a willingness to challenge constructively, ask questions and continuously improve ways of working. Nice to Have Experience working in fintech, banking, payments, financial services, tax, compliance or related domains. Experience working on platform capabilities, shared services or backend-focused products and services. Exposure to migration programmes, large-scale integrations or data-intensive initiatives. Experience using AI-assisted tools to support discovery, analysis, modelling or documentation activities. Knowledge of SaaS, cloud-based platforms or enterprise software environments. You'll help shape an evolving profession, influence how solution design is practised in an AI-first environment and work on complex platform capabilities that support products across Sage. items.desc: At Amentum, we're not just solving problems; we're engineering the future. Our team is driven by an unyielding commitment to innovation, integrity, and collaboration, tackling some of the most significant challenges in science, security, and sustainability. If you're passionate about making a real impact and want to be part of a community that values ethical excellence, this is the place where your ambition can thrive. Here, we believe that success comes from continuously pushing boundaries and working together to deliver on our promises. We embrace challenges with confidence and are dedicated to creating a secure and vibrant future for all. We’ll inspire and empower you to deliver your best work so you can evolve, grow and succeed – today and into tomorrow. We offer an exciting range of opportunities to develop your career within a supportive team who always strive to do the right thing for our people, clients and communities. People are our greatest asset, and we offer a competitive package to retain and attract the best talent. In addition to the benefits you’d expect, UK employees also receive free single medical cover and digital GP service, family-friendly benefits such as enhanced parental leave pay and free membership of employee assistance and parental programmes, plus reimbursement towards relevant professional development and memberships. Work-life balance and flexibility is a key focus area for us. We’re happy to discuss hybrid, part-time and flexible working hours, patterns and locations to suit you and our business. About the Opportunity We are looking for a motivated Junior Geophysicist with at least two years of professional experience to join our Subsurface Solutions team within the Earth and Environmental Operations Area. You will bridge the gap between complex data collection and practical engineering solutions, supporting environmental, defence and energy projects. This is a hybrid role involving hands-on field data acquisition, advanced processing, and technical reporting. You will be working within a multidisciplinary team with specialities in low strength sedimentary rock, high strength rock and Quaternary geology, and in disciplines ranging from hydrogeology, land quality, geotechnical engineering, engineering geology and geoscience related safety case work. Much of the work we undertake involves siting, site characterisation, site descriptive models and understanding subsurface conditions and hazards. In addition, you will be encouraged to work with the wider Amentum community to further strengthen the team’s capabilities. You will also gain experience in complex bid preparation, project management and technical planning. As a result, we are looking for people who have the passion and drive to be involved with major projects with strong adaptability, prioritisation and teamworking skills. Whilst much of our work is focussed on exciting projects that form part of Amentum’s Energy, Environment and Defence businesses. We would be interested in candidates with experience in carbon capture and storage (CCS) and geothermal energy, which could compliment future growth opportunities. What You’ll Do: Field Data Acquisition: Lead and support geophysical surveys using in-house survey equipment such as ERI, GPR, EM and HVSR. Site Investigation: Assist in the design of survey programmes to identify subsurface risks like voids, utilities, or varying bedrock depth and integrate findings with geotechnical and geoenvironmental teams planning intrusive investigations. Support the design of third party onshore surveys such as MASW, 2D reflection and refraction, wireline and cross-hole seismic, providing field supervision. Support the design of third party near-shore marine surveys such as SBP, Magnetometer, 2D reflection and refraction, providing field supervision (offshore certification and training provided). Data Processing and interpretation: Utilise industry-standard software (e.g. Res2DInv, Geolitix) to process raw field data into actionable models. Assist with the interpretation of 2D and 3D seismic datasets (IHS Kingdom). Conduct structural analysis and fault mapping using geophysical, borehole, and field data and integrate with other datasets to support subsurface evaluations. Develop an understanding of the underlying requirements of our clients, and how we can meet those requirements. Reporting: Technical writing of factual and interpretive reports, ensuring high-quality visualisations and clear recommendations. Safety & Logistics: Manage field equipment maintenance and uphold strict Health & Safety standards on-site. What We’re Looking For Education: A degree in Geophysics, Geology, or Civil Engineering (MSc preferred). Experience: 2+ years in a commercial engineering or environmental geophysics environment. Technical Skills: Proficiency in GIS (ArcGIS/QGIS) and geophysical processing software. Field Readiness: Willingness to travel to remote sites across the UK and overseas when …

items.desc: Band 6 Specialist Wheelchair Therapist -Occupational Therapist or Physiotherapist An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Band 6 Wheelchair Therapist to join our patient-centred multidisciplinary Wheelchair Service team. We are looking for a registered Occupational Therapist or Physiotherapist who is keen to develop their knowledge and skills in this diverse, niche and rewarding area of wheelchairs. You must have experience working in a wide range of clinical areas, with both adults and children, have excellent organisational, interpersonal and communication skills, and be passionate about delivering personalised care to wheelchair service users. Ideally you will have experience working in a Wheelchair Service, with competencies in wheelchair assessment, prescription and provision; however, this is not essential, providing you are quick to learn and can demonstrate underpinning and transferable knowledge and skills in posture and mobility assessments and management. You will be part of a highly motivated multi-disciplinary team providing assessments and wheelchair provision to people of all ages with a wide range of conditions that have a permanent disability that requires them to use a wheelchair (or associated equipment) on a long-term basis. It is patient facing position which is clinic based but also requires you to visit service users in their place of residence or other establishment in the community as/ when required. You must be able to start and finish work at base every day, and work across both of our locations (Wirral and West Cheshire), according to the needs of the service. It is essential that you are able can drive and have access to a suitable vehicle for work purposes. Wirral Community Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust has been rated as Good by CQC (Dec 2023) with some outstanding areas. As an aspiring outstanding Trust we have numerous policies and procedures in place which provide standard organisational ways of working, in line with organisational objectives, relevant legislation and requirements. Policies allow for continuity and consistency within the Trust. Employees must abide by and adhere to all Wirral Community NHS Trust’s policies, at all times. We deliver NHS wheelchair services to adults and children living in Wirral and West Cheshire for Cheshire Merseyside Integrated Commissioning Board (ICB); and have nearly 8,000 wheelchair users with equipment on issue from our service. We pride ourselves in delivering excellent customer service and on-going clinical support to all our users, along with a comprehensive maintenance and repair service which is provided by an approved contractor. We strive to be a great place to work and thrive; and are committed to investing in you to help you fulfil your potential through a range of learning and development opportunities. Our staff are very much valued, and this is why we offer a range of employee benefits including family friendly policies, additional leave purchase scheme, laptops for remote working, staff wellbeing support services including counselling and inclusive staff networks. For the main responsibilities of the post please refer to the attached Job Description. Responsibilities include: Utilising therapy skills to assess for, prescribe and provide wheelchairs and associated equipment to an identified cohort of service users. Working within the local eligibility criteria for the provision of wheelchairs and associated equipment. Offering people who are eligible for new/ re-provision of a wheelchair a personal wheelchair budget in line with legislation and service operating model. Handing over and adjusting any prescribed equipment, advising the service user and carers on its safe use. Prioritising, organising and managing own workload autonomously and in the most efficient and effective way. Documenting assessments, interventions and equipment details on the Wheelchair Service’s clinical and asset management system. Supervising and supporting the development of identified Therapy Assistants/ Support Practitioners. Being a proactive clinical educator and supervising both Occupational Therapy and Physiotherapy students, regardless of your own profession. Providing specialist advice to other health and care professionals on wheelchairs and postural management. Recognising and working within own competence and professional code of conduct/ standards. Taking responsibility for own CPD and keep up to date with clinical practice and wheelchair products. Do you have a high level of skill in the assessment and care of people who present to ED in mental health crisis and those who have mental health needs during their inpatient stay in the acute hospital? The MH&LD Liaison Team provides assessments, advice, and reasonable adjustments for people with mental health needs and learning disabilities accessing treatment at St Mary's Hospital. We aim to improve the parity of care for people of all ages with mental health and learning disabilities in the acute hospital and work with their family and carers to ensure they have the best possible care and treatment. The MH&LD Liaison Team works across the full age spectrum and provides a 24-hour service across seven days of the week. You should have excellent written and verbal communication skills and be able to interact at all levels. There will be opportunities for you to participate in the teaching and training of health professionals in ED, medical and surgical wards. This is a challenging but rewarding role, within a busy and evolving multidisciplinary service. We can offer great opportunities learning, professional development and research in liaison services. There is access to training opportunities locally and through the Open University, as well as with mainland universities such as those in Portsmouth, Southampton, and Bournemouth. We offer a supportive working environment, we have a robust appraisal and supervision policy and to assist you to realize your potential and achieve a greater degree of job satisfaction, as well as the usual NHS discounts, pension, salary, generous annual leave entitlement and relocation expenses, subject to meeting criteria. items.desc: Are you passionate about supporting individuals to achieve their employment goals? Do you believe in the transformative power of work and its impact on health and wellbeing? If so, we want to hear from you! We are looking for dedicated Employment Specialists to join our team and deliver the Individual Placement Support (IPS) model, helping people with mental health conditions find and sustain meaningful employment. What we’re looking for: A commitment to empowering individuals to reach their full potential. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Experience in employment support (preferred but not essential). Knowledge of the local job market and the ability to build relationships with employers. A positive, proactive, and compassionate attitude. A strengths-based perspective, focusing on clients’ abilities. If you’re ready to make a lasting impact and help change lives through employment, we’d love to hear from you! Please note, the role requires travel for meetings with colleagues, service users and local employers. We have vacancies across Liverpool, Sefton, St Helens, Warrington Interviews planned for 19th and 20th November 2026 The Employment Specialist will join an Individual Placement and Support Team (IPS) working under the direction of the IPS Employment Services Manager to deliver IPS as part of the holistic recovery plan for mental health service users. The post holder will work directly with employers to secure employment opportunities for people who have experienced mental health problems, and subsequently provide ongoing support depending on employee’s and employer’s needs. The aim will be to enable people who have experienced mental health problems to gain and retain paid employment. The Employment Specialists will be responsible for: Work closely with individuals to identify their skills, aspirations, and career goals. Build strong partnerships with local employers to promote the service and secure employment opportunities. Collaborate with healthcare professionals and community organisations to provide integrated support. Offer coaching, advice, and guidance to help individuals navigate recruitment processes and thrive in their new roles. Champion the IPS model, demonstrating a person-centred, strengths-based approach to employment support. Mersey Care is one of the largest trusts providing physical health and mental health services in the North West, serving more than 1.4 million people across our region and are also commissioned for services that cover the North West, North Wales and the Midlands. We offer specialist inpatient and community services that support physical and mental health and specialist inpatient mental health, learning disability, addiction and brain injury services. Mersey Care is one of only three trusts in the UK that offer high secure mental health facilities. At the heart of all we do is our commitment to ‘perfect care’ – care that is safe, effective, positively experienced, timely, equitable and efficient. We support our staff to do the best job they can and work alongside service users, their families, and carers to design and develop future services together. We’re currently delivering a programme of organisational and service transformation to significantly improve the quality of the services we provide and safely reduce cost as we do so. Flexible working requests will be considered for all roles. The Employment Specialist will be expected to deliver the IPS approach, working directly with all relevant stakeholders. The Employment Specialist will maintain a professional relationship with the service users of the IPS service, key internal and external stakeholders, with particular attention to confidentiality and the maintenance of professional boundaries. To adhere to mandatory administrative and data capture protocols when recording the progress of individuals. To keep accurate and complete records of casework, using the appropriate electronic clinical notes systems. To act independently, using own judgement, knowledge and initiative to develop and understanding of the needs and potential career aspirations of job seekers. To sensitively gather information, to develop a shared vocational profile and an agreed Job Notion or Curriculum Vitae, for each individual job seeker. On occasion complex, sensitive and contentious information will need to be provided and/or received. To research the labour market and spend time getting to know local employers in order to negotiate job opportunities that meet everyone’s strengths, needs, abilities and preferences. You will be accredited with BABCP or eligible for and working towards accreditation with the BABCP. We want patients and staff to recommend our organisation as a place where they would be happy for their friends and family to be treated. You can help us do this by bringing your skills, experience and commitment to The Wellbeing Service. The Wellbeing Service is expanding, and we work closely with community colleagues to support people living with Long Term Conditions as well as our core work. We will offer evidence based psychological treatments to help individuals to live well with their condition, and strengthen links with key physical health colleagues in our area. Additional training in working with Long Term Conditions will be provided. You will provide high intensity interventions to a range of adults with anxiety, depression and trauma related problems. You will receive regular supervision as well as in service training and CPD days that ensure your continued learning and development. This is an opportunity to join an established team of Psychological Therapists providing a range of NICE compliant treatments at Step 3. You will work as part of a multi-disciplinary team. Experience of working in Primary Care will be an advantage. As well as 1:1 work you may be expected to co-facilitate group interventions. For the delivery of group work we provide training and additional support, should you need it. As a Band 7 therapist, you will contribute to the on-going development and evaluation of the service. The post will be based in one of our sites in Ipswich or Bury St Edmunds, dependent on applicants own location, however, there is a requirement to work across Suffolk as required. Treatments are currently being delivered digitally and remotely from home as well as face to face treatment provision in clinical spaces across the county. There will therefore be an expectation to work a hybrid model of set days at home and set days from a clinic setting. Why work for us? We have challenges as a Trust, but we have ambitious aspirations, are pushing ahead with exciting transformation work and we need dedicated individuals to support us on our journey. We have strong, established nursing networks coupled with an exceptional leadership team who will ensure you are truly cared for and cared about. Why Norfolk and Suffolk? The people here are warm and welcoming, you’ll never be far from the beautiful coastline or Broads National Park. We’re an hour and a half away from London and have an international airport in Norwich too. Our villages, towns and cities are packed full of history, independent cafes, shops and theatres. We have excellent shopping, eating out, top ranking schooling and affordable house prices too. Benefits Benefits included with this role are: - NHS pension a comprehensive in house & external training programmes career progression starting annual leave of 27 days per annum increasing to 33 days pa based on length of service (plus paid bank holidays) staff physio service NHS discounts and many more Here at NSFT we pride ourselves on being a welcoming, talented, friendly and supportive team who like nothing better than sharing experiences and learning from each other. In addition to ongoing training and development opportunities, we are committed to providing an environment in which you can thrive. Please find attached our Job Description and Person Specification for more detail on your Key Accountabilities, then if you feel you have what it takes to make a difference in your local communities, click APPLY!

items.desc: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust has an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and motivated Registered Nurse to join our dynamic Complex Discharge Team. This role offers the opportunity to develop specialist knowledge and experience in discharge planning, patient flow and case management whilst working within a supportive multidisciplinary environment. The successful candidate will work closely with ward teams, community partners, local authorities and care providers to coordinate safe, timely and person-centred discharges for patients with complex health and social care needs. The Complex Discharge Nurse plays a key role in identifying and resolving barriers to discharge, supporting the implementation of Home First and Discharge to Assess principles, and ensuring patients receive the right care in the right place at the right time. Using digital patient flow and clinical utilisation systems, the post holder will monitor patient journeys, coordinate discharge actions and support ward teams to deliver high-quality discharge planning. This is a rewarding opportunity to enhance clinical, leadership and communication skills whilst contributing to improved patient outcomes, patient experience and effective hospital flow. Responsible for coordinating safe, timely and effective discharge planning from admission, ensuring needs are identified early and plans progressed throughout the patient journey. Provide proactive case management for patients with complex discharge needs, overseeing assessments, referrals, actions and timescales. Identify and escalate discharge barriers early to reduce avoidable delays and length of stay. Act as a key contact for patients, families, ward teams and external agencies. Work with the MDT, Transfer of Care Hub, community services, Local Authorities and care providers to coordinate safe discharge. Support daily board rounds and MDT reviews, progressing EDDs, discharge plans and outstanding actions. Provide specialist advice on complex discharge processes and pathways, including Discharge to Assess, CHC Fast Track, end-of-life care and placements. Review medically optimised patients and escalate barriers to discharge. Promote Home First and least restrictive discharge principles. Maintain accurate discharge documentation and contribute to service improvement and patient flow. The role provides proactive oversight from admission to discharge, supporting patient safety, timely transfer of care, reduced avoidable length of stay and effective patient flow . Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust comprises Aintree University Hospital, Broadgreen Hospital & Royal Liverpool University Hospital. We are part of NHS University Hospitals of Liverpool Group, formed on 1 Nov 2024 from the coming together of LUHFT and Liverpool Women’s NHS Foundation Trust. The Group was born from a shared aim to improve the care we provide our patients. UHLG is one of the largest employers in the region, with over 16,800 colleagues dedicated to caring for our communities - from birth and beyond. For the 630,000 people across Merseyside, we are their local NHS. We provide general and emergency hospital care, alongside highly specialised regional services for more than two million people in the North West. Aintree University Hospital is the single receiving site for adult major trauma patients in Cheshire and Merseyside and hosts a number of regional services including an award-winning stroke facility. Broadgreen Hospital is home to elective surgical, diagnostic and treatment services, together with specialist patient rehabilitation. Liverpool Women’s Hospital specialises in the health of women and babies, delivering over 7,200 babies in the UK’s largest single site maternity hospital each year. The Royal Liverpool University Hospital is the largest hospital in the country to provide inpatients with 100% single bedrooms and focuses on complex planned care and specialist services. For roles at Liverpool Women’s, visit their careers page . The Complex Discharge Nurse is a senior registered nurse responsible for coordinating, facilitating and overseeing the discharge planning process for patients with complex health and social care needs. The post holder will work collaboratively with patients, their families, carers and multidisciplinary teams to ensure safe, timely and effective discharge from hospital, whilst reducing avoidable delays and improving patient outcomes. The role requires proactive case management, excellent communication skills and the ability to coordinate complex discharge pathways across health and social care systems. The post holder will act as an expert resource for ward teams, supporting the delivery of Home First and Discharge to Assess principles and ensuring patient-centred discharge planning is embedded throughout the patient journey. items.desc: Westlands Ward is looking to recruit a motivated and compassionate Band 5 Registered Nurse to join our established Multi-Disciplinary Team. Westlands is an 18-bedded female inpatient unit providing intensive, high-quality, person-centred assessment and interventions within a trauma-informed care model. The service supports individuals experiencing acute mental health difficulties, helping to inform decisions regarding ongoing support within the community or referral to specialist treatment services where further intervention is required. The successful candidate will work collaboratively as part of the wider multidisciplinary team to deliver safe, effective and recovery-focused care. You will be expected to provide clinical supervision and support to junior staff across the service and contribute to the development of a positive and therapeutic ward environment. Applicants should have experience of delivering evidence-based, values-driven and recovery-focused interventions that promote independence, resilience and positive outcomes for service users. Excellent communication, assessment and clinical decision-making skills are essential, along with a commitment to delivering compassionate, high-quality care. This is an excellent opportunity for a dedicated nurse who is passionate about supporting individuals on their recovery journey and developing their career within an experienced and supportive team. Reporting to the Team Lead/Clinical Lead, the post holder will work as part of a multidisciplinary team, supporting individuals experiencing mental health difficulties. Working alongside psychiatrists, psychologists, occupational therapists, healthcare assistants and other allied professionals, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred care that promotes recovery and positive outcomes. Key responsibilities include assessing patient needs, developing and maintaining care plans, completing risk assessments, and ensuring accurate clinical documentation. You will support service users to maximise their independence, wellbeing and recovery while working in partnership with families, carers and external agencies. The role requires excellent communication, observational and assessment skills, along with the ability to remain calm and make sound clinical decisions in challenging situations. You will also be responsible for administering medication, monitoring treatment outcomes, and escalating concerns appropriately. This is an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful difference within a supportive and dedicated clinical team, delivering compassionate, recovery-focused care to individuals with mental health needs. The ITSM & Integration Architect provides technical leadership and assurance across ITSM platforms, data integrations and technical solutions within large-scale service transition and transformation programmes. The role ensures solutions meet customer requirements, align with DXC standards and support successful transition and ongoing operations. Working across complex, multi-vendor environments, the architect validates designs, assesses data and environment readiness, resolves technical challenges and supports transition quality gates and exit criteria, including Walk-in Take Over (WITO) scenarios. Key Responsibilities Architecture & Technical Assurance Review and validate ITSM configurations across enterprise platforms such as ServiceNow and BMC Remedy and other ITSM platforms, including workflows, business rules, SLAs, reporting and integrations. Assess integration architectures covering APIs, middleware, data mapping, transformation and orchestration, ensuring solutions are robust, scalable and supportable. Validate data quality, migration readiness, environments and tooling; identify technical gaps, risks and dependencies, and drive remediation. items.desc: We're unlocking access to the NHS, because healthcare is not truly free until it's truly accessible The world’s best healthcare, for free. It's not a new idea, it's called the NHS. But the largest healthcare provider is fundamentally broken. Patient satisfaction is at an all time low, and the biggest reason cited is lack of access. So we’re on a mission to fix it with technology that actually works. We're building the front door of UK healthcare, creating a future where one billion NHS appointments are transparent and instantly bookable, and patients are guided to the right service first time using AI. We're developing critical national infrastructure. Today, 26% of GP practices in England use our patient registration software, while one in five GP practices in London use Bookable Search to help new patients find and book appointments seamlessly. Our latest product, Bookable Navigator, extends this vision by automatically booking appointments for existing patients. We operate from within a working GP practice in East London We're backed by Y Combinator, Innovate UK and the NHS Clinical Entrepreneur Programme, and were previously ranked the 8th fastest-growing startup in the UK and 33rd fastest-growing in Europe Our Principles Exciting challenges lie ahead. Guided by our principles, we’ll meet these challenges with a thoughtful and caring approach. These principles drive everything we do at Healthtech-1: Care deeply Work hard Be your word Trust in radical truth and transparency Do your life's best work Find the fun Read more about our principles and our "why" in the Healthtech-1 Handbook. The role We're hiring a mid-level Product Designer to work directly with our CEO to own the design of the Bookable Navigator Inbox: this is the place where GP practice teams receive, triage and act on every patient request. It's used all day by receptionists, care navigators and clinicians, and every rough edge costs them precious time with patients. To be clear: this isn't a senior or leadership role. It's for a designer who has spend 3-5 years shipping within fast-paced product teams and wants to accelerate their career. You'll have a lot of ownership, be expected to stay close to users, and work closely with engineering. If you are hungry, want to work hard, and want a role of a lifetime, we'd love to hear from you. What you'll do Get close to users Talk to practice staff regularly: run interviews, sit in on real shifts, and watch how the Inbox gets used Research and scope product tickets before they reach engineering, so we build the right thing Become the user: dogfood the product until you know its friction better than anyone Use data Dig into product metrics to find where people get stuck, then turn that into design work Measure whether what you shipped actually made things better Design and ship Take ideas from scrappy MVP through to polished, high-fidelity design Make things simple, beautiful and usable, for people working under real time pressure Work side by side with engineers, from first sketch to what goes live Use AI tools like Claude every day to research, prototype and move faster About you You've cut your teeth on at least two great products, shipped and used by real people You've worked in a product team, and you've worked at a startup You're obsessed with UI and think about design constantly, down to the spacing on a button You're excited about talking to users and getting close to the problem You have the fire to improve: you seek out feedback and want to get much better quickly You're comfortable with numbers and can make a case from data You already use AI tools in your workflow Bonus: the best candidates will think like a product manager. You ask why before how, can scope a problem down to what matters, and have opinions about what to build next. We'll explore this in the interview process. Progression As AI changes how software gets built, the line between design and product is blurring, and this role sits right on the edges. You'll start owning the Inbox experience, and grow towards owning product decisions end to end. We want people who could one day found their own company. Here you'll get the reps to do it: real users, real problems in the NHS, and the freedom to work directly with our CEO to shape what we build. Trusted with one of the biggest datasets in the world. Our office is within a GP practice. This is our unfair advantage. Got a question? Pop down the corridor. Want to learn how your work affects real patients? Pop downstairs to reception. 4 days in the office and 1 day WFH (for most roles). We highly prioritise in-person communication and prefer candidates who want to work 4+ days a week in the office. Our anchor days are Mon, Tues, Thurs and Fri. items.desc: About CIR The Centre for Information Resilience (CIR) is an independent organisation dedicated to exposing human rights violations and threats to democracy. We achieve this through open source research, digital investigations, capacity-building with local partners, and collaboration with media to amplify our impact. CIR was born out of a determination to expose those spreading harm – online and offline – around the world, particularly in areas of violent conflict, such as Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar. Our projects are at the forefront of efforts to investigate and document human rights abuses, war crimes, harms targeting women and minorities, and influence operations. We work closely with multilateral and national justice accountability bodies. Role details: Contract Type : Contractor Closing date : 26th October 2026 at 23:55pm Contract length : ASAP until 31st March 2027 Hours needed for this role: Full time, 19-20 days a month. Part time roles may also be considered. Location : Remote About the Project CIR specialises in rigorous, ethical, and impact-driven research on technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), translating evidence into accountability, advocacy, and practical interventions. For this project, CIR’s is seeking to recruit an open-source researcher to investigate how gender norms and identity can be weaponised to escalate conflicts. We are seeking someone with experience in conducting narrative and network analysis in the MENA region, including analysing online narratives surges to verified online incidents, to test whether and how gendered identity content precedes, accompanies or follows escalation. Main Responsibilities Employ open-source intelligence (OSINT) and social media analysis (SOCMINT) tools, techniques, and methodologies to conduct research into the MENA information environment. Use SOCMINT tools to conduct audience analysis and gather audience insight. Analysing and documenting evidence of Ethnic, Religious and Gendered Hate speech, coordinated Inauthentic behaviour and other violations of platform terms and conditions and standards. Contribute to CIR’s investigations into how gender and identity are exploited on social media in relation to ongoing conflicts in the MENA region. Input information into the project’s databases and code that data to pre-set information fields as required. Ensure that all data is preserved and archived according to project and organisational standards. Work with other investigators to analyse data from multiple sources and create comprehensive analytical reports on gendered hate speech and narratives, trends, and dynamics. Support the design and production of high-quality reports that effectively explain insights and the evidence and methodology underpinning them. Requirements Essential Criteria: Proven experience with open-source intelligence (OSINT) and social media analysis (SOCMINT) tools and techniques. Expertise in monitoring of ethnic, religious and gendered hate speech. Expertise in narrative tracking and social media research techniques. Proven experience with the development of GESI framework and lexicons. Ability to write short- and long-form reports using concise, clear and accurate language. items.desc: À propos Rejoignez Allphins, une start-up insurtech dynamique qui redéfinit la gestion des risques dans l'industrie de la (ré)assurance grâce à une technologie innovante. En tant que Data Scientist - Analytics, vous aurez l'opportunité de jouer un rôle clé dans notre croissance rapide et notre expansion internationale. Notre parcours a commencé en 2019, au Lloyd's Lab, le principal accélérateur InsurTech de Londres, et à Station F, Paris, où notre équipe de data scientists, de software engineers et de chefs de produit a développé les solutions révolutionnaires d'Allphins pour les réassureurs. Notre solution est une plateforme SaaS permettant aux (ré)assureurs de comprendre efficacement leurs risques beaucoup plus rapidement et avec plus de précision que jamais auparavant, favorisant une prise de décision éclairée lors de la souscription. Aujourd'hui, nous sommes une équipe internationale, rentable et en pleine croissance, avec une présence au Royaume-Uni, aux États-Unis, en Allemagne, en France et en Suisse. Nous servons plus de 30 réassureurs à travers le monde dans tous les principaux secteurs commerciaux et spécialisés — y compris la propriété, l'énergie, le maritime, le risque politique, la responsabilité civile, la cybernétique, l'aviation et le terrorisme. Notre objectif est de résoudre les défis les plus pressants des (ré)assureurs pour une expansion rapide, avec l'ambition de devenir le leader mondial de la gestion des risques commerciaux et spécialisés. Nous valorisons la créativité, l'ingénierie pragmatique et la collaboration transparente pour offrir des produits de pointe qui répondent aux défis réels du monde professionnel. Descriptif du poste Vous souhaitez appliquer la data science et les LLM à des problématiques concrètes, pour des clients internationaux qui pilotent des risques complexes ? Nous recrutons un(e) Data Scientist – Analytics . Vous serez rattaché(e) à l’équipe technique et travaillerez au quotidien pour l’équipe Exposure Management, aux côtés de nos experts métier. Job Description Our PRISM (Supply Chain) is looking for an AI Engineer based in Paris. As an AI Engineer dedicated to agent deployment, you will be at the heart of a tight-knit technical team. Your will play a critical role in the industrialization, deployment and monitoring of our Agent capabilities. You will closely work with digital teams (Data, Product, Engineering) to architect the deployment infrastructure, design intelligence routing, and build secure infrastructure allowing our agents to interact natively with our corporate data and legacy systems. Responsibilities Design and deploy solid foundations that will allow our AI agents to be hosted, run, and interact smoothly with our systems during production release. Design robust pipelines enabling multi-step asynchronous agentic execution (e.g., transactional ingestion and writing flows), by implementing distributed resilience patterns. Integrate agentic orchestration SDKs (notably Google Vertex AI Agent SDK / ADK), bypassing "black box" limitations of managed frameworks. Also ensure quality and speed of task execution. Strictly define the scope of action for each agent. You guarantee they only access data and actions for which they are formally authorized, respecting our confidentiality rules, while ensuring data security. Build advanced performance measurement and tracking pipelines to trace agent reflections and decisions from end to end in order to debug logic in production. Work with the team to define relevant and consistent data evaluation metrics relative to the defined functional specificities and metrics. Hard Skills Robust backend design (Python), operational mastery of containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and pipelines (CI/CD, automated testing, observability, log management) to ensure robust production releases. Production-focused Python expertise, mastery of deployment platforms (Vertex AI Agent Builder, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) and client/server integration protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Experience optimizing context windows for massive frontier models. Request routing to models suitable for the selected solutions. Ability to build test frameworks for LLMs (LLM-as-a-Judge, Golden Datasets), mastery of deterministic metrics and strict validation of output formats (JSON schema enforcement). Practical experience with Agentic RAG, Semantic Caching to reduce latency and API costs, or using prompt optimization frameworks (e.g., DSPy) Applied experience in supply chain, retail technology, or model deployment via Databricks / MLFlow Soft Skills Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Ability to work effectively in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Adaptability and willingness to learn new technologies and methodologies and share them. Ability to translate complex technical concepts into understandable terms for non-technical stakeholders. Ability to understand user challenges and associated needs. Qualifications Senior Profile: You have solid experience (Machine Learning Engineering) with a strong focus on production infrastructure release. Ability to leverage managed solutions (Vertex AI) while knowing how to "dive into code" to debug distributed architectures, develop custom connectors, and bypass framework limitations. Demonstrated ability to evolve in shifting technical environments. Operational skills on GCP and understanding of containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) to autonomously deploy the Agentic layer. Technical Environment Agent orchestration: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Vertex AI Agent Builder Infrastructure & Cloud: GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines. AI & Integration Protocols: Model Context Protocol (MCP), LLMs (Gemini), LLM routing & memory management. Security & Access: Google Cloud Model Armor. Je bouwt modellen, prototypes en end-to-end AI-oplossingen in Python en combineert daarbij machine learning, Generative AI en Agentic AI. Denk aan toepassingen zoals RAG, documentverwerking, kennisassistenten en AI-agents die systemen en databronnen met elkaar verbinden. items.desc: Ubicación: Las Rozas, Madrid (Calle Jacinto Benavente) Modalidad: Híbrida, con asistencia a oficina 1 día a la semana. Diseñar y entrenar modelos predictivos con algoritmos como LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost u otros similares. Procesar y analizar grandes volúmenes de datos, trabajando con datasets de millones de registros. Implementar procesos CI/CD y gestionar entornos de ejecución mediante Docker y herramientas como GitHub Actions o GitLab CI. Optimizar el rendimiento de consultas y procesos de datos utilizando BigQuery. Colaborar con equipos técnicos aplicando metodologías de desarrollo, revisiones de código y control de versiones. Requisitos imprescindibles Experiencia sólida y demostrable con Google Cloud Platform (GCP), especialmente Vertex AI y BigQuery. Experiencia desarrollando modelos de Machine Learning con algoritmos como LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost o similares. Experiencia trabajando con grandes volúmenes de datos y optimizando tiempos de entrenamiento e inferencia. Experiencia en MLOps, llevando modelos desde entornos experimentales hasta producción. Buenas prácticas de ingeniería de software: Git, testing automatizado, code reviews y gestión de dependencias. Experiencia con arquitecturas modernas de Deep Learning para series temporales: Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), TiDE, PatchTST, TimesFM, Chronos o Transformers. Conocimientos de IA Generativa, LLMOps, RAG, agentes, evaluación de modelos y observabilidad. Experiencia optimizando hiperparámetros con Optuna, Ray Tune o herramientas similares. Conocimientos de paralelización del entrenamiento, optimización de inferencia y reducción de costes computacionales.

Experience with Git workflows, CI/CD pipelines and automated testing. Knowledge of containerisation and orchestration technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes). Understanding of authentication and authorisation protocols and standards (e.g., OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT). Experience working with Agile/Scrum methodologies. Ability to work autonomously and within multicultural, multilingual teams. Nice to have Experience with Python back-end frameworks (e.g., FastAPI, Django, Flask). Experience integrating large language models into applications, through vendor APIs or self-hosted inference servers (e.g., vLLM, Ollama), including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Experience with search engines (e.g., Elasticsearch, OpenSearch), including full-text and vector (semantic) search. Experience building document-processing pipelines for PDF and image files, including OCR and structured data extraction. Experience deploying containerised applications (e.g., Docker, Podman) in on-premises or air-gapped environments. Experience integrating enterprise single sign-on (e.g., OpenID Connect / SAML identity providers). AWS Certified Developer – Associate or Microsoft Azure Developer Associate certification. items.title: Ingénieur en système de perception (H/F)
items.card: missions : Dans le cadre du développement des systèmes d’assistance pour les engins miniers, vous contribuerez à l’élaboration des stratégies de perception de l’environnement. Vos principales missions seront : Réaliser des études de faisabilité pour le système de perception d’environnement autour d’une pelle minière (détection d’obstacles : engin minier, piéton / localisation pelle / cartographie terrain).
items.desc: Les missions : Dans le cadre du développement des systèmes d’assistance pour les engins miniers, vous contribuerez à l’élaboration des stratégies de perception de l’environnement. Vos principales missions seront : Réaliser des études de faisabilité pour le système de perception d’environnement autour d’une pelle minière (détection d’obstacles : engin minier, piéton / localisation pelle / cartographie terrain). Développer les modules logiciels d’acquisition, calibration, fusion et traitement de données provenant des capteurs de perception (Lidar, Radar, Camera). Identifier les technologies et approches les plus adaptées à une application minière et aux besoins définis. Définir et réaliser des tests avec des outils de simulation ou sur machines, en usine et sur site pour valider les concepts. Réaliser des cahiers des charges de composants ou fonctions logicielles et assurer le lien avec les fournisseurs. Analyser les données remontées par les machines sur le terrain. Rédiger la documentation associée aux développements. Le profil recherché : Ingénieur en mécatronique, orienté Computer Vision, avec une expérience de 5 ans minimum dans le développement de systèmes mécatroniques, de perception pour l’automatisation d’engins mobiles. Avoir de bonnes connaissances en systèmes de perception (Caméras, Radars, Lidars, …). Maîtriser Python, C++ et ROS/ ROS 2. Être autonome, rigoureux et avoir un bon sens pratique. Faire preuve d’ouverture d’esprit, avoir un bon sens relationnel et avoir l’esprit d’équipe. Maîtriser l’anglais. Nous proposons : Poste en CDI, statut cadre en forfait jours (convention collective de la Métallurgie), télétravail partiel possible Prime de vacances, Participation, chèques vacances, 13ème mois, Percol Restaurant d'entreprise Un Comité Economique et Social actif et une bonne couverture santé et prévoyance prise en charge à 90% par l'employeur. Notre entreprise s'engage en faveur de la diversité et du handicap, et à ce titre étudie les candidatures à niveau d'exigence égal. Avons-nous suscité votre intérêt ? Si c’est le cas, nous serions ravis de recevoir votre candidature en ligne. Si vous avez des questions, veuillez contacter Mathilde GAUTHIER. One Passion. Many Opportunities. Une passion commune. Tant d’opportunités. L'entreprise Liebherr-Mining Equipment Colmar SAS, acteur majeur dans l'industrie minière, présent à l'international, spécialisé dans le développement et la production de pelles et de tombereaux. Reconnu pour ses produits fiables, de qualité et un service de proximité, nous nous engageons à surpasser les attentes de nos clients avec des solutions innovantes. Chaque année, nous investissons dans l'amélioration de nos produits, tout en répondant aux défis de décarbonation. Avec des projets de recherche axés sur les nouvelles technologies, nous offrons à nos employés l'opportunité de façonner un avenir durable pour notre environnement. items.desc: Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. What We Do The Navigation team at Mapbox develops and operates web services powering virtually all of Mapbox’s strategic navigation initiatives in consumer, automotive, and logistics verticals. We are a highly multidisciplinary organization, with work spanning distributed systems on AWS to geospatial localization, traffic telemetry, and mapping. Collectively we are revolutionizing in-car experiences with technology to build fast, industry-leading maps and navigation for any vehicle. We’ve launched products such as MapGPT, Mapbox for EV, and we’re enhancing the visual experience of in-vehicle navigation with 3D styling with our new Mapbox Standard through web and mobile SDKs. Mapbox has worked with automotive partners — including BMW, Toyota, and GM — to bring the best aspects of mobile app development into in-vehicle navigation and infotainment. Mapbox Blog: Introducing 3D Live Navigation Mapbox Blog: Route Notifications Improve Driver Safety Mapbox Newsroom: AI Features in New Navigation SDK As AI becomes embedded in modern engineering workflows, we value engineers who can thoughtfully integrate AI into design, development, and decision-making. Our interview process will include discussion of how you use AI in your engineering workflow. What You’ll Do As a Machine Learning Engineer III on the Routing Cost team, you will lead the design, development, and delivery of highly trafficked recommendation systems for our routing cost engine. Your technical contributions will include: Lead the engineering team(s) to execute end-to-end feature implementation within the larger navigation organization (~80 engineers). Design and build new ML and data pipelines, as well as optimizing existing ML and data pipelines. Build tools for automated quality assurance and data exploration. Leverage geospatial algorithms to optimize pipelines, as well as creating automated tuning and outlier detection algorithms. Partner with data scientists to make improvements to our models for determining patterns in movement and/or traffic. Mentor colleagues and participate in code and design reviews. Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends. What We Believe Are Important Traits For This Role 8-10+ years of backend and ML experience: Extensive hands-on experience showcasing expertise and a strong track record in the engineering field. Technical knowledge: Extensive experience with Python, distributed processing pipelines (Hadoop, Spark, Airflow, Dask), and very large datasets – statistical analysis, data quality control, optimizing storage. Cloud proficiency: Extensive experience with cloud and infrastructure services, including, as well as deploying and managing infrastructure in cloud environments. Operational excellence: You drive a culture of quality and continuous improvement in your organization. Strong passion for clean code and robust architecture, with a drive to elevate engineering practices and design standards across the team. Ownership & execution: Own the technical vision, lead the strategy and guide the team to execute towards building the future of our routing cost engine. Customer focus: You care deeply about your customers and their problems, and you work tirelessly to innovate on their behalf. Growth mindset: Have the humility to accept mistakes, learn and grow from them. Mentorship: Experience mentoring and leading engineering teams developing skill sets and career growth. Strong written and vocal communication skills: You can talk and write about complex ideas concisely to a wide audience. You are able to lead and resolve org-wide technical discussions and are able to collaborate and include input from cross-functional teams (security, devops, data, compliance and product). Data informed mindset: You believe in the value of data informed decision making and strive to measure things that are not straight forward but essential. You also have the right instincts to make speedy decisions in the absence of perfect & comprehensive data What We Value In addition to our core values, which are not unique to this position and are necessary for Mapbox leaders: We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities. We believe in individuals being their whole selves at work. We commit to this through …

items.title: Distinguished Engineer – Software & AI Products (w/m/d)
items.card: Aufgaben und suchen Dich als: Distinguished Engineer – Software & AI Products (w/m/d) In unseren Teams Software Engineering und DevSecOps entwickeln und betreiben wir einen umfangreichen Software-Stack für kritische Kommunikationsnetze, basierend auf Microservices-Architekturen, Cloud-basierten Plattformen und containerisierten Lösungen. Im Fokus stehen die Verarbeitung großer Datenmengen und die Integration von KI
items.desc: Ab sofort in Berlin, Hannover, Bonn Deine Familie, Deine Freunde und Du verlassen sich rund um die Uhr auf Rettungskräfte und Einrichtungen der Regierung. Eure Helferinnen und Helfer sorgen 24/7 für Eure Sicherheit und wir sorgen mit Leidenschaft und Einsatz rund um die Uhr dafür, dass sie es können! Wir betreiben seit über 10 Jahren Kommunikations-Netzwerke für den Digitalfunk BOS und die Netze des Bundes. Unser Motto: helfen helfen! Sei dabei! Wir wachsen mit unseren Aufgaben und suchen Dich als: Distinguished Engineer – Software & AI Products (w/m/d) In unseren Teams Software Engineering und DevSecOps entwickeln und betreiben wir einen umfangreichen Software-Stack für kritische Kommunikationsnetze, basierend auf Microservices-Architekturen, Cloud-basierten Plattformen und containerisierten Lösungen. Im Fokus stehen die Verarbeitung großer Datenmengen und die Integration von KI und Machine Learning in unsere Produkte. Als Distinguished Engineer bist Du die technische Instanz zwischen Engineering und Unternehmensführung: Du schreibst nicht selbst den Code, verstehst ihn aber im Detail und vertrittst technische Strategien überzeugend vor der obersten Führungsebene. Aufgaben Du treibst die Entwicklung von Microservices-Architekturen, Cloud-basierten Plattformen und containerisierten Lösungen voran und verantwortest die technologische Roadmap. Du gestaltest skalierbare, hochverfügbare und sichere Systeme für heterogene Datenquellen und die Integration von KI/ML-Lösungen. Du bereitest strategische Technologieentscheidungen (z. B. Architektur, Make-or-Buy, Partner) vor und vertrittst sie gegenüber den Entscheidern. Du bereitest komplexe Zusammenhänge als Entscheidungsvorlagen für die Unternehmensführung auf und bewertest Investitionen und Risiken. Du förderst eine Kultur der technischen Exzellenz in der ALDB. Profil Studium der Informatik oder vergleichbar, oder Du überzeugst uns, dass es auch anders geht Fundierte Erfahrung in Architektur und Entwicklung komplexer Softwaresysteme sowie in einer technischen Führungsrolle Tiefgreifende Kenntnisse in Microservices, Kubernetes, Cloud, CI/CD, DevSecOps, Infrastructure as Code, REST, Datenpipelines sowie gängigen Technologien wie Java, Python, TypeScript und React Gute Kenntnisse im Bereich KI/ML und Erfahrung mit Systemen in hochsicheren, abgeschotteten Umgebungen (air-gapped) Strategisches Denken, wirtschaftliches Verständnis und souveränes Auftreten auf oberster Führungsebene Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse Wir bieten Sicherer Arbeitsplatz : Gesellschaftlich relevante Mission · Überdurchschnittliches Gehalt · Betriebliche Altersvorsorge · Interessante Herausforderungen Work-Life-Balance : Flexible und mobile Arbeits-Modelle, die zu Deinem Leben passen Attraktive Zusatzleistungen : Job-Rad · Job-Ticket · Firmenfitness · u. v. m. Langfristige Perspektive : Zahlreiche Chancen für Deine persönliche Entwicklung · Regelmäßige Trainings · Zukunftsorientiertes Umfeld Angenehme Arbeitsatmosphäre : Tolle Kolleginnen und Kollegen · Offene Kommunikation · Hervorragendes Arbeitsklima und Teamgeist Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE
